Well, this one's going to be one of my favorite games of all time.
What can I say? It's excellent in any aspect if you want to try nitpicking this one, and at the same time it remains a single fantastically working entity.
Let's break it down a little.
Puzzles, the main part of the game are fun and unique. A lot of interesting mechanics to work with, a lot of different ways to do it, too. Just couldn't get bored with it. And it's great that you are up to decide the puzzle you're going to play, the ability to skip over and then come back to it - it helps a lot. Being able to clear your mind and change focus when stuck instead of just bashing onto a wall is a huge plus.
World around you, boy oh boy. Looks great and promising, but that's only the tip of the iceberg - exploring it pays off much more. All the hidden stuff adds up amazingly to the story, making the game pretty damn solid lorewise. Well, easter eggs don't really add up to the lore, but who cares, right? And they're placed around the game in the best traditions of Serious Sam. Croteam sure has a talent for doing that :)
Plot. Strong, compelling, well tied up to everything happening in the world around you and to you directly. Narration, text and voice, dialogues are a masterpiece, I just can't say less of it. I haven't seen anything so well-written, well-directed and well-delivered in a very long time. You get exactly that "immersive feeling" not only by looking at stuff, but mostly with getting caught up in the plot itself. I just can't find proper words to say more positive stuff about it. It's damn GOOD it sure is.
Ok, next. Gotta stay focused.
Music is pretty nice. It's not a Transistor/Bastion level of greatness, it's just not needed much. It feels exactly right to not get annoying while solving stuff or bore you to death. Also it's really good at reflecting the area you're being at. Gotta say I felt a lot of Serious Sam vibes while being at Egypt area :D And I'm glad I did, it's a good nostalgic feeling, yet it's not just Serious Sam, no, just the flavour of it. Great stuff by a great composer who knows exactly right what he's doing with this game.
I've already talked about the world, but I have to say about exploration itself on it's own. It's unbelievably satisfying. I don't feel the urge to explore everything in any game, but when I do, I know - that's the stuff. I've completed the game almost 100% excluding achievements, and never got bored with it. In fact, i want more (Road to Gehenna, here I come).
I don't want to spoil good parts of it, and tbh I don't want to type everything down either, just trust me - if you like your games explored to bits - it's exactly suitable for it. And it's gonna reward you for it in different ways.
Online interaction is a little but fun thing to do. Leaving a sophisticated message, or, on the contrary, a rude and challenging one for future "Children" to look at was a bit i enjoyed. Finding messages of my friends, too.
The philosophical part was extremely hard to maintain properly... yet it's still done brilliantly. How do they even manage? I never had such fun talking to AI (eh heh) as I did in this game, not even mentioning tons of stuff being possible to read and think about. I mean, wow. Developers and writers did such an amazing job making this game what it is.
Technicalities. Game looks great, sounds great, and DUDE DID YOU EVEN SEE THE OPTIONS MENU? Like, it's harder to find  stuff you CAN'T tweak around. Graphics mostly, of course. You can make this bad boy run at any rate at any system is what I feel. And it's gonna look fantastic, maybe a little less fancy on weaker systems, but still fantastic.
Well I can't only say good stuff, right?
I tried my best to nitpick something out of it, and the only stuff I managed was:
A little bit weird physics engine. It's not even needed much and game covers it mechanically very well but it's a disadvantage, a ridiculosly small one, not hurting gameplay in any way, but I just have to find bad stuff not to feel one-sided, sorry.
3d person animations are kind of clunky too. Not like it ACTUALLY MATTERS but hey, still nitpicking.
...And that's it. This is stuff I find bad in it. Nothing else I could remember. I was too busy having loads of fun, probably.
I absolutely adored The Talos Principle, this is the stuff that keeps me playing videogames, this is the stuff worth waiting for, while getting average "AAA titles". Thanks a lot to Croteam and every person working on this game with them, I had tons of fun with this game.

SERIOUS NOTE - Many people have said this game crashes. I have figured out why. This game appears to only work with NVIDIA graphics cards. Seriously, this is one of the best Disney game I've ever played! And one of the best driving games I’ve ever played :D
I love this game!
The game is about Lightning McQueen and Cars.
The graphics are great. Quite appealing if you ask me. The town looks amazing with a lot of cars roaming around town, the best part is smashing into them and watching them fly and say funny quotes! The town looks like how you would expect it to look in the film. The characters look accurate to what they look like in the film which is pretty cool. The voice acting was totally awesome and pretty funny. For example, as McQueen overtakes a racer, he says "objects in the mirror may be closer than they appear", that cracked me up!
The game has free roam (best Disney Cars game IMO), you can drive as Lightning McQueen around 3 different areas including Radiator Springs, what I enjoy doing is ramming into other cars and watching them fly while they say funny things xD
Free roam is pretty much calm and fun to explore!
The story doesn't really cover the film's story, it's kind of based on what happened after the story, so if you haven't watched the film then this game has got some spoilers for you. Spoilers, get it? The wing on the back of a car...?
There are a lot of fun tracks to race on and a variety of characters to choose from, from Lightning McQueen to Wingo, and a bunch of paint jobs to customise them with. The characters have different stats like top speed, acceleration, handling etc. The characters' personalities fit perfectly to the film, and they do make races lively with funny and memorable quotes: Like McQueen’s "KA-CHOW!" phrase xD   He says it in different ways, he shouts it and whispers it and some of them sound funny to me.
The bad thing about character selection is that there are some cars (like Luigi, Sarge and Fillmore etc.) who can race with you, but you can't race as them, so that kinda sucks :(
There are fun mini games added to the side, like Mater's Tractor Tipping game, where you have to wake up tractors without waking up getting caught by Frank, and also Sheriff's Pursuit, where you have to pursuit cars while they are moving fast. They are harder than they sound, but they are enjoyable. The bad part is that they are too long and take too much time, like around 10-15 minutes.
There are also Piston Cup races, each being 12 laps around. There is also a pit stop mini game with Guido as he changes the tires and refuels the car. But you could only play as the race cars in Piston Cup races, like Lightning McQueen, or Chick Hicks and Doc Hudson etc. not Mater or Ramone (lol) But I guess it makes sense, hence it being a Piston Cup race.
Now onto the important part, the gameplay. The cars drive at different speeds and the drifting is handy, although it doesn't look like the drifting in the film, hence the "turn right to go left" quote. The wheel still goes in the direction you want to go, so the car just looks like it's making a hard turn instead of actually drifting. The gameplay is really fun, smooth and easy to master each track with various shortcuts.
However sometimes the car decides to flip and go upside down if you try to crash yourself, it sounds funny and it makes up for it because it is funny lol.  Making contact with other racers will make your car slower which isn't what I'd expect from a racing game, but they do talk after collision which is a good thing.
This game has controller support, so you can play 2 player split-screen multiplayer with your friend, which is a pretty fun addition.
This game is friendly towards kids alright? So don't go wrecking other cars lol, because they don't show damage marks like scratches or dents.
Or if you want to get straight into the action, use cheat codes to unlock all characters and race tracks and there you have it :D
btw there are other cheats like unlimited boost which is fun!
The soundtrack is amazing by the way, like awesome tracks from Bruno Coon and great music like "Here I Am" by the Explosion, and "Free Ride" from Edgar Winter Group, the soundtrack is addictive so listen to it if you dare XD
The only bad thing about this PC version (Steam version) is the lighting at night.
Because the game is old and wasn't really updated, when playing mini games and races in night, it's too dark to see or drive, which is annoying and is preventing me from fully completing the game. So, I hope that gets fixed soon.

Played this for over 2 years, used to be a great game. Once Daybreak took over, things started getting meh but it was still decent and playable.
Then, Daybreak decided to hire one of the Youtubers called Wrel - the brain damage of this r*****ed kid who thinks he can be a developer totally broke the game's balance.
Of course it did so mostly for one side - if you absolutely must play this, I recommend avoiding Vanu.
At the time of writing this, VS had nearly ALL of its unique features removed (most recent removal: RIP Lancer) - the remaining ones are honestly utter cr*p (Aphelion), nerfed to oblivion (PPA, Lancer) or so very situational that they're a joke when mentioned in combat (Lasher).
Hill climbing, which up till some time ago was a highly overrated ability of only Vanu (FailRaider), has been significantly improved on other tanks, strafing is a joke with the speed that tank shells travel at and the special abilities that other tanks have (anchor, shield) are SIGNIFICANTLY more useful, forgiving and newbie and pro friendly compared to what Maggie could ever offer.
In terms of guns, from the experience of two VS chars (BR 120 and BR 109), one NC (BR102) and one TR (BR107): VS guns are....medicore....they do not excel at anything, supposedly jacks of all trades which is an obvious lie. VS guns also have something called no bullet drop. Yet another thing that is highly overrated because it matters ONLY on long ranges (and even at that point bullet drop is easy to compensate for after some time) but guess what - the vast MAJORITY of the game is close quarters combat. Stick your nose out of the building = die if you're not with a zerg. Why? Because of superiority of other factions' tanks over maggie and other factions' specific Harasser guns over what VS has to offer.
NC guns? Heavy hitting with medium fire rate and very easy when it comes to controlling recoil. Also, Jackhammer - a BURST SHOTGUN (lol) that can kill ANY character in one mouse button click. LA1 Anchor is awesome, Gauss Saw is one of my favorite starter weapons. Remember that Deployment Shield sundy next to a base? Well, that's not a problem for a Phoenix - a rocket that you control from a safe spawn room while it's slowly flying - just get a friend to drop a C4/mines while you keep the shield down.
TR? Spray and pray (hello 909rpm Lynx, 896rpm armistice)...My personal favorites here were Armistice and the >burst sniper rifle< Trap M1....yea...you can burst fire with snipers....
What about Maxes? Well, NC maxes are a long known joke in-game - not in terms of 'funny' but because they have been (for sooo long) and are so OP with their instakill shotguns (and yet NC still cries about them being only CQC-only which has ages ago been proven to be a lie by a few youtubers sniping at medium ranges with Mattocks and slug attachments). Oh, they also have a special shield that blocks damage.
And two laser guided rockets launchers...
TR? Good weapons AND anchor (the same as their tank has - basically you cant move but you gain massive bonus to: Reload Speed (50% faster) and shell travel speed (30% faster) for the Prowler and Fire rate, projectile speed and reload time (50% faster) on a MAX). It's worth noting that you can turn Anchor on and off at any time and it takes less than 1 second to get back to the normal mode to run away.
Want to block a room? Get 2 anchored maxes with pounders (aoe grenades~) and shoot at the door.
But hey, what do VS have? An awesome ZOE - at max rank, this beauty gives you 10% more damage output IN EXCHANGE for....receiving 20% more damage :)
And this was STILL considered OP by Wrel (that's a quote, check his videos if you wish to confirm that).
If that's not enough, then take a look at aircraft - ultimate farming machines to which you will die way too often and which you will rarely ever kill because Lock Ons are so easy to avoid/counter by semi-experienced players and because they do cr*p damage (and guess what, almost noone bothers shooting at aircraft).
Also, Empire Specific Fighters are damn quiet when flying slowly so they can, and will, sneak up on you and farm you over...and over...and over. Of course FailBreak fails to see how broken these are so you're stuck with being a farming meatshield for an undefined amount of time.
Moreover - a while ago Daybreak implemented an anticheat drug called BattleEye into the game....
This did practically nothing aside from adding an additional clogg for your CPU  - there are still tons of cheaters (check youtube for "Planetside 2  MuscleLittleMan" - a video from a day ago). Reporting such people does literally NOTHING - you will still see them all the time.
The biggest joke was a while ago when a guy with a name starting with "RepentForYourSinsxxxx" literally obliterated anything and everything with an Archer (a very slow firing anti material rifle), be it galaxies, tanks, people (through walls), etc etc etc.
And last but not least - the requirements...an i7 4770k WC'ed, overclocked from 3.6 to 4.5GHz with an EVGA GeForce GTX 980 Ti HYBRID WC - I had issues with keeping this game at 60 fps. And no, we're not talking Ultra settings here, no 4k or HD resolutions either (i tried this at 1680x1050 at some point but it was unplayable).
So as you can see, things are going only downhill for PS2. It used to be cool, it used to be unique, I loved the long battles, the competitive gameplay and so many different playstyles and ways to approach each base but FailBreak did its "great" job with hiring that ******* Wrel who wrecked this decent title into the trash that it is now.
Conclusion? AVOID! There are a lot better titles out there - there is no point in playing a game where the so called 'devs' create such an imbalance and claim it's all OK.
Ps: large parts of the community are extremely toxic..

Plays similar to smash bros, but combat is not fluid enough (using KB + mouse) and enemies hit you in the middle of a roll/dodge. Co-op is impossible with the friendly fire - ON setting
Early on a lot of enemies are bullet sponges that don't get knocked back from hits, but simply absorb them before counter-attacking in the middle of your attacks. Some enemies dont show any visual hints about their attacks, so there is quite a lot of trial and error involved. You can't quickly hit or turn backwards to hit an enemy before it hits you in close combat as there is some delay in turning to attack. Some ledges have very tight hit detection and you might have to "fall" to the ledges in order to grab them. You have to be turned the right way to grab the ledge (can't turn mid-air), too.
After the first few rooms you don't find much any NPCs to talk to or chests to loot for coins, so you can't even afford a camp token (checkpoint) for a long while - especially if you've spent just a little bit on equipment. After playing quite a lot further, you unlock a checkpoint with a token vendor that sells camp tokens for a lower price. This allows you to progress much more safely, especially when certain soul transformations (for example the mimic) can cheese through the enemies easily.

I expected a Portal 2 knockoff, but this is so much more than that. For starters, it's a lot closer to Super Mario 64 in terms of level design, with varied worlds to explore and challenges to meet. The story itself is intriguing, presenting the protagonist with mind-bending philosophical conundrums and classical science fiction themes like conscious AI and blending it with religious overtones that aren't preachy or overzealous. On top of excellent world-building and an interesting plot, the puzzles are well-made and the mechanics are intuitive and simple. The "Record" mechanic is one of my favorite puzzle elements in recent memory, leading to some super rewarding moments of figuring out how to piece everything together. I also look forward to exploring the Steam Workshop for user-submitted puzzles utilizing the fun mechanics that the base game provides.
I highly recommend picking this game up if you're looking for a solid puzzle game and an intellectual crash course in philosophy with a sci-fi twist.

First, forgive my English because I am still learning.
If you're into deeper philosophy then this game will subjectively speak to you. If a tree falls in a forest and no one is around to hear it, does it make a sound?
Yes, No, or it depends.
If you have a technical mind your answer can be.. well there's gravity and physics which guarantees the tree will fall and the impact will cause sound waves to travel and sound waves creates sounds.. So yes.
If you're more scientific, anatomy and physiology suggest...a sound is something that can be heard. If a vibrating air never enter the cochlea, then it's simply a vibrating air. So the absence of human says no.
Then again.. I can picture an Entomologist raising his or her hand.. hey do I get a say about this? Who cares if there aren't any humans there!
Nonetheless, in philosophy it's never that simple. There are always layers of external impact. Are we literally speaking of trees? expound what falling and sound mean. Does the absence of a man when the tree falls pertain to the argument does consciousness pre-exist and creates the universe or is consciousness a product of neural process? Or is it... if a good man lived a righteous life but noone was around to witness it, did he even existed? A spiritual person may say.. sure! God sees all of course he did. And an Atheist may say well.. I don't believe in God so you can toss that argument out of the window. And it goes on and on.
I gifted Talos + Gehenna to a handful of my most rational friends hoping we can have a dialogue afterward. And to my delight, I was correct to presume that Talos affected everyone differently. And we also solved the puzzles differently. Some with elegance and some with pure technicality.
Each puzzle and terminal encounter will also affect people differently especially in Gehenna. And this is why I have a personal affection for Talos Principle. Give yourself time to absorb this game. Read the text journals, think, and reason. I hope you just don't breeze through it to see how efficient you can be in solving the puzzles. If you allow it, this game will speak to you in terms of how your moral compass guides you in achieving your personal eudaimonia. And that is quite a rarity in a game.
If you enjoyed Talos Principle I hope you buy Gehenna.. because there lies the absolute fulfillment. I am very fond of my Crito moment with Admin. The puzzles and terminal interactions in Gehenna are more profound so you may consider Talos an allegory of the cave into metaphysics and epistemology.
I wish I can take a mind bleach and erase Talos in my memory. Just so I can go through the mind warp again. I gave my original account to my nephew and Talos was the first game I re-bought in my new account. I am very excited about Talos Principle 2 and hopefully a Gehenna 2 of some sort as well.

Ash is on a journey to assemble a friend, and he has to jump, dodge, smash and hang out to find the pieces. The End is Nigh is a great game with smooth, simple controls. The platforming varies from easy to extremely difficult, and the cartridges offer a great challenge for people who have completed the main story. Colleting the tumors is fun (and often takes some brain power to figure out how to get them), and finding and collecting all the mega tumors is a challenge. There are plenty of secrets and NPCs with interesting (but useless) dialogue. The music for the game is also amazing, providing awesome rock and metal remixes of classical songs. The End is Nigh never feels too easy or too (extremely) difficult, and the game's unique mechanics, like Ash's ability to hook onto the edges of platforms, are easy to learn and are mastered by the player easily.
If you are looking for a challenging but fun platformer, and you like Super Meat Boy, please, do yourself a favor and GET THIS GAME!

I have gotten to almost 40 hours on the game and I am about to beat it, so I decided to review it anyways because why not? The End is Nigh is easily one of the best platformer games on the market, and a spiritual successor to Super Meat Boy, which I also love. However, I wouldn't even compare this game to SMB at all except the fact that they're both platformers and are from Ed. With that said, in my opinion, TEiN combines a simpe video game with complicated cinematic style story telling. It of course has deeper meaning to be interpreted by us just as you can expect from Ed. The game features simple base mechanics, however, you can't sprint or wall jump, instead, you are highly mobile already, can hang on ledges, and have insane air control. This couples for a very interesting platforming experience, while it stays true to the base of the genre. The game isn't afraid of itself, by that I mean, it is very open about what kind of game it is, Ash, the main character, is a typical gamer guy who curses a lot. By the way, in case you didn't hear, this game takes place after the apocalypse, where Ash is the one survivor, so he doesn't have much of an audience on his livestreams, and his game cartridge crashes and he sets out to make a friend blah blah blah. Sounds pretty simple and innocent right? Nope. You will die time and time again, only to become get to the next level and repeat the same process, trust me, I have 40 hours and I'm still not done yet, so that means the game will last a while right? Anyway this game has an amazing soundtrack as well, which I can only urge you to hear for yourself to see what I mean. I give The End is Nigh a 9/10 in numbers or whatever. Thanks :)

REVIEW FROM 2014:
Unfortunately, I cannot recommend this game. Develepors, if you are reading this, either the cost needs to be drastically reduced, or you need to stop focusing on tiny lil fix-ups like cloud shadows, and focus more on giving more meaning to the game. True, it looks beautiful, and you can build, but that's about it. There's no objective. There's no leveling. There's no models, no creatures, no upgrading, no survival... nothing but a world with really nice looking blocks. I know it's a really early stage in your game's development, but do NOT price the game at $35 as soon as it's on the shelves if there's nothing to do but place blocks and swing around. That's why you don't have more people playing this game: It's a game for rich people with nothing to do other than sit around and build things in games to feel good about themselves, to be blunt. How many commonplace people can afford a game like this, and how many of Them will be disappointed when they don't get their money's worth out of it? I'd say that at the very most, this game needs to be $15. I'm sorry, again, but this is utterly rediculous.
P.S. If the servers are costing you so much, get rid of a few of them. It's not like there's ever gonna be any more than what, 15, 20 people playing at one time.
*EDIT FOR 2015:
It's been over a year since I wrote this review, and only find it fair to look at the progress that the newly named Boundless has taken up, and give a new review. Since I had written this, the Boundless team has achieved NPCs, basic playermodels, better inventory setups, skins and models for weapons and tools, and more. My previous statement of them just making blocks prettier has been built on as well, making much better lighting, realistic environmental sounds, high quality textures, and different shaped blocks for more advanced building. Along with a slight growth of population, world amounts are apparently being toned down, and the focus is starting to shift more to the players than to the environment. I can see now that my $35 were, indeed, well spent, and I now encourage people to try and purchase this game. It is now successfully timeworthy, and has not even reached 1.0. Buy this game.

Do you remember the absolute insanity of the VGA era of PC games? Where playing as a goat sentenced to witchcraft was something you wouldn't bat an eyelash at? Escape Goat is such a game. The play consists of a set of one screen puzzle areas, where we must first learn what each switch, button or other action does, and then correctly hit them (or use enemies and allies to hit them) in the right order and with the right timing to get to the exit. The difficulty can actually ramp up fairly quickly, fortuately we get to autosave at the end of every level, and can return to the hub to choose a different puzzle theme at any time. Finally at the end, we go through a series of super hard levels that combine all of the previous areas types into one. Awesome controls, great puzzles, and a great sense of humour. High reccomended especially if you can get it on sale (since it does seem to be on short side).

My boyfriend and I bought this game two nights ago, and had a blast playing for the rest of both nights. A lot of people bring up Minecraft similarities, and while the building system is similar, there's more to it with this game for sure. Boyfriend and I played a lot of MC, and we already like this game more.
+ The graphics are phenomenal. We really feel our buildings come to life in this game. The textures and shapes of the blocks, paired with the gorgeous atmosphere (sounds, lighting, sky, everything) really make everything pop.
+ Right now, you start with a few different block types in your inventory. You can set it to infinite blocks, so you don't have to spend time gathering. However, I've found a new type of block through exploration, which was really nice.
+ When I needed a break from building, grappling my way around the world was equally as fun. The landscapes are breathtaking, and it was also really fun searching for signs of life. It's so nice stumbling upon a cabin, or a room built into the side of a mountain, or a tower in a valley. Also, exploring other servers has been a blast, too. Some of the structures are mindblowing. :D
+ Right now, all there is to do is build and explore, and I think it's worth the price as is. With all the stuff that's in the works, this game could be huge. I can't even say how excited we are. The team is also very interactive with the community, and patches come out oftem.
+ The only one thing missing as the game is, is playing as a character. All players are orange blocks right now. You forget that pretty much instantly though, as soon as you start to build or explore.
I really could go on and on, but this gets the major points across. I can't wait to see the game and community grow. :)

I'm confused as to how this game received mixed reviews. This is simply one of the best videogames I've ever played. Sure it's story is generic but it is executed pretty darn well. What really stands out in this game is it's combat mechanics and I love games with an in-depth combat system. In all my experiences with combat mechanics in games, nothing tops this masterpiece of a game. It it truly satisfying to pull off different moves and have variation in what you do all of which affect your enemies in the slightest but most unique ways. Harness the potential power of your environment with throwable objects and traps to use against your enemies which is the most enjoyable part of this game. All of this is made possible with the SOURCE ENGINE! So not only do these abilities and such sound good but are executed equally as good!
What I also admire is it's Immense replayablility for a game that seems so linear. The game presents you these three playstyles that you can go full out on one or try and experiment between them and create cool hybrids. There are no boundaries, no "choose your class" type ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t, it just gives you the game and goes "go nuts". And the repayability that this creates is awesome! Speaking of replayability, you can also find secret areas along your travels and the game also sports multiple endings!
All of this is played in FPS which adds onto the immersion. Not many fantasy games play out in FPS which makes this game pretty unique in that sense.
The game is more feature rich than you would think. But my only gripe about this game is the voice acting. TERRIBLE TERRIBLE VOICE ACTING...at least from the main protagonist. If you can get past it like I did, you'll have a bomb of a time.

At first I found this game rather enjoyable. It introduces alot of very interesting and unique concepts along the way, and item progression, as well as skill progression, actually matter quite a bit in this game. The main pitfalls (heh...) of this title are the mechanics, the physics engine. Enemies are tough to kill in combat, even if you tool yourself out with the best equipment possible, the game is brutally difficult. As such, many just resort to ranged combat, and trick the AI into getting stuck, so they can peg them with dozens of arrows.
Main issues I encountered were such:
Getting lost again and again, which I realised was partly due to several progression bugs which prevent key doors from opening. The level layout does tend to make everything sort of blend in, so figuring out just which corridor contains the identical looking wooden door you need to go through does happen.
The rope bow/arrow, well before the latest Croft game and other titles empoyed it, is quite fun, until you start floating through walls while climbing ropes, because the physics engine was not programmed to deal with this vital game mechanic. The number of times I died whilst trying to do the fiddliest of tricky platforming (which as always, in a first person game, is just an awful idea from the start), due to the rope intersecting with a chunk of rock, which caused me to noclip out of the level... It gets frustrating very quickly.
Finally, the magic in this game feels utterly flat. Fireballs hit enemies as though you just threw a small water balloon at them. Lightning appears to have the same effect as assaulting your enemy with a particularly wet piece of paper. There was absolutely no appeal to using magic in this game except as a means to use the mana I have anyway.
If you really want to try it, nothing I say is going to stop you, but otherwise i'd say leave this game where it belongs, in the past.

This game has so many equally good and bad things going for it.
+ Half life 2 engine still looks gorgeous. The art here is pretty generic D&D but the models are nice and the entire atmosphere is very well done. Music is moody as well.
+ This game is challenging. If you turn the difficulty all the way up, it's just like playing Dark Souls but in first person! Even a single zombie can kill you. If I didn't use all the combination of weapons I had (swords, daggers, bows) and also magic, I couldn't get past even the 3rd chapter. This is NOT a game to go hack/slash in. You will die as quick as you start fighting.
+ The RPG elements are fun and although aren't as deep as any traditional RPG, they are fun to mess around with. I played as a pyromaniac swordsman and it was definitely fun! BUT read the final negative below point as well.
+ Lots of ways to set off physical traps and kill you enemies with. For example, cut a rope holding up a bunch of logs and watch it fall down on your enemies. Never gets tiring.
+ The game is barely more than 10 hours long. First playthrough anyway but because of last point, there's moderate to high replayability.
+You can kick enemies into spikes and pits.
- There are lots of bugs. I encountered a lot anyway. Graphical, like black boxes appearing over my spells when fired. Controls, like assigning a spell to a number on my keyboard and not having the spell come up even though I pressed the corresponding number several times. This gets very annoying especially when you're in a tight situation and want to change your weapon or change to a spell. It just doesn't work sometimes. Sound bugs, as in voice overs repeating or missing or playing in the wrong places which could mislead the player. As I said, lots of bugs.
- Platforming is CRAP. It was bad in Half Life games and it's still bad here. And the fact that there's almost a high amount of it in the game makes it the more painful. You even have a bow which extends a rope down for you to climb and this gives possibilities to explore more of the world or just get past levels but the jumping and walking controls are so loose that it just doesn't work in an enjoyable way.
- Most of the time your objective becomes VERY obscure and I personally got lost a lot in most of the maps simply because the exit to some rooms were so out of sight and unlikely to be where they actually are that I needed to look at walkthroughs in some places just to know how to get out of a certain dungeon.
- The story is almost non-existent. Don't come into this expecting any cohesive, attractive story or ending. Even though there are 4 endings, they are alll equally predictable and not worth playing the game for.

- multiplayer is long dead. Unless you have other friends who have the game on steam. But it's nothing special. Passable.
- Most of the time, the game throws loads and loads of enemies at you which seems more like what a shooter would do than a game like this. Soon it becomes such a chore to manage a crowd of 5 ferral ghouls who are attacking you from all sides.
- The RPG elements are fun but really unbalanced. You find so many weapons from the 3rd chapter on that you can't equip way into the game unless you were super pin-pointed towards a certain role (fighter, archer,white mage, black mage, thief). If you want to spread out a little like, say, be a white mage/thief, you're not going to accumulate enough upgrade points to truly be that until the very end levels of the game. That seems pointless to me as well as the fact that some classes like archers and thiefs will never be strong enough to take on most of the enemies in a game which is so close-combat oriented. The fact that you don't get any experience from defeating enemies but only from story checkpoints is a very bad choice to me.
As you see, I can say the game has much potential and I am going to give it a thumbs up even though it annoyed and frustrated me as much as I enjoyed some of its better moments. If you're willing to risk, give it a go. I'm sure you'll find your own reason to like it. It tries to be deeper than what it is and sometimes that's both a blessing and a curse.

Well, I wasn't sure if I should write a review, but I saw that most of the others are just crap so I decided to ake 15 minutes and write my thoughts.
This is a sort of 2D fighting game, simple and not pretencious, where you have to clear some levels until you eventually get to the big boss. Overall this is a good game, but there are some things that ought to be improved.
Pros:
Abyss Odyssey has a stunning visual, the artwork is marvellous, especially the artstyle of the enemies. You find yourself fighting against monsters never seen before. Also the music is beautiful, even if a bit limited. The three characters are different and balanced and the difficulty of the game is not too high. When you die you get "revived" as a second character and this is a quite god idea, so that you don't have to restart from the beginning.
Cons:
I'm afraid these are a bit more. There are some problems in this game that are quite annoying, The firs thing is that this game explains absolutely nothing. Ok, you know how to attack and move, but you don't know how to capture souls, how to use mana, how to respawn, and how to use the power ups. These and many other mechanics are not explained, and you need to play many times before knowing rules and tips. This might give the game more longevity but sometimes it becomes frustrating.
Second is the combat. You'll find annoying trying to turn left/right, because either you attack or turn, many times I found myself swinging in the wrong direction. The counterattack is more or less useless, a bit better for the dodge, because you just have to do the same 2 combos to keep your enemies down.
Other things badly managed are the inventory, when to buy weapons, and how merchants ar eplaced through the levels. Unfortunately when you die you lose your equipement (unless of course you find an altar with your soldier, but even there I lost all my potions bracelets, etc..) and you have to be lucky to find a merchant or a good weapon. Many times I was beaten because there wasn't anywhere to buy potions or a good weapon. I thought "I just need to level up and it'll change". Well that's not true because after 12 hours I still think levelling doesn't serve any purpose, the damage you inflict seems to be based on your weapon, not on your level.
As for the power up section, I still don't know if it works, if I put all the power ups to the attack, mana or shield, I see the same results. One last thing I want to mention is about some traps, that in a very few cases are unavoidable and placed in a silly way. One time I died with my souls and the monk becouse I couldn't jump over a black hole (I  lost my equipement).
Talking about the multiplayer, I played with a friend and the game is fun, we found it a lot easier than the single player and we enjoy beating those monsters, the only problem we have is that the game doesn't run well. Probably it's jjust us but I see my teammate halfway through the floor, and on my laptop lags. I followed instructions on some forums but still couldn't fix it. I resigned myself to lower the quality to improve the performace, and by the way I bought this laptop 2 weeks ago and it is a spaceship, this game shoul run smoothly.
Well to sum up, this game is for sure enjoyable and it can keep you busy for more then 10 hours, but I wouldn't pay 15 bucks for it,  I think I got it in a bundle. There are some good ideas but some things ought to be improved, if not in this game, for the next one. Have fun playing

The tutorial is much better than the hand holding that most city/base builder games give you when you start a new campaign. For those other games, you only have the choice of turning your tutorials on and off, while they nudge you in the direction they want you to go. In RimWorld, the tutorial only pops up when you come across an event that you haven't encountered before. And then it never shows up again, unless you want it to.
The gameplay flows very well. You begin with simple mechanics, and then as the game goes on, it becomes a more and more complex balancing issue. Rather than solving problems as they arise, RimWorld essentially forces you to prevent problems before they happen. This requires a lot of pre-planning, making sure to keep you on your toes.
You will face challenges such as weather conditions, sickness, and of course, the occasional enemy. Trade is an available option to you, and there are times when the game's "storyteller" will bring in a trade vessel at the desperate moment your colony is about to fall apart. The storyteller is a built-in mechanic which selects a series of events for you, and interlaces them into the gameplay seamlessly.
There are multiple difficulty options, and a further set of nuances which determine a situational difficulty level when you start the game. As you select your difficulty, you will also select an area on the world map for your colonists to land. The area can be a frigid tundra with little to no fertile soil, or even an arid desert which constantly gives your colonists heat stroke. Even further than this, your colony could be exposed to the open air, or safely tucked away inside a mountain.
Sound and graphics are decent for what they are. Everything is simple enough to the point where you can tell what is what, and then make a quick decision based on that.
The game does support mods, and many of the mods add levels upon levels of extended entertainment to the game. You can find the mods on RimWorld's forums.
I would recommend this game for people who enjoy city/base builders. There is a lot to offer.
I wouldn't recommend this game for people who don't like micromanagement or extended planning.

I was actually surprised at how good this game is!  The air/land/water vehicle transformation gimmick works out nicely, as your vehicle controls rather differently in each form, and the game includes kart-racer staples such as boosts for extended drifting or doing flips and rolls off of ramps (or barrel-rolling out of the way of obstacles when in plane mode)
There are no lightning bolts or blue shells to result in cheap losses in this racer, and most attack items work almost instantly; your demise is entirely determined by how well the other guy aims regardless of any amount of defensive driving. On one hand, most attacks won't slow you down all THAT much, but on the other hand, regaining lost position is not as easy as most racers. If you fall to last place, count yourself lucky if you can get back up to fourth or third.
Apart from the standard GP and single races, the game also features a robust "world tour" mode filled with challenges ranging from drift challenges, traffic dodging, time trials, battle races, and even boss battles against a tank.
I'd definitely call this game worth trying, even if you aren't the biggest fan of Sonic and friends.

Went ahead and downloaded with Steam JUST so I can right this review. The steam playtime on here for me is bar none. But that's because I've played Strife through its standalone launcher for many hours. My account level right now is 10 about to be level 11. (if that can be of any representation)
I have had a lot of fun playing this game so far. It's different. It feels very refined as a MOBA. It's smooth. Cartoony even. With many ways to keep you in the action.
1: The trailer isn't kidding. The respawn times don't start getting outrageous until almost 35 minutes in a match. and many matches I've played haven't lasted that long.
2: Out of Combat Regen. My ♥♥♥♥ing best friend in a nutshell. So long as you haven't dealt or taken damage for I think 5 seconds. You start to regen your health and mana back. This regen is near doubled when standing next to an ally tower. This system. If used well. Can keep you in lane until late game when you start to really take a beating. In that case. Use the return to base button.
3: In-lane item buying. One aspect I liked about Dota. But is also applied into this game. But the difference is. Everyone has their own personal courier without having to buy one in the shop. Just buy. Press a button. And a little box carrying squirrel brings your items.
Alright. Down to brass tacks.
Pros:
-Very smooth gameplay.
-many reasons to keep fighting in a match.
-unique crafting system.
-Every playable hero is free from the start.
-paid currency is only for account boosting and cosmetics.
-very good balancing
-complex shop, but not complicated at all.
-pets! each time you start a match. you have a choice of pets that can aid you in different ways. Such as healing you. Or restoring some of your mana. or boosting your resistance. pets can easily change a playstyle and are just adorable too.
Cons:
-Right now. The game isn't very known so there aren't a lot of players. Making longer queue times.
-Needs more america. XD. I'm sorry. It's just that I keep getting into games with Russians. Making it near impossible to communicate with my team. Pings can only do so much.
-Unfortunately. there is a built in voice chat with this game. Why it's a con. That should be obvious.
-When someone disconnects from a match. They have about 6 minutes to reconnect or be perma booted from the match. Which makes it very easy to hinder your team. 3v5s suck. Upside though, the gold that the booted player had earned gets distributed amongst the players still in the game.
That's about it. If you're tired of League or Dota. Whether it is the amount of salt being poured from either or you are just bored with it. Play Strife.

This is much better than I thought it would be.  It's a fun platformer with combat mechanics borrowed from Smash Bros.  The graphics are gorgeous; there are a few different environments that all look colorful and drastically different from one another.  Music and sound effects are pretty good, but not remarkable in the same way the visuals are.
The controls are janky.  There's problems with autocorrecting, with facing the right direction, with climbing over obstacles and with spacing in combat, all because the controls aren't dialed in very well.  The game remains playable but the crappy controls will lead to some frustrating deaths.  The game isn't very long.  It's made so that you can start it, beat it in maybe an hour or so, then come back a day or two later and beat it again.  Your character gets stronger and maintains that strength throughout multiple deaths and playthroughs.
I play on an HTPC and the game is easy to read on a 50" TV from 8' away.  All the fonts are large, clear and bold.  Combined with full voiceovers, I consider the production value to be very high for a title at this price point.
I wholly reccomend this game to anybody who enjoys platformers or smash bros.  If these types of games aren't strong draws, this is still a good time waster if you can get it on sale.  There is a co-op mode and the game has some replay value.

No witty intro this time. Is it a good game or bad game, that's the real question here.
Story/Design: The story is as much as you'd expect from a chapter based RPG Like game. You play as Sareth, the usual main protagonist of any RPG, he's not much during cutscenes but likeable enough. Unfortunately, the main plot is not the highlight of Dark Messiah, the plot is predictable, the plot twists are recognized from a mile away, and just not all that interesting. Is that a bad thing? Not really, you don't need the best story to make a great game, but it could have used a bit less clichés and more original ideas. The ending(s) do it a bit of justice, but not by much. Overall the story is just a bit too bland for me to enjoy besides the last few stages, and only slightly memorable if you look at the endings.
Design wise, it's what'd you expect for a late 2006 game. Luckily it's made with the Source Engine so at least it has some decent looking details from then, but not everything is top quality obviously. Nothing hinders it, and it can hold up still for a few things, besides a few NPC designs of the humans. Unfortunately there's no real modding community or big graphic overhauls on this game as of this review, so you're stuck with the graphics. But again, it's not a flaw against the game.
Gameplay/Mechanics: I'll start by saying Dark Messiah of Might & Magic has THE BEST first person RPG combat I have ever seen. Unlike Oblivion/Skyrim as you constantly spam your attack button hoping to kill them at first before they kill you, the combat is much more strategic and can vary depending on the situation. It's an RPG like experience, so you can be a few different kinds of "classes" I'll put them in. Mage, Archer, Rogue, and Warrior. Standard of course, but each have their strengths in this combat system, it's unfortunate I cannot put into words how well and fluid the combat is with each class type, as it's one of those systems where you need to try for yourself and see it's not just another clunky button mashing system like in the Scrolls games. Traps and environmental hazards are plentiful, and ragdoll physics are just fun to mess with during fights, as kicking Orcs into a wall of spikes or off a cliff has never been so satisfying. (Or kicking a bird on a beach, I mean why not?)
The A.I. is surprisingly smart and can be ruthless if you're reaching your breaking point, some say it's cheap and the A.I. is way too tough, but I'd prefer a challenge over a way too easy game experience where I don't die at all. They do not have health bars either, which I believe is a nice touch, as if they're injured enough they'll plea for their lives of limp away in agony and try to escape or get help.
There's not a specific class either, you'll be needing to use all of your tricks to take down enemies, with stealth as best you can being very effective and immensely rewarding, to long ranged assault on unsuspecting goblins, or magic against non-humanoid creatures. It's never just one class throughout the game, which can help make each level feel fresh.
Overall, what is this game? Does it have a compelling and memorable story? No. Memorable characters? Not really, unless you're a pervert and wanting to remember all the slightly nude women. (Why have that?) Best level design? Not really, unless it's well placed birds for you to kick, then that's a plus.
What it does have going for it is the combat, the gameplay, the A.I, the kind of fights you'll remember a few years down the road when playing some other RPG with awful combat ... not naming any names. Some games don't need to have a good narrative or plot going for it, as the gameplay can make the game. It's not perfect, but it's not bad either. Only if they made this a more open world like Oblivion and keep the combat like this, it'd be my favorite RPG. (One day...)
Overall rating: 7.5/10
+Best combat out of any RPG I've played
+Smart A.I.
+Interesting hidden items!
+Can punt kick a bird off a beach.
-Bland story/characters
-Non memorable protagonist or plot
-Mixed level design
10/10 If you dont have it, get it!

Abyss Odyssey offers what feels like a cross between a Souls-like and Street Fighter-like approach to complex combat mechanics amidst a gorgeous, sometimes whimsical, eerie 2D background.  Yes, the controls can feel counter-intuitive and frustrating as others have mentioned, but once you get into the groove of dashing, parrying, and cancelling out of and into actions and abilities, fighting begins to feel extremely rewarding.  You will most definitely want to use a controller.
Enemy AI is sophisticated enough to make battle feel like a UFC squaredance.  Foes read you, and they are quite good at it.  They anticipate moves and react accordingly.  Hitboxes are fair and accurate. Enemies often provide enough time and space between moments of engagement to allow you some room for planning attacks.  Add to this the fact that each character has unique moves and skill sets, and the main playable characters have ability unlocks and customizable loadouts, and you have a ton of great replayability.  There are plenty of characters to master as you collect the souls of monsters you encounter, including some boss souls--gotta catch 'em all!
Itemization leaves a little something to be desired.  The few weapons and items available have standard fantasy attributes (fire, ice, poison, curse, charm), and while they look aesthetically pleasing, help destroy foes more easily, and add another nice layer of complexity and fun to combat (especially charming and freezing), more could have been done by the developers to diversify and add to the repertoire.
If you enjoy rewarding difficulty with precision control mastery, stunning art and music, smooth pacing from stage to stage, and a fairly unique spin on 2D action platforming, get this at full price or on sale.  Either way, it's worth it.

I was actually surprised at how good this game is!  The air/land/water vehicle transformation gimmick works out nicely, as your vehicle controls rather differently in each form, and the game includes kart-racer staples such as boosts for extended drifting or doing flips and rolls off of ramps (or barrel-rolling out of the way of obstacles when in plane mode)
There are no lightning bolts or blue shells to result in cheap losses in this racer, and most attack items work almost instantly; your demise is entirely determined by how well the other guy aims regardless of any amount of defensive driving. On one hand, most attacks won't slow you down all THAT much, but on the other hand, regaining lost position is not as easy as most racers. If you fall to last place, count yourself lucky if you can get back up to fourth or third.
Apart from the standard GP and single races, the game also features a robust "world tour" mode filled with challenges ranging from drift challenges, traffic dodging, time trials, battle races, and even boss battles against a tank.
I'd definitely call this game worth trying, even if you aren't the biggest fan of Sonic and friends.

Half-Life: Opposing Force, the first expansion of Half-Life. The single concept is already interesting on its own because we experience the great Black Mesa incident from who is supposed to be the enemy of Gordon Freeman. In addition to that the game has several new elements that make this expansion a fresh experience. Let's see what Opposing Force has to offer.
The protagonist, Adrian Shephard, is someone who was sent to fulfill a mission that any other soldier could have done. However, he ended up doing something much bigger, something that had an impact on the future of the whole world. I don't know if it would have been for better or worse but the sequel, Half-Life 2, would have been completely different if Shephard had failed. Personally I would have liked to know more about him in the sequels but unfortunately Valve never developed the character any further. And since it's very unlikely that Valve'll release a new Half-Life game in the future things will probably stay that way.
The gameplay is practically the same as the first Half-Life. The movement, the weapons, the enemies, everything is great, fluid and responsive. In addition to this there are new cool weapons, both of military and alien origin. New enemies, the Race X, which is are completely unrelated to the Xen creatures, and that add a new feeling and pacing to the game. Opposing Force is not a copy of the first game, it's an original adventure located at the same time as it is.
The same as the first game, although with a slightly greater amount of details. The graphics for its time were pretty good. The FPS' were still developing aesthetically and Half-Life was a step forward without a doubt. It's obvious that by today's standards it isn't impressive. However, for me the visuals of this game are a classic, a stamp that was won over the years product of the nostalgia of players like me.
It's the same as the original game so it inherits all the good elements of it, although new material is needed. It seems to me they just reused SFX and music of the original game. It's good to hear the anazing music of the original game again, but I would also have liked to hear something new.
In conclusion, Half-Life: Opposing Force is an incredible expansion. It inherits all the good elements of the original game and expands upon it. I recommend you to play this if you loved the original game, like me!

Polished, atmospheric  first (optionally third) person 3D puzzler.
Great visuals.
Solid sounds.
Entertaining and rewarding gameplay.

Reasonably successful at making philosophical content a core element.
Very tweakable, far beyond the usual audio/visual/interface desireables such as high FOV and rebindable keys.

It stands a hair below Portal overall, for me, but thats down to my slight bias for humour and conflict over prolongued seriousness. TTP is quite dry by comparison, though there are a few chuckles to be had reading the various texts, and the philosophical content is meaty enough to be enjoyable if a bit patchy and hand-wavey.
The style and difficulty of the puzzles is varied and fun. The learing curve seems reasonable but you Cattell 152 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s are going to whizz though it ;)
Some puzzles require doing things that previous experience will have taught one to discount, such as jumping and climbing. The 'jumpy bits' are the worst aspect of the game mechanically as the rules of when/how are never clear thanks to the heavy handedness with which one's gymnastics will be curbed by an unseen hand in one context, then artifically boosted in another (especially when seeking optional/hideen objectives).
There are two puzzles in particular which chapped my♥♥♥♥♥ There was no way to logically assess/analyse the situations to derive a plan then execute it; one was apparently just expected to mash options in anger until something unexpected happened, such as jumping fifteen feet foward when two inches has been a problem for the 14 hours prior.
The balance of mystery and revelation throughout the narrative is well maintained and the ending(s) are cathartic and rewarding. It reminded me a lot of STALKER SoC, which has - by miles - given me the best late-game and game-end experience I've ever had.
The armchair tour through chunks of philosophy is pretty solid I suppose (given the vehicle and market). Spoiler free review
The premise is really interesting and was a neat take on the topics it covers. Also, the way they slowly give you hints as to what's going on was a lot of fun.
The puzzles are great and a lot of fun to solve. You're using a lot of the same tools but you end up using them in just about every conceivable way, so I really appreciated that. The difficulty was perfect for me, as well. Most puzzles had me thinking for a bit and trying out a bunch of ideas before finding the solution but I never felt frusturated with their difficulty.
Well, except for the challenge stars. I know those are supposed to be extra difficult, but so many of them I could never even find! I wouldn't mind if they made those a bit more visible to save some frustration.
The philosophical stuff was often interesting and I loved the debates you could take part in, but I do have a couple of complaints about this aspect.
1. It can sometimes get a little pretentious and artsy for my tastes. Some excerpts felt like Croteam was trying to be mysterious and abstruse without having much substance (The Athena and Scribe of Osiris in particular). Fortunately, there were many other entries that contained truly thought provoking ideas that I loved.
2. In the main game, using the terminals felt a little incongruous with the rest of the game. I think this is why reading the entries was interesting but often felt like a chore I was obligated to do.
Though, I'm happy to say the terminals were greatly improved in Road to Gehanna and it makes me happy to see Croteam trying something unique in the dlc. Having the terminal entries be something you earn and making them more relevant to your character and the world he/she inhabits definitely addressed my previous two complaints.
Overall, it's a great game. I expected to like it and even still it surpassed my expectations. I really appreciate the work of Devolver and Croteam.

Have you ever wondered what it would be like in Adam and Eve's shoes (if they had worn any)? No? Well, too bad, they made a game for it anyway. I am just going to be honest here and say that The Talos Principle is amazing. It makes you think quite a lot, though a lot of the ideas in the game are largely based on "offending nobody's religion". As long as you don't mind that, chances are very good that you will love this game if you can make it to the end (it is long AND hard). I bought this game during the Steam end of year sale for $10, and for that price I can say that it was beyond worth it. Knowing what the game is now I would have even payed the full $40 for it, which I cannot say for many games. It took me approximately twenty five hours to reach the "end", which, at least from what I have heard, can vary greatly depending on your decisions.
The Talos Principle is a marvelous addition to the first person puzzle genre, and I can say for certain that this game goes on my list of best games of that type of all time. Right up there along with Portal, Portal 2, Antichamber, and Myst. I feel like I should mention that this game can also be somewhat depressing at times, and is not always the happiest thing in the world. Despite that, though, it was still extremely fun to play and see what would happen next.
My final summary: This game is amazing. Play it.

It's Luxor.  It's in HD. If you like Luxor, you'll like it.  If you like Zuma, you'll like it.  If you like Arkanoid or Space Invaders or Galaxian or Centipede you might like it, too.
It's difficult to say much about a game already so well known.  It's Zuma with vertical shooting instead of rotational.  It looks good, and it plays smoothly, and it's essentially a prettied-up version of the original.
If Luxor 2 has a flaw, it's a lack of courage or ambition. It presents a huge pile of maps, but doesn't add much of significance to justify that '2' in the title, and what little it does add (more powerups) are present from the outset.  That makes progress feel a little meaningless -- you go from one map to the next, some harder than others, but the gameplay is consistent.  In that regard Luxor 3 was an improvement; allowing you to earn coins with which to strategically purchase upgrades for your favourite powerups made success in a level feel more rewarding in the long term.  Otherwise, the core gameplay is great, but quite interchangeable with any other Luxor title.

Luxor 2 HD
A classic in it's own right. Luxor fills the gap between puzzle and action.  There is replay ability if you go for the in game achievements. Luxor 2 has a great soundtrack. Even with a low end PC and windows 10, I had no problem running Luxor 2 HD at a steady 60 FPS.
It seems like most people on Steam missed it, but the Luxor series is a puzzle classic. Creating its own genre. A mix of Action-Puzzle, Shooter, Match three. If you spend a little time with Luxor you will find it is fairly fast paced and can become very challenging in late game.
The end game stages and achievements is where Luxor finds its replay value and really makes you think on your toes. It can actually be very difficult so I don't know why Luxor 2 Hd is tagged casual. There is three game modes. The classic adventure, with 25 maps that increase in difficulty as you move up in 14 stages. Adventure mode has a grand total of 88 levels to complete. There is survival mode and a practice mode, where you can go back and replay any unlocked level. The average time to complete Luxor 2 is 60-100 hours.
With that much game play needed for completion it is a good thing Luxor 2 has a great soundtrack to go along with it. The tune has stuck with me over the years and one of the reasons I decide to purchase the PC version. I already own the Xbox 360 version. Regardless of the other warnings that Luxor had not aged well essentially.
I had no troubles playing Luxor 2 on my low end PC with Windows 10. The frame rate was consistently above 60 fps. The only difference in performance from the Xbox 360 version and the PC, was the mouse. At times the track seems to skip across the screen rather than roll smoothly. I have a feeling this snap function with the mouse may be intentional and it was far from game breaking.
Over all, Luxor 2 HD speaks for its self, It's a timeless classic with unique game play mechanics that work. With plenty of challenge and replay ability, coupled with a great soundtrack. Thankfully Luxor 2 has aged well and preforms as expected. I would definitely  recommend trying out the Luxor series and Luxor 2 HD is a great place to start.

What sets this apart from LoL is the features that benefit solo-queue:
1. When someone AFKs or DCs and you don't feel like doing a 4v5, no problem.  After a DC timer, you have the option to leave without penalty.
2. Shop system where you can buy on the field, no need to RTB.  Less downtime, more farming and fighting.
3. OMG, the ping system is awesome.  Not just a sound is sent to the team, but verbal announcement by your character like "Enemy missing mid".  "On my way mid"  There are about a dozen pings you can send with two ping radial menus.
4. Speaking of verbal announcements, not only are multikills announced, but your character makes his own announcement.
5.  Customization through items with crafting.  Tweak your gameplay with crafting and pets to give you your personal edge.  In traditional MOBAs, there are only a couple real usable builds per character role.  Everyone has the same masteries and runes and items for a specific character and role.
6.  Along with the shop system.  Item builds are easily accessible and items pop up from your build as soon as you can afford them.  And your hero abilities can be planned and set to auto-level.
7.  More streamlining of the interface making the gameplay smoother.  Even a little easier to click on a specific mob in a group of mobs.
8.  Once your game is loaded you are placed in the game able to shop while you wait for everyone else.
Feels fresh and streamlined, but maintains the solid gameplay you expect from a moba.  It feels easy to play because the interface is superior.  THings like when you get hit, your missing health is temporarily shown in a different color so you can better guage how the fight is going and time the engages and disengages.

This is one of the few "retro-style" games out there that absolutely NAILS the early 16-bit aesthetic. None of the elements here, from the graphics to the sound to the gameplay itself, would feel out of place on an SNES or Genesis.  I appreciate that (apparent) fidelity to the limitations of those older systems, especially when it's become popular to market any game with affectedly pixelated graphics as "8-bit". If you're nitpicky about stuff like that, you'll probably appreciate Escape Goat.
As for the actual gaming element: it's fun, reasonably challenging, but it feels like it will be over too soon (I'm probably about 3/4 of the way through); I had to quit, pace myself, so I wouldn't finish it in one sitting. I want to savor the goat. The good news is, it comes with a level editor, so the goat action never has to end!
Also: it's about time we had a game where you get to play as a goat. I love how the sprite changes when you're standing near a ledge; it totally captures the goat's goatishness.

A surprisingly--and strikingly--enjoyable game. Oxenfree is a walking simulator with choices, ala Firewatch, and manages to have an especially creepy vibe to it despite the fairly cute art style. In fact, this game nears the top of my list for atmospheric/creepy because there's just so much unexplained, and the rules are unclear. At time the plot dives to remorselessly dark, but it's far more of a mystery crossed with a psychological thriller than horror.
The two main characters are engaging, and a third comes close. There are two more that I found a little flat, but the dialogue was refreshing: not the stilted amatuerish writing I found in other similar genre games (e.g. Life is Strange). There are no puzzle mechanics in this game, but the game IS about puzzling out what happened/is happening, and what kind of relationship you're forging with the characters. Choices do matter here; perhaps not to the overarching storyline, but certainly to the individual relationships, which is arguably the most interesting aspect of the game anyway.
There are some flaws; like any walking simulator it's also a patience simulator, and if you have the directional sense of a paperclip you're going to find yourself angrily walking in circles like I did. Let me save you some time: ctrl is where your map is located. Yeah, there's a map. Yeah, I found it 2/3 of the way through the game. Additionally, there are quite a lot of unanswered questions at the end of the game (disclaimer: I ended my first playthrough with 4/13 achievements, so perhaps I didn't put all the puzzle pieces together like I should, but I prefer an organic playthrough.) I'd appreciate just a few more loops being closed (ha) during the playthrough. We can infer and overanalyze clues all day long, but without just a few more pieces by the developer some of the story lines end without answers. That's just a bit unsatisfying, especially after such a rich and unexpected game experience.

An interesting development of dialogue in games that worked very well, while still providing feedback to players about how their choices affect the story.  The plot itself, and characters, are nothing extremely special, I'd say, although they do get the job done; the antagonists, while clearly the villains, have a generally relatable motivation of self-preservation (as do the protagonists).
The greatest flaw with the game, I'd say, is that it is not immediately clear if the dialog choices will interrupt the conversation, or will apply at the end of the conversation.  This seems like a small complaint, but is extremely important for this game, which is entirely centred around the conversation and dialogue.
Ultimately, I'd recommend the game just as an experience as to how the dialog choices are handled, as many interesting ideas are developed in the game, even if they aren't completely perfect.

This game is one of those gems that come out every so often from of non-AAA developers. One of those games that really show how much the developers cared for the project and spent time and effort into every aspect of it in order to get the most out of each moment. It really shows the potential of gaming as an industry when indie developers with much smaller budgets than big AAA titles can deliver engaging experiences such as this one. The only gripe I have with it is the beginning, which is a little slow, but only for the first 10~20 minutes or so. This is an incredibly well made game, and I can't say that enough. The music is spectacular and worked provoke a sincere emotional response from me, even though I played it through only once. I loved how this game actually made me feel anxious, yes, I actually felt anxiety in a few moments, because I didn't know what were the consequences of my choices, how would one path change what happens next and what would happen to each character, and I see how this would probably be how any person would feel given the situations the game puts you in. When one puts the music together with the simple and atmospherically fitting aesthetic, very good voice acting and its intriguing plot this story driven adventure is one well worth undertaking. A true piece of art.

Well I've been wanting to play this game for a while now and I've finally gotten 'round to it.
Likes: Incredibly fun to play. The guns feel great, all the different vehicles and machines you pilot feel great, and all the enemies feel satisfying to kill. The engaging story was quite a surprise, as I came into this game thinking it would just be action action action. The architecture looked amazing and there was enough environment variety to keep things fresh every chapter. The little snippets of newspapers really helped build the world and made everything feel real. I felt like an actual soldier rebelling against the Nazi regime. The characters felt engaging and I felt a genuine sense of camaraderie with my allies.
Dislikes: Once in a while you can get lost as indicators are rare and sometimes you travel through rooms that look exactly the same. Switching guns is also somewhat tedious as there are a lot of options. The game should probably pause in the background when scrolling through weapons.
Overall, a great game. I can definitely see why this was Totalbiscuit's GOTY in 2014.

Have you been looking for a fun racing game for you and your friends that brings back the old days of an SNES and Mario Kart? Well look no further, because it has arrived, and it really is that good.
From nostalgia driven track design, to the humorous characters, the driving control depth, to the zany weapons this is the best Sonic game I've ever played. It at least ranks in the top 3. I didn't even mention that there are 3 disciplines to master. You don't master land, sea and air on their own. You tackle them all in the same track while it statically changes as you progress through the race. All of this while trying to keep your boost up, your butt covered, and your speed up.
You can play up to 4 player local split screen. That's right 4 players!!!!!! Or go online for a race, or 2, or a battle. Even thinking about all this has me trying to type in as much info into each sentence as possible.
The bottom line is this: If you are a fan of arcade racing games or karting games, this is a must buy. If you like fun group play games, this is a must buy. The only people who shouldn't get this are people that don't like games. Or hedgehogs I guess. You can find this game on sale for $7.50 or less. If you're even thinking about purchasing at that price just do it. You can thank me later.
The only reason I'm not giving this game 5/5 is because IT'S HARD! I really mean it. The game does not ramp up difficulty. The difficulty on hard or expert is seriously a challenge even on the very first race. If you are unable to complete something on hard you will not be able to unlock the entire World Tour/Career Mode.
Rating: 4.5/5

Remember when you could play a platformer on the PC that was just fun? We get it, you're either a hardcore platformer fan from back when or you're a millenial faux retro hipster and you want to prove to the world and to yourself just how hardcore or retro you are. I hate to burst your bubble, but there was a little more to it than putting pixels and spikes everywhere when it came to having a successful game in the 80s-90s. Alot of the time fun had to be involved as a priority, crazy i know! This trend of indie pixel wiggling difficulty just to be difficult games is beyond tiresome. It was a dead horse back when IWBTG fangames became a thing, which is a while back by now! Trust me, this kind of game is nothing like retro gaming at its core, it's more for the idiots who drew parallels between the crash bandicoot re-release and Dark Souls.
Having ranted about what the game represents and what it doesn't, I'll discuss more about what this game is. It's Super Meat Boy without some of the more fun mechanics, the good music or the humour. Not to say theres no (loosely defined) humour here, because it's full of anti jokes and "it's funny because everything is bad here". So if you're that kind of trendy, depressing person you may like that aspect. But, everything is like this, as it goes out of it's way to be as joyless and depressing as possible. If this is the art direction, and i'm pretty sure it is, well he accomplished it! If you're one of those "ironicly enjoying" kids, i'm sure this was intended for you! For people who unironicly enjoy fun, i doubt you will enjoy this!

I don't know which one came first.  Luxor or Zuma... but they're essentially the same game with a slightly different theme.  Zuma focuses on an inca/aztec style while Luxor focuses on ancient Egypt.
They're not 100% clones of each other, and neither one was terribly original to begin with. Basically, a stream of colored balls come rolling along a path and you have to launch other colored balls so that when 3 or more of the same color are side by side, they disappear.
Zuma occasionally makes a ball glow to signify that it contains a powerup, and luxor makes any 3 consecutive matches give a random power up.  Some of the power ups are very much the same (notably the one that gives you a laser sight to show you where the ball will wind up) and some are way different, such as the dagger powerup which allows you to eliminate single balls with each shot.
It's fun enough to play for 10-30 minutes at a time but after that it starts wearing thin.  There just isn't enough progression through the game to make it feel like you're doing anything other than clearing a level (set number of waves? Predermined score? I have no idea).
I think the edge in this case goes to Zuma Deluxe by PopCap.  It just has more character to it and some occasional humor.  This game is much more dry by comparison.   They're both still fun (in small doses) though.

It's a pleasant looking game, it's got a fantastic community, it's got wealths of potential, and I'm genuinely excited to see where the game is this time next year.

Amazing short little game -- you won't believe this is a port from XBLIG, given that it's easily the best game ever released on that platform.
Yes, you'll finish it in a few hours even your first time through, but it's enjoyable beginning to end. Every stage feels lively and intricate, but the puzzles never get frustrating. The music is particularly amazing as well.
I can't recommend playing the
bonus levels, however. Unlike the main game, those levels overstay their welcome and require extremely precise control, beyond what I feel the game's engine really allows -- Try dashing into a one-block spot and you'll hit the wall by a pixel or two every other time. This never matters in the main game, but in AIP it'll kill you over and over.
Even though I gave up on those stages, Escape Goat is absolutely worth $5 for the main game alone.
Post-Escape Goat 2 update: This one still stands out as the best. EG2 is great too, but it's absolutely worth it to start here.
