At the right price, it's an OK buy.
Combat is too easy in the beginning, but too wacky in the end.  For example, staffs are great at the beginning, but they require magic affinity later on.  Eventually, they're awful since enemies move way too fast (such as ghouls and vampire knights), so those magic affinity points are wasted.  You don't really need them even for casting spells since mana potions recover mana at a fixed 50 mp/potion.  Daggers are the weapon of choice later on, but early on, you really can't assassinate everyone, especially when playing on hardcore.  Going stealth really doesn't yield many combat options aside from equipping stronger daggers and armor, but later on, you don't care anyway since you're just slashing like crazy to land hits on those fast enemies anyway.
Archery's mad weak.  Don't even bother going for headshots.  They don't count.
Magic is only good in the mid game.  In the beginning, spells are too weak.  In the end, they're strong, but only against individual enemies which means it doesn't help against packs (until you unlock inferno and sanctuary which are way OP, but only if you land the initial hit.  If you miss, then you might as well just reload your quicksave since you'll be dead before you know it).
The story's kind of interesting.  It makes you really think about good and evil since the plot isn't straightforward.  Good guy orcs that fight against not so bad demons is a neat angle, and in between is a powerhungry necromancer leader who's trying to stop a prophecy from coming true.  You can really think about why you're doing what you're doing.  The story never really explains why your father is locked away by dragons either, and it makes you wonder if his "demonic" heritage is only opposed based on what he looks like.  There's no real indication that the demons did anything "bad" to deserve getting locked away.
Also, the rope bow gives a lot of exploration options, and combined with the burglary skill, you can find a lot of helpful loot.  Actually, you'll end up throwing a lot of gear away just to make space for future discoveries.
The game seems to offer the chance to play through in many different ways, but ultimately, you really can't.  You use staffs in the beginning, daggers later on, and a few support spells (freeze, charm, and heal) to carry you through...
...and all the while, kicking enemies off a cliff, into a fire, or into a wall of spikes is still your coup de grace.

I simply adore this game.  Everything about it makes me happy: the look, the sound, the music, the title and characters and tone of writing, the way the controls feel, and of course the puzzles that deliver your satisfying "a-ha!" moments.
However, most of all what I love about it is the mechanical movement of all the room elements.  You see, most of what you actually do in Escape Goat is trigger switches, wary of their consequences, which typically involve all manner of blocks and platforms and electric arcs and explosives changing positions in ways that are necessary for completing the room but will also kill you if you haven't planned things out properly.
What I find so wonderful is that all of these things that change do so along tracks and pulleys and cogs that animate throughout the background.  Blocks do not merely shift into new positions but rather travel to them believably and in concert with other moving pieces.  This is hardly necessary to the gameplay, but it creates an aesthetic experience that transports me behind the eyes of a child seeing a trip passage in a fireplace or a hidden compartment under a stair for the first time—every time.  I sometimes find myself triggering switches without cause, only to study the resulting machinations.  It just sparks my imagination, one of those uncategorizable details of videogames that make them a delight uniquely to you.
Will you agree with my feelings?  I have no idea, but it's worth a try, wouldn't you say?

This is a solid 2D platformer with a simple theme and excellent soundtrack, that is why i recommend it.
If you like these types of games then my praise will not be effective, but I must warn you. Not adding to the other reviews here I have two HUGE problems with it.
Problem 1:
The vast majority of levels are hard but well designed. Every main level is never too hard and you can 100% the main story quite easily. But there are some hidden levels that you can unlock known as "Cart Levels". While these are not essential (praise the lord) they are considerably harder than anything else in the game. Harder than most levels even in Super Meat Boy.
I say this not because they require precision or reflexes. They are insanely long and unforgiving. Some people like grinding through time consuming levels over and over again until they learn not to stuff up, but fundamentally this difficulty doesn't challenge anything other than trial and error, and memory. I do not find this fun at all. If you want all of the achievements (like me) you will have to complete 10 or more stage levels in one life. Each stage may not be that hard, but doing them perfectly every time can be very stressful and dull. If you are trying to practice one life over and over again, you will have to quit the cart and enter again, which wastes a lot of time.
Defend it however you want, I call this poor design.
Problem 2:
People seem to have a hard time explaining the difficulty of this game, comparing it to super meat boy a lot. Relative to other platformers, this is not that close to SMB. The difficulty may vary from player to player. But there are two things everyone agrees with in the end. The cart levels are what make this game extremely difficult (and the final stage, but the final stage is optional and really kind of fitting), and the difficulty spikes really fast. I consider this an underrated problem because a lot of other platformers will either : A, slowly introduce you to more and more obstacles and interactions, or B, will introduce you to the whole world at once, allowing you to explore and come back at your own pace.
This game is neither. It is linear and branches at only two points ever. The difficulty is immediately above what i consider new players to be comfortable with. There is still a progression of difficulty  throughout the game, but it is so small it is negligible (until you reach the last few worlds where it spikes again). Being used to these kinds of games i had no problem with it, but I can easily imagine someone who starts this game with no experience at all. I'm willing to bet it wouldn't be so fun.
TL:DR
Game = Solid
Bonus levels (cart levels) = not fun/boring
Difficulty progression = starts hard doesn't change for most of the game

The story chronicles the homeless and extremely unstable Banzai when he is arrested for urinating on the New York Mayor's limousine. In a sphere of corruption and powerplay political repercussions abound. Banzai is left locked in a cell and facing three jaded detectives. All 4 under threat from the politically outmanoeuvered precinct captain to find dirt on him. There is also a pr0stitute but don't get the wrong idea.
What the detectives finally unearth gives poignant reason to Banzai's mental instability.
Jon Bernthal gives a stellar and unforgiving performance as Banzai, depicting in vivid detail the destroyed mind, his mysterious and brutal past and the violent consequences of it.
I don't often see performances as stark and powerful as what Bernthal accomplishes here.
The three detectives are played by Bruce McGill, Mark Nassar (yes, the original writer) and Charles Malik Whitfield who provide an above average performance in their supporting roles, managing their characters well and believably throughout the film.
At a few points the acting can be somewhat wooden, in other parts the writing can seem forced. Nevertheless they portray everything from hardline professionalism to friendly camaraderie and contemplative pity very well.
The two other supporting actors are Elizabeth Rodriguez and Jon Getz that play the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and precinct captain respectively. There is nothing much to say about their performances, they weren't bad but they weren't spectacular.
I have tried to keep this review as succint as possible with a lot of big words to impress clever people and intimidate everyone else. Overall I recommend this film highly for those wanting what I have described.

Rimworld is a colony sim game run by a one-developer shop. The game consists of picking a starting location, some colonists that will do the surviving, and a storyteller that creates the challenges you'll face.
Through the game you'll build your colony, manage assets like raw resources, food, colonist mental health, colonist physical health (damn bullets), defenses and a host of other things! Rimworld keeps you on your toes as you expand and build necessities to survive challenges like Raiders, crop blights, electrical fires, man-hunting animals, disease and a host of other horrible, horrible things.
The UI is simplistic but easy to navigate, allowing you to make adjustments to allow efficiency in playing the game.
The fun thing is that every time you play, you learn a little more about what works and what doesn't work. The most fun is at the beginning, when you're struggling to survive in a harsh environment with an AI storyteller that wants you to SQUIRM. I definitely recommend enabling permadeath to remove save scumming, and it's hilarious to watch your colony get destroyed in the most unanticipated of ways.
Rimworld also boasts a combat engine that has an extra tactical layer than what these games usually have. Distance/cover/weapon type/hit location all come into play. Sometimes your colonists are fine, other times they're down a finger/hand/leg/eye/kidney (especially kidneys!).
Overall, I play this game obsessively every time a new release is out (one dev shop, takes some time but damn is it worth the wait). Definitely worth the money!

Reasons to buy it:
-If you'd love to play a very hard platforming game.
-If you are a masochist and love to feel pain.
-If you want to die.
-If you want to enjoy a hard but with pretty well designed levels game.
-The soundtrack is an awesome remix of some classical music songs, of which really fits the "dark" theme and atmosphere of the game.
-You loved Super Meat Boy.
Reasons to not buy it:
-You dislike hard or "stressing" platformers.
-You absolutely didn't like Super Meat Boy because it's too hardcore for you.
This game is made by Edmund McMillen (the creator of Super Meat Boy and also The Binding of Isaac) and Tyler Glaiel. This game in particular feels like a spiritual successor to Super Meat Boy, but there is no wall-jumping, instead you can hang on ledges, and while it may seem simple at first, it opens a lot of possibilities platforming-wise and gives a fair enough different feel than SMB, and also it ends up being more complex. The most difficult levels and even some achievements are considerably more difficult than Super Meat Boy, if you want a pretty challenging platforming game this may be your game. The controls feel perfect and precise, if you make a mistake, the mistake will be completely yours, no bad control design involved.
Also you collect tumors and retro game cartridges, you can play them after in your house, they feature a retro aesthetic design, with their own "retro" remix of a classical song, and most of these retro games are extremely challenging, some of them being the most difficult challenges in the game.
The game features a good amount of collectible and secrets, with various endings.
Highly recommended if you are a masochist like me.

Early Alpha Review
The moment you start up the game you see the vision and inspiration of the dev team. This game is clearly not a clone or a quick money grab like we have seen from so many other games. The dev team is putting some really love behind this game and it is utterly beautiful. I am pretty astonished at what they have done in this early Alpha I HIGHLY recommend anyone and everyone that is interested in the Voxel MMO genre that is starting to develop to throw their support behind this game.
Whats the Good
- Absolutely beautiful environments with amazing atmosphere. You really start to get immersed into the game because of the graphics and sound
- Exploration, you can go anywhere and everywhere. The grappling hook adds a really fun angle to the game that lets you move quickly through the immense environment
- The vision of the dev team is translated really well into the game. You can tell they love their work and this game
- The mechanics are solid. Of course Minecraft laid the framework for Voxel games so at this early Alpha state most of the mechanics mimic any other voxel game
- Its on steam, big plus!
Whats the Bad
- At first you are overwhelmed at the shear vastness of the environment. The world is immense and it can be a bit daunting at first
- Lots of unclear block types. The world is alien so you have purple blocks, strange blocks with circles and others. You aren't sure as to what tool to use on what blocks. But it doesn't take much to harvest blocks so it isn't a big deal.
- Performance is a bit slow and you can understand why. My newer gaming laptop handles it well but there are times that performance gets hit and being in early Alpha it is understandable.
Getting the Game
I really don't like pre-ordering games and I like getting into Alphas even less. Too many times the games don't live up to the hype or the game turns into garbage. Heck some devs just abandon the community for a year. I am a huge fan of MMOs, rogue-likes, and voxel based games. Oort has all of these elements and is doing them well in this early Alpha stage. If you want to support the growing voxel MMO genre I would recommend you get into the Alpha. Even if you don't play it that much supporting the dev team will help push this game and genre forward. We need to support developers like this that are making a great game not just another cheap money grab.
If you don't want to invest in the game yet (I understand I really do) then get the word out on social media to create some hype. The more people know about this game the better it will become.
**Highly recommend and look forward to this game ruining my life when it gets released. Kudos to the dev team over at Wonderstruck.

+ fun "physics based" puzzles and platforming
+ fun retro music that loops well
+ retro graphics that really feel retro, not just "cheap pixel art"
- HUGE difficulty gap between normal and bonus levels
You can see the art and music in the video so I won't comment on that. The puzzels work mostly by playing around breaking blocks, hitting switches, sending your mouse helper around, etc., until you figure out the right order to do it in to beat the room. It's about experimenting and discovery, and isn't frustrating. The platforming in the normal levels isn't anything hard. Something about being a goat head-butting into things makes it fun anyway.
If it looks fun from the video, it probably is fun for you. I say try it.
Then there are the bonus levels. Now I enjoy these, but I spent an entire afternoon in them and only made 30% progress. I'll probably never beat them all. The platforming needs to be perfect, with perfect jumps and perfect timing. You'll die 20+ times figuring out just one jump, then 20+ times on the next, etc., until you figure out the level. Then add in another 100+ deaths since you'll just plain screw up plenty of times. Death is low-frustration because you respawn in 2 seconds, and the music keeps playing without resetting. The music is very catchy and keeps me motivated. But low-frustration over 200+ deaths starts to accumulate into real frustration. :p
So the bonus levels aren't for everyone. I don't regret trying them, since beating even a few is very satisfying. But ... I probably won't finish!

>And basically a complete or even beta 'game'.
This game's in Early Access for a reason, you could say it's Proto-Alpha, but it's still surprisingly presentable even then.

The screenshots do it a certain amount of justice - I'm a fan of the art style, and the animation is smooth and flawless, but I'd argue the sound, music and voices are what really immerse you in this game. The soundtrack is on Spotify for a reason. You will want headphones, turned up.
The dialogue system is a little uncomfortable at first, similar to the Telltale games - get used to interrupting other characters and choosing your line against the clock. I have to be honest this isn't my favourite design choice (after decades of having the luxury of contemplation with basically every other game) but to be fair it probably adds to the gameplay as much as it takes away. Also I'll do you a favour, CTRL brings up the map. Yeah I didn't see that mentioned anywhere ...
All in all a great game, very glad I picked it up. Only wish there was more of it - it took me only 5 hours and I wasn't in a rush. I hope they do a sequel or something. Also +1 for flawless execution on Linux. If only every dev could burst out the gates like this. (pun not originally intended but I'm gonna run with it)

I'm going to keep this very short. Abyss Odyssey is an okay game with a pretty neat art style.
The combat seems complex with move cancels, blocks, dodges, normal attack, jumping attacks, special attacks, and the ability to combine them in interesting ways. It can be a little overwhelming when trying to keep track of all the movesets that you have to fight with and against. Every monster has their own movelist. The player also tends to have access to at least 3 movesets in a run if you're not switching out captured monsters often. The one bad thing about combat is facing which can become frustrating quickly. It can be sometimes difficult to face the correct direction, especially if the enemy walks just far enough to be on the other side of you and evade all your hits. The feeling can be amplified if there are multiple enemies around. I quickly became a big fan of any fast or sweeping/aoe attacks.
You aren't just the character you select, you can be various monsters depending on your level since that determines which ones you can capture. If you die, you come back as a soldier that wields a weapon dependent on your main character until you hit a shrine or trigger a monster stage in-between areas. I saved up 25K gold and spent it on the wishing well to purchase a pretty cool halberd character with plenty of sweeping attacks that covered both sides. She's the one I could beat the game with since her normal attacks are pretty boss, although the monster that wears the sombrero really helped me out in the end. Some monsters feel much better than others and I enjoy playing as the good ones.
Finally, I thought the story had an interesting Chilean flavor (journal pages), the environments were mostly nice (hazards sometimes blended in a little well), and the game is built around replayability if you like collecting monsters or enjoy the fighting system. The map is randomized for every fresh run. The only thing you keep is gold while weapons and equipment will go poof upon game overs.
Abyss Odyssey is okay. You need to be willing to learn how the combat works. I definitely recommend dropping 25K in the treasure room (it's the gold room on the map) for the halberd character for an easier time.

The game looks phenomenal.  I can honestly not think of a better looking 2D side scroller.  The backgrounds are bright and beautifully detailed.  The characters are large, colorful and well animated.  There is some floatiness and screen tearing, but nothing that detracted from the gameplay.
Combat is deep and engaging and of a higher complexity than similar games in the genre.  The player will not get far by simply charging through and mashing the same attack.  One must vary attacks, defend and utilize level changes to effectively negotiate an adversary.  The parallels others have drawn between the combat in Abyss Odyssey and fighting games are warranted.
The replayability of this game is high.  The levels and layouts of enemies and treasure are randomly generated each play through.  You can unlock and play as multiple characters and even capture and play as the game’s enemies.  The dying and extra lives mechanic is quite unique and adds to the overall creativity.
Abyss Odyssey has its own style, which was appreciated. The story unfolds succintly and is of interest without being too laborious or text heavy.  I like to play games and not read or watch them.
The game is initially challenging, but some progress is persistent as character levels, starting areas, learned creatures and gathered, unspent gold carry over between plays.  I had some quick runs before I improved my play and gradually became stronger.
Overall I really enjoyed this game and will continue to come back to it due to its replayability.  I am baffled by the mixed and negative reviews and encourage anyone looking for the high points I laid out to play this game.

This game kinda grew on me.
I was first drawn to Abyss Odyssey because of its art style. Really enjoyed it and I think it’s one of its main distinctive features.
At first, when I started playing, it felt a bit awkward, the controls (keyboard and mouse) felt a bit clumsy and chunky, and I was thinking "disappointed with a great looking game". But I got used really fast.
After this adaptation period, no more felt awkward controls, all went smoothly.
Added to really nice art style, Abyss Odyssey has enough variety to keep a player engaged for a few hours, in my case, 27 hours. It has lots of characters to play with, each with its play style, and the 3 main characters have different abilities to choose from and upgrade. The player starts by choosing one of this main characters to play with, but during the game he can capture the essence of fallen enemies and turn into them.
The game structure is another of the features that caught my attention: on each playthrough, the player has the opportunity to play randomly generated rooms with different difficulty levels, to play special rooms, to play with different characters, to play against an assortment of enemies and to choose and upgrade your equipment, adding to replayability and longevity.
All in all, Abyss Odyssey is a good action sidescroller, with great art style, interesting gameplay and design, and enough to keep a player engaged for a few dozen hours.
On some side notes, it has achievements, which always add value to the game, and also competitive multiplayer, although mostly "dead" due to lack of players, which is fine by me, since I usually don't care much for MP features. I do get annoyed when games have achievements for MP, but in this case I found some friend on steam to help me with the game single MP achievement.

If you don't have Borderlands by now you really missed out on a great game. Borderlands mixes MMO style RPG elements with a FPS game.  Solo play can be fun, but where Borderlands shines is in its multi-player experience. There are no level requirements for playing together, no party xp nerfing, and you gain xp no matter how far away you are from the rest of your team. This means you can split up and accomplish different objectives, or leave the lowest level player at the quest turn-in spot while you move from quest to quest. Gameplay is gory and funny. Some of it can feel repetitive and long play streatches begin to suffer as you find yourself running over the same ground and killing the enemies spawning from the same den over and over. Also, end game is a bit of a disappoint. With all that said, this game is still worth the $20 for the base game. I haven't played the DLC, but some of it seems to link into Borderlands 2 if you care a great deal about story.

I was a fan of Sonic from a very early age, and the only Nintendo products in our house were Gameboys, yet I still never thought I'd buy this game. During the 2012 holiday sale I bought the Sonic bundle (before this game was added to it) but I figured this would be no great loss, because after all it's just another Mario Kart clone right? Perhaps and also perhaps not. Sonic has a lot more going on than any other kart game I've played, and doesn't have the same obvious rubber banding that is present on the more recent versions of Mario Kart, which leaves you feeling more in control of what is actually happening on screen rather than having Nintendo pushing you along with magic bullets and saying "That's it just a little further, the rest of them aren't that far in front of you" before walloping the person in first place for making the other kids look bad. The Sonic karts handle nicely, the ability to perform stunts has been added to get speed boosts, tracks attempt to cause sensory overload in the most excruciatingly pleasing way possible, and your kart frequently transforms into a boat or plane depending on how the track has been destroyed since your last lap or whatever obstacle is coming up. This is a great game to play with friends, but it's equally as good to play by yourself given all the challenges and unlocks that are available. Unlocks based on game progression are absolutely how this sort of game should be done, so I was somewhat disappointed to find that Sega had released a robotic Sonic DLC - but assuming this is just a skin I suppose you can't blame them for trying to wring every last cent out of us. Mind you, this game was a gift so I'm in no position to have a whinge about that. Had I not been given this game, I wouldn't have realised just how good it is, and how it is well worth buying.

Sonic All Stars Racing Transformed is easily one of the best kart racers to be released this generation. With mechanics that promote fun and fairness in game play without penalising skill in the process, something that anyone who has had a blue shell encounter will appreciate and understand. The standard mechanics of kart racers combine with a fusion of diddy kong racing-esque level up weapons, dynamic changing levels that test your skills in all vehicles (most of the time during a single race) Mario kart drop in and out fun.
The single player content (which can be completed with up to four local players also) give a wide verity of challenges and fun, although unlocking all the characters can take a little while for the newly initiated. It’s worth the effort and time to invest. There is a levelling mechanic related to each character that allows you to unlock ‘mod’ that can alter stats on the characters, meaning you can change your play style a little bit upon unlocking these mods, things such as handling, overall speed, acceleration and boost can be modified with these pre-set mods. Even if you don’t win a race it is worthwhile completing races just to gain experience.
The PC version of this game is by far the best, with little to no loading times, improved frame-rates/resolution (Rig dependant) as well as the inclusion of four extra characters, Football Manager, Shogun, General Winter and Team Fortress. Online matches are smooth stable and quick in being setup compared to its console counterparts but can have the odd hiccup at times.
I would highly recommended this game without question, especially when it’s on sale for the likes of £4.99 even without the sale its standard price is easily justifiable.

The End is Nigh is a monotone platformer. The game is brutal, with thousands of deaths on the first campaign alone. The game relies on collecting tumors, 450 tumors specifically. As always, don't buy this game if you're easily offended because Golgotha (The hill where Jesus was crucified) and S.S. Exodus (A ship full of Jews which the Nazis bombed). The game controls like near flawlessly, even in the Betas. The game works as your average platformers except for how you can't wall jump and instead use hooks and ledges to scale walls.
The bonus game carts start off easy enough (even though very few people play them) but quickly turn into hell on earth. Encountering Steven and collecting enough Tumors grants you the ability to attempt collecting an Iron cartridge. Iron cartridges are supposed to symbolize the 5 stages of grief (Helps that they're named after them) during the 4 stages of cancer (Due to tumors) and lastly, accepting death. Glitched carts are encountered in the second campaign and are better versions of normal carts. Acceptance is the final Iron cart but you'll spend days trying to beat it as it has the other four Iron carts and THEN 10 new ones.
The story is simple, your only source of entertainment just broke, now its time to venture into the apocalypse and make a friend. Sounds simple but finding a Heart, Head, and body will lead to thousands of deaths.
I do have some problems with the game though. Acceptance is a bland way to end the Iron saga. The Future stage to collect Depression is bad. The birds are just a tad bit too fast. The machine was boring. The game doesn't even tell you that you get bonuses for not dying at all in a cartridge!
Overall I wouldn't say this game isn't perfect but I'd say this is a 7/10.

This is going to be a mixed review, however I will recommend it for EXPERIENCED or VETERAN MOBA players. If you are starting out in the MOBA scene, this is not really the game for you, sorry, it's simply just not polished enough for people beginning in the world of MOBA's.
I don't have a whole lot of experience with this game so far, but I have clocked literal hundreds of hours on LoL and DotA 2, so I do have MOBA experience.
Positives:
- Personal Courier System: a really interesting idea that I think works well, and helps focus the combat on killing heroes and creeps/minions/brawlers (from now on will be referred to as brawlers), and not on looking out for couriers to earn some extra gold.
- Recipe System: A really cool idea that allows you to change the components that make-up a recipe, thus giving you different stats, but still what the weapon is supposed to do.
- Pets: Another interesting idea, that provides a little bonus for your hero, and aren't too overpowered or take away from the obverall experience
- Last-Hit System: Playing and looking at the demo-videos of Strife it is obvious that they have purposely designed this MOBA to minimise toxicity between players, not only through community (Like LoL) but also through core game components and mechanics, I feel that this works really well, and benefits everyone.
- Constant Stream of Heroes: This is both a positive, and a negative (which will be brought up later). Not much to be said, the more the merrier right?
- Waiting for Loaders: When waiting for other loaders you are placed in the game. Your hero/champion cannot move, but they can level their chosen skill and purchase items from the shop. I like this as it makes waiting for others a little less boring
Negatives:
- Towers: I think every review has covered this, towers are horrendously overpowered. seriously. in League or DotA its possible to tower dive for about half a minute or so to secure an enemy kill, but in Strife, the moment you attack and enemy hero under their tower you are targeted (this is ok), but the towers hit like a truck. for the whole game. Fully levelled people are still scared of those damn things. This needs to be fixed. ASAP.
- Constant Stream of Heroes: Unfortunately the constant stream of heroes is also a case of too many cooks spoiling the broth. With a large amount of new heroes, the ones already in the game cannot be refined fast enough, and there are some glaringly obvious heroes/champions with OP abilities and such.
- Penalty for leaving: You can't play another game until the one you left is over. Yup. Thats it.
There are probably a whole bunch of things that I've missed about this game, but on the whole I enjoy it as a refreshing take on the MOBA scene.
Misc Things:
- No AU servers: This obviously only affects AU players, but a constant ping of 200-300 is kinda annoying.
- No all chat: I just can't find it, maybe it doesn't exist, probably due to the anti-toxic community take the team are going for.
Overall, to conclude, I would say that this game is what it is. Early Access, BETA. Its a pretty cool and new take on MOBA, but its still early access, and needs some (or a lot of) work. If you enjoy MOBAs and know your way around them, give this one a shot, I think you'll like it for what it is. If you are new to MOBAs and are looking for one to start off with? Give this one a miss until you have more experience, simply because I think you'll have a better experience with other MOBA's
Now this is all my exerience with the game, with a measly 10 hours under my belt, thanks for reading guys

So before anything let me clear one thing, ' i ' pesonally see Oort Online as a game of it's own, pushing what's already there to a higher level with new features and ideas that are outstanding. If you want to say this is a "Minecraft clone" ok sure i can understand that, but know that it's not a ripoff, cheap, money grab game, this is as legit as it gets from a "Minecraft clone" , heck it's doing stuff 10x more awesome than Minecraft. Now that's out of the way...
It's in pre-alpha, so a lot of bugs, optimisation issues, not all the content is there...etc, and the price is really high to get it now, in the pre-alpha, but that's going way down once it's released, so I'm just going to talk about the my thoughts of the game with no consideration of the price at the moment, if you want to get in go ahead, but if i had to say realistically, it's not worth getting 'now' for the asking price, would say at the beta stage is a good start.[Update: thought the price was 100$ for 35, if you that's a reasonable price to get in now, so im going to say 'no and yes']
So anyway, the game looks absolutly gorgeous, just look at the pictures and videos. The sound effects were recently added in and it sounds just great. The build part is as nice as the game, and adds detail to it's 'blocks' by making it so you can have a triangle, a slope, some other shapes i don't know what's the name of, and it still has its simplicity in building. There's also blocks with effects, like a bouncing block, slippery block..etc.
Also the portal system in this game is just mind blowingly awesome, where you see a portal in the world, and look through that portal you see another world (another server) in real time, and you go in, in that second you go in, your in another world, in another server that's on the other side of the planet.
Also the addition to hooks in the game is really awesome, aside from the awesome swings you can do with it, it really helps you reach high places with such ease, you don't have to put a block over a block and continue doing it to reach a certain hight of where you fell from. The hook, at this point on, is an essential for me to build.
There's a lot more i can talk about, and obviously there's bad parts about the game, but so far that's been technical problems as mentioned in the beginning, and i can't wait until the game reachs beta to launch, to me this is my next innovative and definitive 'Minecraft'.

Your master has sent you to deliver some sort of artifact to a friend in a far off city, but has transported a woman into your conciousness to be your guide for mysterious reasons. Xana is pretty much a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ version of Cortana from
. You'll either tolerate her character, or outright despise her. Once you actually get to your destination, stuff hits the fan and you're thrust into a campaign to defeat an evil Necromancer. There are quite a few plot twists along the way. The biggest will probably be obvious to you, but I can guarantee there are plenty of left-field ones. The question is... will you even care enough to, well, care about what happens? 6/10
Ahhh, now here's Dark Messiah's shining beacon of awesomeness. I'm going to be blunt about this one, straight out of the gate: Dark Messiah has the greatest first-person combat I've experienced in a game. The guys at Arkane are
when it comes to first-person animations; everything is incredibly silky smooth and satisfying to witness and interact with. As you progress through the game, you'll be rewarded Skill Points which you can then distribute as you please through two skill trees. There's no skill that will drastically change up how you play; just some generic "More HP" or "Slightly Bigger Fireball". Still, it works. You can also get some skill points by finding certain secret objectives within the world.
Dark Messiah's level structure is not unlike Doom or Quake... Littered with clever secrets (Some I didn't find until my fifth or so playthrough!) filled with special loot like new armors and weapons. Using either a Sword & Shield, Dual-Daggers, Staves, Bows, or Magic, you'll slice and dice and stab and smash and burn and freeze and electrocute your way through hordes of Mercenaries, Orcs, Giant Spiders, Undead, and more. Though you can mash your attack button, that is rarely effective. The true combat is found using the various styles of power attacks. Not unlike the system found in Elder Scrolls, you'll preform different attacks based on which direction you are moving. From vertical swipes to long reaching stabs to hard-hitting slashes, you'll need to use every available move to defeat the very clever Orcs later on. Swords are nimble; the all-around weapon. They're capable of parrying foes, and you can even disarm by power-attacking while aiming at the hand. Daggers are lightning fast. They chop up foes before they can get a swing in, and they are capable of instant kills against unaware and fleeing enemies. Staves lack damage, but in smart hands they are the most powerful in the game. They can strike multiple foes at once, and blows to the head almost always stun instantly, leaving the foe extremely vulnerable to being kicked off their feet and into traps and the like. Bows work like you'd expect; headshots instantly kill unaware enemies. Once you get the skill that makes you draw faster and a secret unlimited quiver, it's possible to go bow-only, most definitely.
Magic requires a lot of skill to use effectively. Sure, you have your standard fireballs and lightning bolts and freeze spells, but in my experience it is just too difficult to use solely these in combat. You'll need to be crafty; turn enemies against each other with a mind-control spell, shrink enemies to the size of mice, and lay traps near instant-killing spike-walls in the environment.
About a third of the way through the game, you'll find the Rope Bow. Truly an inventive tool that I would adore seeing in another game. Near useless in combat, this weapon is instead used to navigate the environment; firing at any wooden structure above you will release a dangling rope you can climb and jump from! This one simple tool drastically changes up the level structure from there-on, and gives room for some dastardly secret nooks and crannies.
Admittedly, it does take quite a while to get used to how the game works. But I guarantee you... when it all clicks, you'll be saying "Holy smokes! This is gosh-dang-diddly-dum AWESOME!" 10/10
If you've seen any sort of high fantasy movie, show, comic, or game, you've seen everything in Dark Messiah before. There's nothing visually that is truly original or outstanding. Admittedly, the super weapons later on have some great designs and one of the final levels is a big palette cleanser after hours of trudging through a boring ol' cave system. The environment, the enemies... it's all generic as possible. Thankfully, the sound is a fair bit better. The clang of metal against metal and swooshes of air as swords tear through it are top-notch and really bring a little extra bit of immersion. You'll probably get sick fast of the early Mercenary enemies who seem to always begin a fight with "Hey, pal!", but the later gruffness of Orcs and Goblins and the like feel a fair bit more threatening. 8/10
Between the many different styles of equipment available, the extremely harsh skill point limit, and the myriad of secrets to be found in every corner, you'll definitely want to play this beast more than once. The average first playthrough will probably take 12-15 hours. There are multiple endings, but trust me; you won't be replaying just to see these. The addictiveness of the combat is far more a reason to do so than the plot. 9/10

NOTE: I bought it on retail, played and finished this game BEFORE I had a Steam Account. I only recently Activated it on Steam. As usual, SEE CONCLUSION if you find this review too long.
INTRO:
Set in the UBISOFT world of Ashan (Heroes V world), you play an adventurer named Sareth who sets out on a quest to stop the "Dark Messiah" from releasing the imprisoned Demon Lord who was prophesied to return.
Dark Messiah of Might and Magic is one of the earlier first person magic/melee games of Arkane Studios who would later go on to make Dishonored. This game has a completley different game mechanic from the original Might and Magic games of 3DO and New World Computing.
PROS:
+ Decent Graphics: - This game utilizes the Source Engine. Although, It may not be the most graphically advanced game, it brings, a decent enough atmosphere and pretty environments with a commendable quality texture work.
+ Combat Mechanic: - Also a CONS (See Below). This game has a good blend of magic, melee and ranged combat. Dealing with different kinds of foes may require you to adopt different tactic to efficiently dispose of your target. Stealth mechanic works fairly well. (Not even close to Thief or Dishonored, but enough to satisfy a more stealthy approach on the missions.)
+ Story: - I personally liked the story which is directly related to the Heroes of Might and Magic universe that I'm a fan of. The plot twists and conflicts are well delivered along with some interesting characters. As usual, this is my own opinion and some people might disagree with me.
+ Lengthy Campaign: -Long enough to deliver the story in a satisfying manner. This game also features  multiple ending scenario where your actions would directly impact the game's ending. It Suffers from the Mass Effect 3 Syndrome though. (Feel free to ask me on what the ME3 Syndrome is.)
CONS:
- Combat Mechanic: - Also a PRO (See Above). Despite the availability of different items, magics and tactics, they are all trumped by your might BOOT. Kicking your target either to stun them or send them to spikes (which are conveniently placed) defeats the purpose of having different kinds of weapons, magic and equipment. It becomes repetitive at times.
- Unnecessary Multiplayer: - There are games that were meant for Singleplayer, this is one such game. Unfortunately, for us, a poorly implemented multiplayer is present which most likely diverted some of the developer's money which would have been better spent on advancing the Singleplayer experience.
- Cheesy Voice Acting: - I did enjoy the voice acting but that's me, most people will probably get annoyed with it and so I place it here as a CON.
CONCLUSION:
Though I generally RECOMMEND this game, I, however, think that new players or people new to the Might and Magic lore may not be able to fully appreciate its true value. This is best played by people already familar with Might and Magic. This game is underrated in my honest opinion.
NOT RECOMMENDED if you're looking for an old school Might and Magic (VI to VIII) experience. For that, check out Might and Magic X or Legend of Grimrock. Also not for people looking for an Elder Scrolls experience.

I'll admit, I wasn't sure I was going to like this game at first. The difficulty curve is steep if you're a noob at fighting games, and the rogue-like elements seem to only exacerbate that fact. Eventually, I started to get better at it, and I've even learned a thing or two about how fighting games operate, though I'm still largely a button-masher. My opinion of the game changed from mild dislike, to neutral, to active enjoyment. I'm glad I gave it a chance.
Things I liked:
+ Characters
+ Light, yet enjoyable story that you need to play to discover
+ Smooth combat mechanics
+ Art style
+ Every enemy is playable (nearly)
+ Plenty of randomly generated secrets to find
Things I didn't like:
- Only 3 characters are selectable to start your game, two of which need unlocking
- Forgettable soundtrack
- Lack of variety to the power ups
- The game doesn't do a good job of teaching you about the characters' abilities, though this is saved somewhat by an excellent tutorial by the devs on the steam forums. I had no idea there were more than 3 selectable "moves" for each character.
Overall, I liked this game and while I'd hesitate at full price, when it's on sale, it's a bargain. I don't know if its fighting game elements are good from the perspective of someone who likes fighting games, as I'm awful at them. I do, however, love a good beat-em-up, and based on that, I ended up enjoying the fighting game elements when applied to that. Plays a bit like the beat-em-up mode in Tekken 3, or the adventure mode in Smash Bros.

THIS IS A FIRST IMPRESSIONS
I can't reccomend this to most people, only those who really like Castlevania style games and even then pick it up on sale.
Pros:
-Good soundtrack
-Pretty Visuals
-combat more complex than most metroidvania style games
-likable character designs
Cons
-Very forgettable level design (levels are randomly generated apparently but that doesn't do much to make them interesting)
-Clunky and slugish feeling fighting mechanics
-forgettable level design
-forgettable main character
-either incomplete or just lazy combat implementation (feels like a gimped Smash Bros.)
-Lack of options in VS mode
-Laughably unbalanced
Main Game
Abyss Oddessy seems to take inspiration from Castlevania and it does a decent job of feeling and looking like a Castlevania but thats about where the similarities end. The levels are really kind of generic. I will attempt to explain how so bear with me. The first level is a subterranean cave, you drop from above into a small area with fallthrough platforms and then you enter the cave area. There is a room to the left with enemies or a chest or both and then a path to the right to the rest of the level and sometimes its mixed up vise versa and the rest of the level there might be enemies and small rooms etc with chests and a save altar or whatever.
The next level is really similar to the last but with a different layout. Different platforms, bottomless holes (by the way every level seems to at least have one bottomless hole signified by some kind of black smoke at the opening of it adding to the sort of cookie cutter feel of the levels) and moving platforms, and then some kind of open space where you stop to fight enemies since the game locks you in with black mist that are really just invidible walls. You go through a gauntlet of these levels and either make it to the end or die and when you die your forced to play as a soldier unless you saved at an altar unless you die again and then respawn or restart as the main character. The requirement to save at the altar costs you a pretty penny of the in-game currency you find. The levels are randomly generated apparently but it certainly doesn't make them interesting.
At one point another entrance opens to "the abyss" and this next entrance is more or less very similar to the cave level I mentioned before except with foliage in the background and caterpillars as small enemies rather than spiders in the cave. The layout seems the same as progressing from one level to the next takes you to another similar looking jungle level with a different layout. From what I'm seeing this is what the rest of the game will be like. Otherwise I will update this review if anything changes but the first two levels seem similar.
I'm a little disappointed with the way the levels seem to be considering the prologue or tutorial level had much more varied level building and varied assets (in one section you are in a burning house.) I hope this changes but so far it seems like this game's gimmick which is disappointing because some kind of Castlevania castle with intelligent design would have been better. Right now it just feels like when building these levels someone had a list of level elements or rooms to insert along the way and just checked off each one in a different order.
Story/Character Building
I don't feel much for the story yet but from what I do see I don't really care about the main character. There's no reason to care, she's cold and emotionless and is a silent warrior which I don't find very interesting. This character does talk but with very little emotion.
Multiplayer/Fighting Engine and Mechanics
One of the features of this game is the fighting mechanics and how similar it is to smash brothers but does it live up and do much in the way of being a brawler? I play a lot of smash brothers so I might be biased. The Abyss Rising has things in common with smash brothers but it falls short because of several glaring issues.
1) There is a HP system instead of a percentage system like Smash Brother's health system. As such there are no ring outs and knockback doesn't change with damage taken. Certain characters really benefit from this kind of setup and this segways into the next point.
2) Balance. I have only unlocked a handful of characters to play as so far but some really seem to outclass the others. The big Ice king seems like one of the very best characters at the moment from what I played. He has very long range with his sword and doesn't seem to have enough endlag or startup lag to have some kind of drawback. If he attacks and you are approaching with an attack he will probably win that exchange. I would say you should probably camp him with projectiles until you can find an opening but then he will just use his own. His projectile is a large horse that runs across the screen and is taller than most characters so you either block it and allow your opponent to move in or you jump over it. Rolling doesn't seem like an option becase of the horse's size you will probably still get his by the butt end of the attack after your roll animation is finished.
General Gripes with how the game works
Other gripes I couldn't really categorize. The main character and I'm sure others, has a back air (jump with your back facing the opponent and press the attack button) that is different from the rest of their ariels. In smash these kinds of moves work because of what I pointed out in the first point. An attack like this in Smash Brothers would probably be a powerful finishing move with high knockback that would knock your opponent closer to the edge of the screen or off the stage when your opponent is at low health. In this game its just an average one hit move that makes you vulnerable with your back facing the opponent when you land.
There is no kind of dash and not only does that limit your mobility but it limits approach options as well because an attack out of dash would help characters who feel sluggish and have a hard time approaching the opponent. Grabs automatically send your opponent up right after grabbing unless you press to a direction instantly but at least this seems to allow for combos. For whatever reason attacks you do by pressing a direction and the attack button are binded to the right analog stick. Pressing left, up, or down will bring out an attack corresponding to attack+direction. This also kind of puzzles me. I guess its nice but in this game its very unnecesary. In smash you get a different attack by tilting the analog stick to a direction (halfway or not touching the edge of where the analog touches) and pressing the attack button and this is different from the attack you would get by quickly smashing the analog stick in a direction and pressing the attack button which is called a smash attack and is usually your best kill option. The right analog in smash basically gives you easier access to moves that would knock your opponent off-stage. In this game the same option just seems unnecesary because no matter how you move the analog stick down and press attack you will get the same attack each time.
So far it seems in versus mode there is no option to not choose a support character (which is mostly made up of regular enemies you fight) so after you lose with your main characters you are forced to play your support character. An option to cut that out and play only as the main characters or even the option to play of of the support characters (since some seem pretty fleshed out) alone would have been nice. Instead either suicide your main character to play one of the side characters or declare the match over once your main character dies.
Yes, you can actually play as the bull in the screenshots and he really sucks. This game has a good number of support characters that make you wonder why the studio wasted their time making them playable.

7) Know that as a noob you have a lot to learn and going to your outfit's training sessions will improve your level of awareness.
8) Do your research on what you are getting. Utilize free trials on equipment now and then.
Your first six hours will be spent -dying horribly-
Push through it and team up with experienced players to improve your chances tenfold. Find players you like to work with on a regular basis. Kick♥♥♥♥♥and don't lose hope when you fail in your goals: there will always be a next fight.
Everyone has the potential to do something well in this game; be it driving a tank, piloting a dropship, going in guns blazing, or patching your teammates up against all odds; you can do this.

Even if you don’t win a race it is worthwhile completing races just to gain experience.

Online matches are smooth stable and quick in being setup compared to its console counterparts but can have the odd hiccup at times.
I would highly recommended this game without question, especially when it’s on sale for the likes of £4.99 even without the sale its standard price is easily justifiable.

Nominated this for Haunts My Dreams -award. As it shows from the review, I love the games extensive knowledge of existential questions that I love pondering during my free time. If only I could nominate it for another award, too.
If you like any of the following, please do yourself a favor and buy this game:
Good puzzles, philosophy about humanity, mysterious (but not too obscure) story,
games!
As I'm more into action oriented games, this was lying on my shelf for quite a long time, until recently when I needed a break from all the hectic swordfighting and shooting. Now that I have pretty much finished it, I can say three things with confidence: It is a great game, I loved it to death and I regret postponing it for so long...
I can also say three reasons why you should buy this game the moment you can afford it.
Gameplay wise, it is a good puzzle game. The challenges vary from simple and straightforward, to challenging and complex and finally to those crafty brain-teasers that require every ounce of your processing and planning power (and some luck in finding the correct spots). A good mix, I say! All challenges can be left and later returned to without worry, and the game encourages you to take breaks from puzzles you have trouble with and try others in the mean time.
I've played (even recently) many games that have made me feel various emotions and connect with the character struggles, but this is definitely one of my top 5 emotional rollercoasters. The game is also very philosophy centric, bringing out thoughts and questions that I'm surprised no other game has handled quite as deeply. Do not worry though, you don't need to know a thing about Kant, Voltaire, Platon etc.. Just go in with your gut feelings, and get your world views questioned (and love every minute of it). Or like me, be amazed how extensive the game is in its subjects and thoughts.
Story itself: You start as an android, alone, in a strange greek labyrinth, with only a booming voice telling you to go forward. From there on, it is your choice to uncover the history of this new world, and your purpose in it...
Much of the lore and story is found in text files you uncover throughout your journey, so be prepared for a lot of text. Still, it is a great feeling when you slowly, but surely, start putting the pieces together, and finally uncover the truth of what has happened and where you are.
Just like I'm more into action games, I mostly prefer some faster music types. But this game's beautiful soundtrack is such a wonder to listen to. It's calm and kind, but also mysterious. In a way it reminds me of Journey's soundtrack, even when they are quite distinct from one another. Now merely hearing it its able to rouse up tears from my eyes.
Get this game. If you are a conscious, feeling person, you will love it.

Let me start by saying that Wolfenstein: The New Order is one of the greatest FPS campaigns of all time.
You may be hesitating to buy this title because it is on the ID Tech 5 engine.
If you have played RAGE, you are aware that this engine is designed for consoles.  It has a 60 fps cap, textures stream in as you turn your camera, and texture detail is sacrificed in favor of texture variety.
I want to tell you that even though the engine is still rough, that this game is an absolute blast, and manages to look far better than RAGE ever did.  It is a thrill ride that should not be missed.  You will have to play at 60 fps, but you will be having so much fun that it will not be a constant annoyance.  The textures are much better than in RAGE, but still not as good as other engines up close.  That will not matter because the game moves along at a lightning pace, without a lot of time for stopping and ogling the textures.  Like all ID Tech 5 engines, the game has a constant graininess to it that almost looks like film grain, with no way to turn it off (without also disabling every other post processing effect at least).  You won't spend a lot of time worrying about it because you will be too busy doing frantic batle with hordes of advanced nazis.
This game has excellent voice acting, incredible sound design, a great soundtrack, a thrilling plot, and beautifully designed levels that take place in very memorable settings.  You can progress via stealth or action, and getting caught in stealth does not feel like a need to instantly reload.  The games weaponry is filled with FPS favorites, including throwing knives, silenced pistols, rocket launchers, sniper rifles, lasers, shotguns, and assualt rifles.  All weapons can be used with either aim-down-sights or dual wielding.  The weapons all have recoil and feel familiar as you play with them more.  The AI is above average without being over-the-top.  Enemies will flank you and use grenades to clear you out of hiding.  The enemies are varied and unique, and you will come up with different strategies to handle each of them.  The plot is exciting, a 12 hour rush you will want to complete in one sitting.  There are 'perks' you unlock by completing simple tasks (like killing 2 people with a single grenade, or assassinating an officer from stealth).  These perks give you useful advantages such as faster reload, or highlighting collectibles on the map.  This becomes quite useful, because there are a lot of collectibles and hidden secrets to find in this game.  The game gives you a choice in the first level that affects both some minor aspects of the plot and some minor aspects of every level.  Between that choice and the collectibles, there is a lot of incentive to replay the game - as an added bonus you keep your perks, collectibles, and progress as long as you start through the level select.
This game is just absolute fun.  Though the game is not flawless, all the flaws are a result of using the ID Tech 5 engine.  Don't let that stop you from enjoying a game that is right up there with legends like Bioshock, Half-Life, and Goldeneye.

So at first I was skeptical to really purchase this as it was in alpha and I generally stay away from unfinished games, especially when they're charging a steep price point for an alpha game.
However, I heard a lot about it, seen a lot of gameplay, and I figured I'd give it a shot.
Now, at first I had a lot of issues trying to actually play. 90% of the time it'd freeze on the control schematic screen.
Many seemed to have had this issue, but a fix for me was just uninstalling a few large games and having more storage space available. Since then, the freezing has been minimal.
As for acually playing, it's a very fun and challenging game. There's a bit of a learning curve and you REALLY NEED A MIC. It's Squad, and communication is KEY. Most servers will kick you if you do not have a working, functional microphone. The gameplay is intense and realistic, albeit perhaps not as realistic as ArmA, but it is very interesting. And for an Alpha game, it can almost be said it's finished, but it isn't. It has so much content for solely being in alpha that it makes you think what else they'll be adding to the game when it fully releases, and theres still gonna have to be a beta phase too!
As for features, you have four teams for different maps. Russian Army, United States Army, Militia (pretty much chechnyans), and the Taliban. There's also a good assortment of maps. As for weaponry, there's a decent amount. To unlock more you have to have a certain amount of members in your squad, so be sure to get the max, 9, to fully see what they have to offer.
The game is pretty good looking, the movements aren't too terrible, as when I run I feel like my character has weight, meaning that the pack and gun truly feel realistic, as if I was holding it.
There's also a good amount of vehicles available, too -- From Transport Trucks to APC's. And I am sure there will be more.
I don't necessarily condone paying full price for an Alpha game, but you can find great deals on♥♥♥♥♥ most likely. Squad is definitely a game worth purchasing if you're into ArmA and other military video games that focus on realism.

I've heard about this game before. It was probably the first fantasy FPS I've seen.
Got it on a sale and boy was I pleasantly surprised. I've played the whole game through in one sitting.
Despite the story, characters and voice acting being rather generic and the game being very linear, the combat and mechanics of the game are really good.
The game features multiple weapon types such as swords, daggers, bows, axes, staffs and shields. Tools such as hammers and pickaxes can be used as weapons too.
The game has 3 (small) skill trees that all can be leveled independently (though it is recommended to stick to one at the beginning) and unlock new combat moves, spells or increase your basic stats.
Combat is pretty simple but can be approached in different ways. You can throw props at enemies and kick them into hazards. Use a frost spell to freeze the ground and watch them slip off into a pit. Priceless.
Because it runs on the Source engine you can expect decent physics. The game has a lot of destructible objects lying around that you can use to throw at your enemies.
The game even has half life 2's gravity gun (reskined into a telekinesis spell) that you can use to mess around with.
Another thing worth mentioning is that you can grab and climb up ledges, ropes and chains. Later in the game you also get a rope bow that lets you attach ropes to wooden surfaces and climb up them.
I'm not arachnophobic but god damn the spiders in this game. The game seems to have a serious spider fetish. In fact the whole story is linked to spiders.
Speaking about spiders, they are absolutely terrifying. Reason being that the character and npc design in terms of models and textures is great. Stuff looks interesting and quite believable. From dull gray castle guards and bald necromancers to sexy demon ladies. All really well made.
When specing into the stealth build the game suffers from the same problem Skyrim does. You can stand in darkness or crouch in semi dark areas and just backstab enemies one by one as others come to check what happened. It becomes ridiculously easy to kill enemies. Not to mention just shoot your bow from a hidden spot and enemies will not know what hit them. If you get spotted however you'll have a hard time as the game is pretty darn hard. I started on the hard difficulty and had to start over because it was too hard, especially because I didn't spec the right skills at the start.
TL;DR:
-Fun, diverse combat
-Good physics
-Kicking things
-Great npc design in terms of models and textures
-Kicking things into other things
-Optional quests that change certain story aspects and the final outcome; multiple endings
-Kicking things off things
-Rope bow
-Kicking things into other things
-Gravity gun
-Replay value
-Source engine; runs great on old pcs while looking relatively good
-Multiple routes in some cases
-Lots of worthwhile secrets.
-Generic characters
-Predictable story
-Boring voice actors
-Linear levels
-Little RPG elements; no stores, no open world, no backtracking
-No mod tools (considering it's the source engine); dead multiplayer as a result
-Conveniently placed spiky plates to kick enemies into everywhere

I kicked a guard in the crotch and sent him flying towards a firey death. 10/10.
Okay, seriously tho, Dark Messiah is a game that wants me to hate it: The combat is repetitive and dull early on (not to mention some of the very frustrating enemy mechanics), the story is very predictable, the environment design can sometimes be really confusing and, to top it all off, the game is riddled with glitches (but considering this is a Source based game, I think that’s to be expected).
But yet, I can’t dislike this game, no matter how hard I try: It’s incredibly immersive; it has an amazing atmosphere and succeeds at making you feel like some sort of almighty jack-of-all-trades warrior. The level design can be confusing, yes, but it’s creative and entertaining. The combat does get a lot quicker and more intense as the game goes on, and the huge “bosses” you have to fight through the game are all epic and nerve-wrecking.
Overall, this game is a recommend for me, but only to people who are willing to overlook some pretty major flaws in order to find a very entertaining and unique adventure. Fully action-based FPSRPGs are hard to find, and Dark Messiah finds that niche nicely. If nothing else, give the demo a shot. It gives you a pretty good idea of what you’re in for.

An action-adventure taking place in a fantasy world and all this with Valve's Source engine! I liked how varied game they developed - you can be a master of swords or become an archer or simply stick with magic. There are a lot of traps here and there which means the game lets you use the environment to kill your opponents. For example: you kick a support beam after which a dozen barrels are dropped on your enemy. Or you can sneak up to those standing near cliffs and kick them down into the abyss. This environmental combat is what makes Dark Messiah a unique game. Looting exists but you cannot really equip that many weapons - it is as if the creators wanted to put the system there as it was a requirement for an RPG anyway.
Putting the insignificant looting system aside Dark Messiah is a very good fantasy game. If you love Might & Magic you can pick up its FPS iteration: you won't regret it.

Abyss Odyssey has some pretty clever ideas and is a pretty fun 2D brawler after some adjustment. Most of the problems I have with it are related to the co-op. First, the netcode is just bad. When you're not the host be prepared for assets to not load in properly or at all, rubberbanding, and occassional gamebreaking desyncs (for instance my coop partner once just had a black screen and couldn't move, while on my screen they were standing in midair between platforms).  Second friendly fire being the default in co-op, just do yourselves a favor if you play this game co-op and don't turn friendly fire on. The menu argues the game is "balanced" for it, but the game is really plenty punishing without your partner stabbing you in the back, and sitting in your side of the arena waiting for an enemy to break off from your partner so you can safely attack them is pretty lame. Additionally, the enemies don't have friendly fire and can freely stack up and overwhelm you, and more of them spawn in the cooperative mode.
There are also a lot of cheap shots in this game. You'll drop into a pit and a waiting enemy will attack you before you can even see what's happening, or you'll hit a trap. Enemies will spawn right on top of you immediately whipping out punishment. It's not terrible when you're prepared for it, but still bleh.
As a single player game it's pretty well balanced and fun. I really enjoy the simple "smash bros" emulating controls, although the game does lack the polish and nuance of smash I still respect that direction. The art is pretty great, although attack animations are sometimes a bit wonky.
Ultimately, if 2D Brawlers aren't your standard fare there are better ones to try first, but if it's a favored genre then Abyss Odyssey is certainly worth a look.

Abyss Odyssey is often misunderstood.  I would best categorize it as an adventure/platformer/roguelite, but there is nuance which cannot be conveyed by those genres alone.
If you like a game with mystery, challenge, and a weird hybrid of fighting game (a la Street Fighter) and platforming beat-em-up, Abyss Odyssey may be in your lane.
Let's start with the art direction and soundtrack, both of which are phenomenal.  There is also a metagame, by which the ways other people play the game as a whole influence the difficulty and types of enemies you may encounter as bosses.  I don't completely understand how it works, but it is interesting to know.
The controls, for me at least, are fine.  When you consider them to be closer to a fighting game than something which requires immense precision like Metroid or Ori and the Blind Forest, they seem properly tuned.  Many complain about this, but I think it is alright once your expectations are set, rather than expecting a tight platformer and getting something "sluggish".
Replayability is high, as that is a main draw for this game.  It took me a few plays to get to the final boss, but now I'm downing the Warlock regularly, and I still don't feel like I'm finished with it.
Of course, this is best played with a friend (local or over the internet) so grab a 2-pack and game it up.

Rimworld is a colony sim game run by a one-developer shop. The game consists of picking a starting location, some colonists that will do the surviving, and a storyteller that creates the challenges you'll face.
Through the game you'll build your colony, manage assets like raw resources, food, colonist mental health, colonist physical health (damn bullets), defenses and a host of other things! Rimworld keeps you on your toes as you expand and build necessities to survive challenges like Raiders, crop blights, electrical fires, man-hunting animals, disease and a host of other horrible, horrible things.
The UI is simplistic but easy to navigate, allowing you to make adjustments to allow efficiency in playing the game.
The fun thing is that every time you play, you learn a little more about what works and what doesn't work. The most fun is at the beginning, when you're struggling to survive in a harsh environment with an AI storyteller that wants you to SQUIRM. I definitely recommend enabling permadeath to remove save scumming, and it's hilarious to watch your colony get destroyed in the most unanticipated of ways.
Rimworld also boasts a combat engine that has an extra tactical layer than what these games usually have. Distance/cover/weapon type/hit location all come into play. Sometimes your colonists are fine, other times they're down a finger/hand/leg/eye/kidney (especially kidneys!).
Overall, I play this game obsessively every time a new release is out (one dev shop, takes some time but damn is it worth the wait). Definitely worth the money!

Let me start by saying that Wolfenstein: The New Order is one of the greatest FPS campaigns of all time.
You may be hesitating to buy this title because it is on the ID Tech 5 engine.
If you have played RAGE, you are aware that this engine is designed for consoles.  It has a 60 fps cap, textures stream in as you turn your camera, and texture detail is sacrificed in favor of texture variety.
I want to tell you that even though the engine is still rough, that this game is an absolute blast, and manages to look far better than RAGE ever did.  It is a thrill ride that should not be missed.  You will have to play at 60 fps, but you will be having so much fun that it will not be a constant annoyance.  The textures are much better than in RAGE, but still not as good as other engines up close.  That will not matter because the game moves along at a lightning pace, without a lot of time for stopping and ogling the textures.  Like all ID Tech 5 engines, the game has a constant graininess to it that almost looks like film grain, with no way to turn it off (without also disabling every other post processing effect at least).  You won't spend a lot of time worrying about it because you will be too busy doing frantic batle with hordes of advanced nazis.
This game has excellent voice acting, incredible sound design, a great soundtrack, a thrilling plot, and beautifully designed levels that take place in very memorable settings.  You can progress via stealth or action, and getting caught in stealth does not feel like a need to instantly reload.  The games weaponry is filled with FPS favorites, including throwing knives, silenced pistols, rocket launchers, sniper rifles, lasers, shotguns, and assualt rifles.  All weapons can be used with either aim-down-sights or dual wielding.  The weapons all have recoil and feel familiar as you play with them more.  The AI is above average without being over-the-top.  Enemies will flank you and use grenades to clear you out of hiding.  The enemies are varied and unique, and you will come up with different strategies to handle each of them.  The plot is exciting, a 12 hour rush you will want to complete in one sitting.  There are 'perks' you unlock by completing simple tasks (like killing 2 people with a single grenade, or assassinating an officer from stealth).  These perks give you useful advantages such as faster reload, or highlighting collectibles on the map.  This becomes quite useful, because there are a lot of collectibles and hidden secrets to find in this game.  The game gives you a choice in the first level that affects both some minor aspects of the plot and some minor aspects of every level.  Between that choice and the collectibles, there is a lot of incentive to replay the game - as an added bonus you keep your perks, collectibles, and progress as long as you start through the level select.
This game is just absolute fun.  Though the game is not flawless, all the flaws are a result of using the ID Tech 5 engine.  Don't let that stop you from enjoying a game that is right up there with legends like Bioshock, Half-Life, and Goldeneye.
Just play it. From the story to the mechanics this game is a straight 10/10 for any FPS Action fan.
