Strife is a mechanically simplied however innovative take on the MOBA genre. It's fast paced and very much skill-based. There are a lot of user friendly features and some anti-toxicity measures in place to ensure players to have a good time. It's a fun experience that any MOBA enthusiast should not miss and new comers can enjoy. Also it is completely Free2Play and
Before we move on to my full analytical review, I would like to say something about myself and what this review will address. I am a pretty avid MOBA player. I seek to play almost every MOBA that exists in Planet Earth. If you can name it, I have probably played it. When I play a MOBA, I stick with it till I have a very good idea about the game and make an informed decision on whether the game is worth continue playing. I am decently high skilled, achieving high brackets usually in competitve ranked ladder. Therefore trust me when I say I will be judging the game as subjectively as possible and applying constructive criticism where needed. It's sad to see the popular reviewers having no idea what a proper review should be. I hate for the newcomers to be driven away by ill-conceived ideas and misinformation due to the lack of understanding of the game as depicted by these reviews. Ok, if you have read this far, it means you actually care about trying out the game seriously and it's safe to say you have made a wise choice. Here's we go.
Strife is a gorgous looking game. While it may not be the most advanced graphics-wise, it strikes a good balance between performance and look. It has wonderful color pallets. Everything looks bright and vibrant, unlike S2 Game's previous MOBA Heroes of Newerth which is grim and dark. Character and skill animations look very smooth. It's always a joy to see teamfight breaking down with all the colors flying through the air. Effects are pretty distinguished to each other and in no time you can fully appreciate them without getting confused. If you have an observant eye, you might even notice some heroes fly/run faster when they get the speed boost moving out of the fountain and environments getting knocked around when spells hit them resulting in debris falling off or the tree branches wiggling.
Why do I make a separate section about this instead of including it with the one above? Because Strife's character design for the most part is pretty uniquely different from other MOBAs. Paraphrasing
, how often do you get to play a super hero cat that throws lightning yarn balls in a cape? Most heroes are humanoids and anthropomorphized, but they all behave in a manner that suits their character. Moxie is the said super hero kitty. Carter is a blue beast dragging two goblins on a cart filled with fireworks and explosives. Trixie is a witch riding on a broom with a horsehead thinking she is a cowgirl. Vex is an alien from Vorbis in a space suit shooting missles and lasers. Apart from the heroes, even the pets and creatures in the game have their own personality. You can have a monkey, a rhino or even a freaking triceratops as a pet companion with you in your adventure. Krytos is a giant creature you can unleash to help your team. You can see him jumping into towers and disabling them while he brutally plummels them or how he pounds his chest before he grabs a giant boulder out of the ground and throws it at the enemies. The characters all feel alive in the world created.
Strife has a dynamic music system. When you are running around in between fights and nothing is happening, the music is melllow and soothing. As a fight break out, the music becomes more dramatic and heart-pumping. If you are pushing the enemy base the music switches to a battle trance alike, getting you ready for the impending victory you feel you can almost grasp. It's a very nice touch. Sometimes it fits so nicely you probably won't even notice it's there.
Heroes all have their distinct voice acting. Ace makes glorious and cheesy remarks. Hale whispers to the players in a calm tone and occasionally lets out his rage in battle. Moxie the super hero cat just, well, meows in different pitches. It's wonderfully done with a great deal of character. The only complain some would have is some heroes could come across as unenthusiastic.
This is going to be the longest section and where I will apply the most criticism as I consider it being the most important. Please bring plenty of eye drops for incoming soreness. I will divide this up into many parts as each deserves its own analysis.
Like most MOBAs, you control a single hero. Everyone has 3 basic spells and 1 ultimate. Not all the spells are active so some heroes will have fewer buttons to press. You have 3 lanes and mid lane is slightly shorter. Minions spawn from your base and attack the enemy minions automatically. There are towers protecting the base along the lanes. You will when you destroy the enemy base, the Crux. Pretty straightforward for people with a bit of MOBA knowledge. The formula is there and now onto the game changers next.
Last hitting gold is shared between all the heroes in proximity. Say a small minion is worth 60g. With 2 players nearby, each will get 30g. 3, 20g. 4, 15g etc. However when only a single hero is in proximity, he/she gets 36g, the rest of the 24g is split evenly to the rest of the team, gaining them 6g each. This applies to jungle creeps and even hero bounty kills.
In place of other MOBAs' "Summoner Spells" or "Glyphs" or whatever variations they call them, Strife has pets instead. These cute little things follow you into combat, providing different benefits to either further compliment your role or diversify it. They all have one active component and two passive ones. There are a great variety of pets and each fills a unique role for your playstyle. It is critical to choose your companion wisely.
You can customize the items in game with elixirs you earn per game. Craft items can have their basic components replace with something else of the same component value. You can also apply an enchantment to the item which provides a marginal benefit but at the same time increasing the item cost in-game. It's always relatively balanced this way so even without crafted items, you won't experience a notable disadvantage. I have not spent any real money in crafting and I already have a lot of items crafted. You just need to play the game.
The in-game UI is quite nicely designed. It tells you everything you need to know without being a huge cluster. You can also rebind the keys on the UI as you play directly while holding down Capslock or F1 by default. You can also choose to use the legacy UI in the options should you desire that. There is a chat wheel as well when pressing down V and smart ping when pressing Alt. Everything is also voice acted by the hero you are playing so even if you don't pay attention to the messages you will still hear it.
There is no all chat to reduce toxicity and anyone who AFK will get kicked. Anti-toxicity measures can also be seen in the gold income mechanics and several other things as well.
As a MOBA veteran, I can enjoy this game greatly without getting bored as matches don't tend to stretch out. While the game is not perfect but it's the potential it could be.  Bring some friends and join
today. See you in the arena!

I'll keep this review pretty straight forward with a slight amount of detail. This game is amazeballs if you like games like this.. By games like this I mean very cooperative first person shooters. You MUST use teamwork or you will inevitably get owned.
Biggest pro by FARRR: the sound. I know it sounds secondary, but no joke I've never heard a game with sound like this. I went out and bought a headset (Turtle Beach Stealth 450) just to play it. If someone is shooting at me from 147 degrees behind me to the left, I can hear that $#%@... Like Daredevil. Every gun shot and exploding grenade is an ear ♥♥♥♥♥♥. Or eargasm if you will. And you will..
Pro: the teamwork. With multiple squads all coordinating attacks, it really separates itself from other games. The communication is key. You'll need to have a mic to play this game.
Pro: graphics. I have a slightly above average build and the game runs great aside from a few lower frame rates in the bigger maps. I run the game on high settings and it's smoother than stuff that's really smooth.
Pro: maps. Maps are HUGE and it really puts to shame the Battlefields and especially Counter Strikes of the world. Every map has great choke points, advantage spots, etc. Great for team play.
Pro: HUD. Practically none. I love it. Tired of playing first person shooters with so much crap on the screen that you can't see an enemy? This is as realistic of a shooter as it gets. No bs crosshairs either. All skill shots, baby. Think of Call of Duty on hardcore but better in almost every conceivable way..
And finally (the best part) PRO: no high-tech weapons, no scorestreaks. Completely tactical based squads in the most realistic of environments. There is a huge niche for this game that nobody has achieved yet. No melee attacks. Why would you? You have people bullets..
Con: only slightly buggy with the newly implemented vehicles but remember, it's still in it's infancy. That's it. That is the only con I can think of and it hardly affects your experience.
Seriously, if you like hardcore FPS's and are looking for something new to dive into, this is it my friends. At this price point just buy it. Doesn't feel alpha-ey at all.

In ages past an RPG either distinguished itself by exceptional story or by great customization. Dark Messiah of Might and Magic does neither of those very well, and I doesn't need to.
Dark Messiah's strength is in its gameplay and level-design, its freedom of choice in the completion of challenges set before you. Dark Messiah sports possibly the best melee combat in any First Person game to date and supplements it with a wide variety of environmental interaction.
Impaling your enemies on spikes, chopping their limbs off, burning them to a crisp or making them slip on ice, a smart player has full control over the battlefield. Every approach is viable, every environment suited to take on foes in different and interesting ways. You can master Archery, Melee, Stealth and Magic to become a force to be reckonned with.
Of course nothing comes without flaws and with Dark Messiah it is unfortunately the engine which often crashes or produces (often hillarious) glitches. Still, if you are looking for a game that will challenge your creativity and mastery, this game is for you.
In the realm of content the game provides around 6-8 hours of gameplay time depending on how vigorously you explore the levels and their branching paths and secrets. The story, while nothing to write home about, with a twist telegraphed from miles away, is enjoyable in a corny adventure B-Movie way. Anyone that ever took part in a pen and paper tabletop will enjoy it as a throwback. Furthermore, it never gets in the way, the cinematics are kept to a minimum and never interrupt gameplay for longer than a couple of seconds. Dark Messiah is all about good old fun through gameplay, no carrots on a stick, no grinding and no pretension to be something more than it is.
Don't be fooled, Dark Messiah of Might and Magic might be old, but it is classic worth both your time and the price of admission.

Let's get the topics I have less to say about out of the way first.
Controls:
The controls are precise, simple and feel good. In all of my time with the game I have never felt like the controls were the cause of any of my (over 8000) deaths. I have been using keyboard.
Music and sound effects:
The soundtrack is a host of remade classical pieces and as expected of Ridiculon, it is great. The sounds are also mostly very good, though some seem a bit too loud and others get annoying after a while.
Visuals:
Looks pretty good for a 2D platformer.
Story:
The story is obviously not the focus of the game. It's rather simple but it's not boring.
Gameplay:
Now for the big one.
The game is not easy. At times it is brutally difficult. However, the game is still a lot of fun and most of the time, the difficulty is fair. The main levels are generally not too frustrating. There are many little collectibles and secrets, a great amount of achievements and the number of levels the game has to offer is amazing. Beating hard challenges is satisfying and there are some optional insanely difficult ones for the hardcore players.
The game does have some flaws though:
1. It makes you replay levels multiple times if you want to collect all the collectibles. Some people may dislike this. (I personally have no problem with it)
2. A few levels contain obstacles that are unpredictable and unfair. This issue is only present in maybe about 1% of all levels though and it mostly doesn't have a high chance of killing you. But it sucks when it does.
3. If you are bad at platformers or have a short temper, this game could be incredibly frustrating for you.
Bonus:
The End is Nigh is very easily moddable and there are already a bunch of cool mods that add extra levels (check out the official discord if you wanna play them). This gives the game quite a bit more longevity. I am modding it myself and I never expected to put so many hours into a singleplayer platformer.
All in all, the game is great and I wholeheartedly recommend it.

I don't usually like puzzle games much but this is easily one of my favorite videogames I've played in years and the first in quite a long time that I've not been able to stop playing until I finished it. I'd need to give it a bit more thought but as of right now I'd easily consider this one of the best videogames ever made.
It doesn't do a lot of the things that I really dislike about puzzle games which I thought it might, it's something that has put me off of playing the game for two years despite loving Croteam. However none of the things I dislike about a lot of puzzle games are present here, it doesn't make you backtrack, it doesn't have completely obscure solutions to problems that require countless hours of trial and error. The game makes you think outside of the box but doesn't hide anything in any place that would require you to go through levels with a fine tooth comb. (Except for Easter Eggs but they're inconsequential to gameplay). It has none of these things but still manages to challenge you just enough to keep you engaged but no puzzle is so impossible you will be stuck on it for countless hours. You can also leave any puzzle you are stuck on to come back to it later at any point. This game is one of the few puzzle games I've played that strikes a beautiful balance in difficulty and has an almost perfect difficulty curve.
The graphics and performance is fantastic, the Serious Engine is great, well made and as always is full of plenty of eye candy. Which is good because all of the environments in the game are absolutely beautiful and masterfully created, this is one of the few games where I've really stopped to enjoy the view.
This is all wrapped up inside a wonderful story that is left to be pieced together by the player, it's offered to you by computer terminals with often confusing and often broken text files. (These can be fixed by means of the player outside of the game which optionally reveals even more about the world). The story of the world is intermixed with snippets of philosophy relevant to the message of the game and all of it serves to keep you motivated to learn more. I actually found myself solving puzzles sometimes simply because I wanted to learn more about the world I inhabit. I wont spoil any story details beyond any of this for the chance I might spoil it for someone reading here, but in my opinion it is one of the most fascinating plots a game has given me in sometime.
If someone asked me to prove to them videogames can be art, this is one of the games I'd show them because  this game truly is art. I cannot recommend this game enough even if you're not a huge fan of puzzle games.

RimWorld is one of those games that can treat you right one moment then sucker punch you the next - but what makes it so good for me is that it doesn't always. It has three storytellers with their own pattern, and those each have their own difficulty. If you want casual play, there's Phoebe Chillax on Basebuilder difficulty; mistakes are easy to recover from. Or you can also choose Randy Random on Extreme Permadeath for a real challenge - What happens is random and once it's done, it's done. Good luck surviving a huge raid on day 3. RimWorld gives a rather strong range of control of challenge right from the start.
The real fun is in the gameplay. You manage a colony (or a tribe) of 1-5 colonists, or pawns, and are tasked with their survival and the ultimate goal of building a ship to leave the planet. Defend them from raiders, killer robots, insect infestations, blights, eachother, and yourself. (We all get fed up with that
pawn eventually.) These pawns each have different traits, skills, and backstories that change how they function, like nudists, psychopaths, optimists, medieval lords, medieval slaves. Injuries also play a big role. A sick colonist will have to spend time in bed recovering or risk death, and a colonist can have their hand, arm, head (yikes!), organs, and more removed and that will affect them adversely. (Who needs a head anyway?) Not to mention that where you choose to build will affect growing seasons, clothes needed to survive, and diseases.
One final feature of RimWorld is the modding scene, and it is huge. A large variety of mods exist on the Steam Workshop and are a click or two away from being in your game, and even more unique mods await you in the Ludeon forums. Just like games like Skyrim, mods can make you spend yet another day managing those wacky pawns. The developer is also active and still polishing and adding more to the game, pushing it bit by bit to its final, grand form.
I didn't expect to love RimWorld as much as I did, and it was a bit of a hesitant buy. However, I fell in love with the game. I struggled to build my first functional colony. I waited on edge to see if my pawn would recover from disease. I felt unease from my first ancient danger. I swore when my pawn kept missing an easy shot. Every colony is a rollercoaster of emotions, and I love every second of it.
Still less tumors than League of Legends.

Used to use this software a couple years ago when I had an SLI setup without issue. It was handy then for keeping the clocks  and fans matched on my gpus. I had started using this again with my newer single card machine, but I've had to remove it due to several issues it has been creating. To begin, it will not allow me to change if it launches with windows, it just always opens at boot, until I used ccleaner to stop it. Upon startup or closing of the program, Logitech Options crashes every single time. I edit video and audio using Pro Tools and Adobe Premiere Pro. Everytime I get my computer under a load while editing, Precision X 16 crashes, shortly followed my audio interface drivers.
Now, my audio interface is not a cheap piece of gear, I've spent serious money putting it together, especialy on cables. Everytime that this happened, I've had to replace my ADAT cables($20 each, need 2) twice as it toasted them. This makes me really worried about the integrity of convertors in my equipment. Should a video card application cause these issues with external audio devices? I think not. I've removed from that pc, and tested my equipment on my rackmount pc. NO ISSUES on my rackmount pc which has not had Precision X 16 on it, though the video card in that one has had liquid spilled on it before(cleaned before reinstalling). I've since connected my audio setup back to the first pc w/o Precision X installed now and haven't had any issues like before, even when rendering big projects.
Not sure where the gremlins went, but I'm glad they left with removing your software. All I needed was a slight bump in clock speed and voltage to render previews slightly faster with a couple extra plugins, but not worth the trouble.
TLDR; Caused issues with unrelated hardware used for pro audio/visual applications. Cost me time and money replacing cables and slowing production. Would use again provided issues were solved, but until then I can't recomend this to anyone.

I don't want to♥♥♥♥♥♥all over a game made by a small team. God knows if I made a game it would be terrible. And this game isn't terrible. But there are an awful lot of RPGs out there, and a heck of a lot of them are from RPG Maker. Being "kind of ok I guess" isn't good enough to warrant this one above any others.
For starters, this game is really short. About 3 hours. I can deal with a short rpg if there is something compelling about it. Like, if there was a really good story, or a really unique twist, or humor, or interesting mechanics... or... anything really. The story of this game is not very interesting. The dialogue is sometimes downright awful. The unique twist is that you can change your class each time you die... but that doesn't really make a lot of difference. There aren't really any interesting mechanics. In combat you'll probably just choose whatever does the most damage until they are dead. There isn't much need for status changing stuff. And there aren't really any complex things going on. You have a wide variety of weapons you can pick from, but it doesn't matter what type they are really as long as you can equip them. Sword, gun, bow? The only thing that matters is what has the best damage. Speaking of bows, the animation for firing a bow has it aimed backwards.
There are some odd things they put into the game. For instance, when you kill an ememy instead of gaining their items they drop a sack on the ground you have to pick up. But there is no inventory limit so there is really no reason you would NOT want their items. So it is just a mechanism to make you forget things on the ground. Also, there is a crafting system which could be interesting but I found literally 4 recipes and only 1 of them was remotely useful because it made explosives you need for a side quest (you could just buy explosives though.) I could make a sword that is worst than one I found and an axe that is also worse than one I found and an hp potion which I guess I could use but I found so many just by opening chests and stuff. Also there is a fishing mechanic. You use it once in the very beginning of the game to do some quests for a chef that are really unnecessary. Then you never fish again.
The characters are.... There. There is no real development. There is a bunny girl, for... reasons, and 2 mercanaries (one is a mercanary class and one is not but you pay the one taht is not to fight for you, thus he is indeed a mercanary) They have no character. They are just present to help you do more damage. I don't know if you can find any other characters, I was going to find out on a new game+. I succeeded in preventing the bunny girl from joining my group but I got bored before seeing if there was any one different I could get. Not that it really matters, as again they are just there to do more damage and have no personalities or input or anything.
I wanted to like this game... And I didn't hate it. I mean it is competant if short, but there are other games for similiar prices that are better. The Zeboyd games Breath of Death and Cthulhu Saves the World come to mind. Both are short simple RPGS with humorous premises, clever writing, and refined battle systems that are pretty interesting. This game, however, doesn't have a whole lot to offer besides just being OK. OK is fine I guess, but I can't recommend a game that is merely ok.

Cart racers are so rare on the PC, so the fact that this one not only exists for the platform but is also excellent is just wonderful. Powerups are perhaps a bit narrow in variety, but none of them trigger the bullshait alarm like Mario Kart's blue shells, stars, or chomp chains.
The transformation mechanic produces a great variety in tracks, many of them changing partway through to introduce new vehicle modes. Power slides and stunt boosts give a huge amount of depth to learning the tracks as you find just how many spins you can squeeze out on a jump or how to chain your power slides.
Heck, it even has more exclusive characters than the console versions: "Team Fortress", "General Winter" (Soviet commander from CoH2), Shogun from Total War, and Football Manager (yeah, the dude in the suit from Football Manager).
Local 4 player co-op too, almost unheard of on PCs.

Dark Messiah of Might & Magic is the epitome of what underrated games are. Arkane Studios did a fantastic job creating this game where you can choose between play styles such as mage, warrior, rogue, archer, and class combinations (archer+rogue or mage+rogue) depending on what talents you choose.
The overall story of DM is rather unique and is exactly what a fantasy story is meant to be with backstabs included for half-price and even cheesy romance. Many of the situations that the story will place you in are smoothly transitioned and are an absolute blast to play in. For example, in one level you awaken to soldiers invading your dwelling and kill the housekeeper who comes to warn you of the danger. This immediately puts you in a state of alert to fight for your life. That scenario is all done perfectly whilst blended with narrative that exquisitely blends what people want in gameplay with storytelling.
Combat within DM is fun, what more can be said? Kicking. I could say kicking. But yes the kicking element of DM is absolutely amazing where you'll boot orcs off bridges miles in the air, sending them plummeting to their doom. The game could even teach TES game a thing or two about swordplay where you have to swing your blade PAST their guard. And while it'll be easy at first, it'll intensify against enemies that are far better at blocking and attacking. Magic is a fresh step in the right direction and it all feels right. Magicking and shooting a massive fireball feels good and so does zapping humans with lightning bolts. Likewise every other combat option is just as satisfying (such as bow&arrow where you have to aim a little above your target to get the bolt to aim true, also staves)
The graphics have aged quite well for this game and I've nothing bad to say of the soundtrack (or good in that matter).
Sadly the largest fault of the game has to be the lack of AI smarts in your oppnents AT TIMES. I think Arkane Studios did a great job at creating good AI, but if you happen to swing a large chandelier back and forth, you'll find enemies constantly killing themselves over jumping into an obvious death machine. I'd hope most people would agree that it's hard (if not impossible) to have designed an enemy AI over whatever is happening in the environment at the time of the game's creation.
I'd heavily recommend this game to anyone who hasn't played this, it's enormous fun for the first run or two through.

Game is a solid 8/10
+Crafting is unique, offers flexibility and replayability to the heroes
**NOTE: Negative reviews seem to have in common that this is a "pay to win" feature. Instead of buying the "forever" recipe, buy 1 day versions of recipes, if you're the kind of person who likes to make/mod many items (I know I am)
+Beautiful graphics with some nice Dx11 features
+Power is an awesome concept, and what sets it apart from LoL is that it applies to many effects and spells, including those of items!
+So much helpful info in the interface, you can gauge hero's power very well and quickly, even in the heat of battle
+The towers in the jungle are clever itterations of wards from other AoS games
+The game's name Strife is elegent, and harkens back to the roots of the genre; Aeon of Strife
+Two separate lane pushing bosses offers a lot to the game
+Heroes are added often and regularly. This is an S2 game, and much like HoN you are going to see active development of heroes, much faster than 1 every month/3/5 months or whatever it takes for HotS or LoL, or close to never as seen in DotA 2 (there's still more heroes in DotA 1 ....)
+In comparison to other games in the same genre, they try hard to make the heroes distinguishable from LoL or DotA heroes
+Pets offer more diversity to play types and characters
-I've had problems using the Steam overlay in-game, it usually doesnt go away after I bring it up. I'll make sure to report that as a bug
-The pets are costly in terms of games played, and there's nothing else to spend seals on once you get all the pets. And as far as I know, you can't rent the pets like you can heroes and item recipes
-The loading screen seems completely independent of your computer specs, game your playing, or how many apps your running, and I mean this in terms of bandwidth, because one game might load very fast for me, another i may be last, and you can't tell how far other players are loaded from the loading screen, which I've always liked about other games.
-There's no unconcious reward-feedback from buying items, gaining levels, or kills (other than multi-kills, which I really liked). For example, half the time I don't notice that I've leveled, because no sound plays. Some kills, I don't know that I got until I look at the indicator on the side of the screen (in DotA, Infinite Crisis, Heroes of the Storm, the heroes talk♥♥♥♥♥♥to each other) and as for items, you might buy something without knowing it because you clicked on the side of the screen, hit a hotkey unknowingly, etc and without the cha-ching of a purchase you might be too late to sell it, if that makes sense. Although, the last-hit gold gain sound plays, which is nice. I just rather play music in the background than listen to in-game music, which is a bad thing. I'd just like to see more hero dialog.
-I would like to see more enchantments for all the recipes! It's so fun to craft and granted there are 2-3 per item, there always seems to be more general ones (% damage to AI) versus item-specific ones (reduces charges needed for chain lightning by 1), and those are the ones I really like to play around with!
Overall fantastic, and can combat with the more well known games in the same genre. People don't like change, so you will still see a slim community here but over time it will come. Some needed improvements but the game is still Early Access so be looking forward to that!

I don't usually like puzzle games much but this is easily one of my favorite videogames I've played in years and the first in quite a long time that I've not been able to stop playing until I finished it. I'd need to give it a bit more thought but as of right now I'd easily consider this one of the best videogames ever made.
It doesn't do a lot of the things that I really dislike about puzzle games which I thought it might, it's something that has put me off of playing the game for two years despite loving Croteam. However none of the things I dislike about a lot of puzzle games are present here, it doesn't make you backtrack, it doesn't have completely obscure solutions to problems that require countless hours of trial and error. The game makes you think outside of the box but doesn't hide anything in any place that would require you to go through levels with a fine tooth comb. (Except for Easter Eggs but they're inconsequential to gameplay). It has none of these things but still manages to challenge you just enough to keep you engaged but no puzzle is so impossible you will be stuck on it for countless hours. You can also leave any puzzle you are stuck on to come back to it later at any point. This game is one of the few puzzle games I've played that strikes a beautiful balance in difficulty and has an almost perfect difficulty curve.
The graphics and performance is fantastic, the Serious Engine is great, well made and as always is full of plenty of eye candy. Which is good because all of the environments in the game are absolutely beautiful and masterfully created, this is one of the few games where I've really stopped to enjoy the view.
This is all wrapped up inside a wonderful story that is left to be pieced together by the player, it's offered to you by computer terminals with often confusing and often broken text files. (These can be fixed by means of the player outside of the game which optionally reveals even more about the world). The story of the world is intermixed with snippets of philosophy relevant to the message of the game and all of it serves to keep you motivated to learn more. I actually found myself solving puzzles sometimes simply because I wanted to learn more about the world I inhabit. I wont spoil any story details beyond any of this for the chance I might spoil it for someone reading here, but in my opinion it is one of the most fascinating plots a game has given me in sometime.
If someone asked me to prove to them videogames can be art, this is one of the games I'd show them because  this game truly is art. I cannot recommend this game enough even if you're not a huge fan of puzzle games.

Today I finally completed this game. I've had a love-hate relationship with this game over the past year or so. I do like puzzles and I do like the fragmented AI and philosophy themed storyline, however because of getting stuck from time to time and the story being more confrontational than satisfactory, I left the game several times, coming back later motivated more by the urge to finally complete it than to have fun playing it.
The contradictions for me are: the puzzles are fun, but become a chore in wanting to see more of the storyline. On the other hand the storyline intervenes with the puzzling experience, because of the terminals and recordings that you find. I found several times that I wanted to get on with the puzzles, but leaving bits of story behind also doesn't feel right.
In short the game is a mix of puzzles and a story you have to build yourself from little pieces. That's great, but the game does, in my opinion, not the best job in combining them in a seamless way.
Nevertheless, both the puzzle and story part are great. Some puzzles are quite challenging but doable (I think I looked at a walkthrough twice). The story consists largely of philosophical and existential dialogue and texts, something I personally find very compelling. It is a lot of buildup that lets you guess at who you are in the game and in real life and the finale is not very surprising but still executed well in its modesty.
In short, a much recommended game for fans of puzzles, finding out a story and philosophical content.
Pros
+ Challenging puzzles
+ Philosophy
+ Question your own existence and purpose
+ Compelling story
Cons
- Story and puzzling mix does not always feel seamless
- At times for me the fun was gone because of getting stuck and/or confronting philosophical content

Amazing game. Extremely hard, and extremely challenging, but extremely fun. I actually don't get angry at all while playing this game, because each time I die I just see room for me to do it again. While I'm around 3.5k deaths already and am still early on the game, gotta say, it's a blast to play and a♥♥♥♥♥♥ton of fun.
Looking for secrets is also very amusing, some of them are extremely well hidden, requiring you to backtrack in order to find the entrance to them.
The game pretty much forces you to die a bunch of times to learn and improve quickly, as each level is relatively small and easy to master (aside from a few special levels, which take a little more patience and skill to do). In other words: Stop Raging and Git Gud, the game.
As for how this game stands along other Edmund games, I'd say it's pretty equal. If you compare it to SMB, the game is almost a polar opposite of sorts, being more calculated, precise and time-taking, rather than a level where speed and skill is what matters most.
There are some really unfair levels for more unskilled players though. On a certain level, I probably died at least 1000 times in 2 screens. Granted I'm not amazing at platformers, it took me a while to be able to be able to do a small portion of it consistently, and a good while to finish said level.
Regarding controls, I wish they were a little better for Mouse and Keyboard users. The game is very unforgiving to M&K, for the fact that it's hard to control your speed, since if you don't have a mechanical Keyboard you can't slightly tilt the key, and jumping turns into a bit of a nightmare, since this game has that one mechanic where the longer you hold the jump button, the farther you jump, which isn't necessarily easy to gauge when you're playing on a keyboard and pressing the jump key a lot. TL;DR, the game kind of has a big favoritism for controllers.
The soundtrack is also very fitting for the game. It just gives just the correct platformer vibe, taking the setting of the game in consideration.
I definetely recommend this game, 100%. If you like Edmund's other game and challenge, this game is for you, my friend.

Opposing Force shouldn't be held on a pedestal the way Half-Life is, simply because Gearbox (the developers of this one) stood on Half-Life's already established shoulders in order to reach even higher. It's hard to deny though that Opposing Force is more consistently fun than Half-Life is, and doesn't have Half-Life's low points, like "On a Rail". Xen makes several reappearances, but it's only used sparingly for effect, which is how you do Xen properly. Awkward platforming sections are kept to a minimum. The new weapons are super fun, the new enemies are creepy in all the right ways, and the level design is top notch. You can tell they were full of ideas for this game, and there are quite a few new features and concepts crammed into the game's comparitively short playtime.
It doesn't quite have Half-Life's level of polish, and it lacks a certain subtlety that Half-Life had, but it's a great game absolutely worthy of the name.

As of the time of writing this review, the price was 300MXN~15USD.
"Talos" is a puzzle game where you collect Tetris figures in order to open next levels. Each figure requires you to solve a puzzle. And each puzzle may use different tools (that are progressively available). I have found so far that there is rarely more than one possible solution. And it's also worth noting that there are undeniable similarities to Portal 2; however the scenarios and music are completely different, and the approach is definitely less "funny-adventuresque" and more "philosophical-post human". Now Pros and Cons:
Pros
-Very good balance between challenge and reward (I have not been frustrated so far, but many puzzles have been far from easy to solve). Moreover, it is possible to request hints to solve the puzzle; which I guess would get rid of frustration. Some of the puzzles are clearly easier than others; so you won't need to use the hints all the time either.
-Beautiful scenarios. So far, There are greek-like scenarios, egyptian-like scenarios, medieval-like scenarios, and syberia-like scenarios (just snow everywhere and a few mountains in the horizon (you cannot walk to far away from the puzzles area).
-Slightly interesting "plot" around existencial questions.
Cons
- The only con, but a huge one, that I have found so far, is that the graphic engine is terrible for handling quick side rotations. You will briefly see some artifacts (that are not part of the game, which sometimes introduces nice artifacts for a purpose) before the actual frame appears. And this has nothing to do with the graphics settings!!!! I have used every possibilities, which are a lot by the way, and I always keep having the same problem. It may be my computer but I severely doubt it: it is the only game I've had this issues with, and my rig is a Sandy Bridge 2700 running at more than 3.4Ghz with 16 GB Ram and two GTX780Ti running in SLI (which is close to the performance of one GTX970).
Final Opinion:
I recently finished the game and I'm very happy with my purchase. But at the current price, I'd be unsure. It'll depend on how much you like puzzle-games and if there are others that you think are better than this one out there.

This review is from the perspective of one who has not played a previous game in the Worms franchise.
Worms, a simple concept- Groups of worms fight to the death in enviornments ranging from simple to complex,  littered with explosive barrels, guns, toxic gas, testing tubes with eyeballs inside, and many other borderline ridiculous items.
Rather simple, yes? Now add some nice physics to it, and add some items, for example perhaps..Bazookas, grenades, dynamite, flamethrowers, sentry guns, water pistols, air strikes, as well as your own grandmother. That last one is a stinker.
Imagine a worm gracefully flying through the air after getting hit by dynamite, followed by said worm landing on a landmine, flying into a small pit with a sentry gun and being shot into the air moments after. Seconds later, the worm has fallen into the water and met his demise. How unfortunate.
Unlikely, yes? Mostly, but not entirely. Now imagine hitting worms off of an edge with a baseball bat, or simply prodding the worm the minimum distance to make him fall to his death, an insult to injury. Throwing an angry buffalo at a group of worms as it literally explodes them 6 feet into the ground. Throwing the holy hand grenade to launch a worm into the sky, dropping dynamite from your jetpack as you fly away from your helpless foes, poisioning multiple worms from a distance to cause damage over time, and even beginning the event that put an end to the dinosaurs. Meteors, explosions, the map becomes swiss cheese. Many casualties ensue-if not becoming a mass-homocide-suicide mix that turns into a draw.
Only one problem, chances are that you're only going to experience this sweet action if you've got some buddies to play the game with, so you're going to have to convince your friends to buy the game if they don't have it already. The single player in this game isn't bad but it can be rather unfair and overall is only for unlocking additional worms, which isn't 100% neccessary.
So forget about the single player and just focus on the multiplayer. Get some friends and cause some explosions, because this game is a lot of fun.

Just got this game...
And because of the mixed reviews, I'd thought I would leave this review in favor of the developers.
At first, it looked a "little dark" but the art was amazing and what really turned me on to it was it's "Inception-like" concept of going deeper and deeper into someone's dreams.
So--the plot begins when a giant hole in the ground opens up to reveal a deep cave termed "the abyss," someplace in Chile. This "abyss" releases these imaginary monsters that the soldiers (or the people for that matter) can't handle or hope to fight against.
This is where you, the player, comes in, as the hero Katrien, an unexplainably attractive swordswoman with a strong will, long red-hair (maybe that explains it) and a mission to stop this horrifying but random event from continuing.
The intriguing part of this plot is the fact that every being ascending from the abyss, the main character Katrien, as well as the abyss itself are all just products of the dreams, thoughts, and memories of a supposed "sleeping warlock" who lies underground, at the bottom of the abyss.
And this is where the plot itself runs hand-in-hand with the rogue-like gameplay of this title.
Because everything is IMAGINERY --
When your character dies (and the soldier that tries to revive your character), you just spawn back to the beginning to try again and again--retaining only your level and gold with each playthrough. On top of that, things that don't exist pop up and beat you in ways that don't quite make sense sometimes (either that or it can be credited to a lack of skill either way--it sucks dying).
Because everything is a DREAM --
The dungeons are procedurally generated--which translates to the abyss appearing differently each time you venture into it. Furthermore, it's not just the scenery that changes, but the pathways that you take, as well as the difficulty of each section of the dungeon changes as well--just like a dream would. It's also good to note that the variations of the abyss don't always appear to be inside of a cave--this makes for some pretty interesting visuals during each trek.
The combat system is NOT a "clone" of Super Smash Bros. (despite some negatively making a comparison of the two games) but being a Super Smash Bros. fan myself--I could definitely see how the developers were influenced and inspired by the title's combat. The characters controls are similar which makes for simple but strategic battles. One thing that you'll notice when first starting is that the controls seem extremely stiff--but after playing and getting the hang of it--you'll soon realize that they're not REALLY stiff but that they are actually extremely tight.
Now, there are a couple of things I don't want to leave without mentioning--
One--is the fact that Katrien isn't the only playable character in the game. There are 2 other main characters that are unlockable in the game--The Ghost Monk (which you will probably unlock first) and Pincoya. On top of that, when your character's mana bar fills up, you're able to (sort of) "capture" pretty much anything you face in the abyss so that you can become whatever it is you want (insert pause). And of course, I can't forget to mention the weak and clunky soldier guy that you have to control after dying with your main character--it sucks but really it's just best to think of him as a "place-holder to a second chance shot at going further."
On top of that--I want to mention the artstyle of the game. This game is beautiful. It's like turning a museum into your playground and because of this artstyle--I can't help but say that this game is like staring at your most horrid nightmares and falling in love with them all at the same time.
And no matter what, every time you head into the abyss for another playthrough, there's always this sense of adventure that takes hold because the game is so well designed in the way of making you, as the player, feel as if you really don't know what to expect once you're in there.
This game is unique and honestly, my playthrough(s) of this game has really brought me back to the time I first played the Vanillaware title "Muramasa" on the Wii and that's a REALLY good thing.
I wanna see more games like this.

In Memories of a Vagabond you're an hero given the chance to reincarnate in different bodies to carry out his vengeance after a demon took away your girlfriend and killed you: said bodies act as classes and you can freely switch between them (whenever you die or reach a certain location) during your journey,
While the premise is very interesting and the actual game is decent enough for an RPGMaker title it sadly suffers from terrible writing, basic gameplay and some balance problems.
-great soundtrack
-a few dialogue lines were actually funny
-a good amount of different items to equip
-the game as a whole works and is decent enough
-very basic combat
-shallow, cliched story
-childish dialogues
-dull quests
-Steam overlay doesn't work with the game
-some balance problems
-tutorials don't explain how certain things work (like having to travel the map to find where dead party members end up for you to resurrect)
-very short at 2/3 hours
My two hours with Memories of a Vagabond were actually decent as, all things considered, the gameplay is bearable, there's no glaring bugs and its short length at least ensures the game doesn't overstay its welcome.
Sadly for an RPG its story is terribly, terribly weak....not only it's basically one cliche after the other but the actual narrative is amateurish with short, shallow dialogues that are dull at best: the fact the game also sports a good amount of broken English and typos only makes things worse.
The combat also suffers from some balance problems as enemies can easily hit your party for half your HPs even on Normal and with decent equipment: this means you'll have to often stop attacking to cast heal spells on all your party or have to spend consumables to resurrect them once they hit the floor. I also had a feeling some of the classes were definitely worse than others.
There's some attempts to add other features, like housing and crafting, but they are pretty useless and feel like an afterthought at best. Memories of A vagabond isn't horrible, and might even be worth a shot if you find it in a bundle and want a quick RPG fix, but it simply fails at too many things for me to recommend.

"What if...?" I think this one of the most profound and fundamentally human of all questions. The ability to build scenarios in our minds may very well be unique to the human animal as it serves no real purpose for other species due to their more instinctual lives. But for humans "What if.." can be everything from the root cause of crippling fear or a source of great amusement. A few games over the years have had "What if.." as their core gameplay mechanic and I'm not just talking about sandboxes. RPGs, FPS, Racing and many other types of games have given players the licence for creative exploration and you can easily say that as the potential for "What If.." to spawn ideas and possibilities has been largely associated with how enjoyable the game itself is. Minecraft, Spore, Fallout and now Robocraft are all big "what if.." games.
But for a moment, let's shelve that thought and address the elephant in the room. Take a look at the negative reviews of Robocraft on steam and you'll see a consistant pattern. Most are players from alpha and many claim that the game is now Pay-2-Win. With regards to how the game used to play, let's ask the fair question - is it fun now even if it is different? The simple answer is yes, Robocraft is currently a ton of fun and if you never played the alpha builds you'll never miss it.
Next the other hot topic. Is it Pay-2-Win? Well, let us just clarify that because there is sometimes a matter of opinion on what it means. Does P2W mean that someone can buy an advantage for real cash that is unavailable for free? Or does P2W mean that someone can pour cash into a game to gain a huge lead over players who do not? Well, regardless of which perspective you prefer the fact is that neither of these apply to Robocraft. Nobody can purchase anything that isn't available for free and secondly, even if someone purchases a ton of crates and gets some insanely good rolls the fact is that rare, epic and legendary items are not innately better than common or uncommon hardware. This is all due to weight limitations, issues with centre of gravity, CPU consumption and a myriad of other limitations you need to work around when building bots. Allow me to briefly illustrate.
I've never put any cash into this game and I have plenty of epic and even one legendary weapon. Needless to say that I'd love to use my mini-gun shredder but the fact is that it is too heavy to create an especially agile bot and its CPU consumption is very high so any bot with it is now limited in size, protection and other types of hardware. Furthermore, it is a big bulky part of the bot that smart players focus their fire on to blow off my bot long before it can deal enough damage to them in return. In fact, you get more functionality and firepower from a small assortment of uncommon plasma cannons than you do from this one legendary weapon. In short, rarity does not mean better - it means different. And that is why Robocraft is far from P2W.
Moving on, a related note. Robocraft is in beta. But it is not a buggy beta. In fact it is very stable, offers a wide variety of gameplay modes and can keep you occupied for absolutely hours. However, that said, it has balance issues. In a game like this where you build your bots from scratch you have the potential to totally gimp yourself if you're not careful but further to that there are certain peices of hardware which are just overpowered or underpowered and the logic behind the balance is just flawed at times. I won't go into details as it isn't a widespread issue but there are a couple items which stand out as needing some serious scrutiny.
Finally, there is the community and the matchmaking system. It's a good sized community; Steam stats indicate that there are between 4000-8000 users online at any one time and since the game runs on dedicated servers you know that these are all players and not just private servers sitting online. The population has been very stable for over a year now with a bit of drop off recently from a steady 10k to 5k concurrent users but this is going all the way back to 2014 so you can expect the 'oh shiny!' phase to be officially over now. The matchmaking is done based upon 5v5 teams so the fact is that it is very well balanced in terms of player experience. Once you join a queue the wait is normally 1-2 mins which is about as quick as the waiting times in Rocket League despite it having a far larger community. However, what is abundently clear is that this is (much like Rocket League) a team-based game and if you have one team playing like it's solo deathmatch while the other team staying close and working together then the disorganized team is going to be steam-rolled. If you're an experienced player on a disorganized team then it can be frustrating but this is the fault of the gamers and not the game. In general though I've seen this matchmaking system produce 5v5 matches that are frequently very well balanced. It is rare to not see games end with scores like 84% to 100% or 98% to 100%. The fact that so many matches end with such a narrow victory says volumes for how well designed the matchmaking is.
All in all, Robocraft is a great game with a solid community and a great future as long as the devs continue to work on balance and frequent content updates.

Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed is a damn fine kart racing game and definitely one of the best ones to come out. The controls are really good, the characters feel different from each other, there's little to no rubberbanding and the game feels like it offers enough event variety and reasons to keep playing. The music is also really good here. The weapon selection is also pretty good. There is no blue shell or warp orb equivalent in this game that would discourage the players from keeping the first place too long.
The developer SUMO Digital really knew how to make a solid kart game. The tracks are well made, they play different and you really need to learn how to drift and boost to win in this game. Not knowing this some go online saying that the game is way too hard way too early. This is only true because the didn't learn the controls. Although the game does play faster than your average kart game because after all it does star Sonic. The game doesn't really get hard until later on when you start going for those expert rankings or if you plan to 100% the game. That's when the game really expects perfection from the player.
Now on the down side the roster could've used some work. I actually wish this game could've been called Sega All-Stars rather than Sonic & All-Stars. The PC version has 27 characters with seven of them being from Sonic and the rest being from other Sega titles with a few exceptions. To me characters like Amy, Shadow and Knuckles felt like a bit too much of the same thing. Also there a few odd and out of place characters like Dana Patrick and Ralph. Also Ralph is really annoying with his lines in this game. Instead of the ones I mentioned I would've like to have seen characters like Billy Hatcher, Ryo Hazuki and Akira Yuki who are featured here, but aren't playable. Also it's a bit weird for an OutRun course to be DLC in a racing game. Not only that but the track is really underwhelming and you can't play it online. Other tracks do a lot better with their source material.
But biggest problem with this game is how long it takes to start, end or restart anything. It's how the menus are made. It takes them too long to animate and you can't use them until the animation is finished. With a game as hard and fast paced as this being able to quickly restart a race should be a given. Also the announcer really shouldn't talk as much as he does in the menus. Also you can't leave the game open in a menu screen because every 30 seconds the announcer tells you to do something.
But look past all the nitpicks you have the best kart game this generation.

Sonic and All-Stars Racing Transformed is a really good game. This is a sequel to the game titled, Sonic and Sega All-Stars Racing. You might think that it is just a Mario Kart clone with Sonic face on it but in actuallity, it is a really solid kart racer. I might say it is better than Mario Kart in some aspects.
However, the main mechanic of this game is the ability to change from a Boat, Car and Plane while on the race track. It may sound like a hassle in changing different gamestyle while playing however the changing of playstyle is natural and fun. Each of the game style have their own sets of physics and rules and controlling each vehicle is comfortable. Though try and play this with a gaming controller if possible and trying to press each button in a racing game will get uncomfortable fast.
The Aesthetics and the amount of references to Sega history will make long time Sega fans giddy. Having characters such as NiGHTS and Beat from Jet Set Radio racing through the Carrier Zone from AfterBurner is just beaurtiful. Also the remixed tracks is just delicious.
Onto the items. In Kart Racers, there is always that item which punishes the players just for being in First Place. However, in Sonic All- Star Racing Transformed the items are well balanced and not cheap. You have to actually aim the item for it to hit and even with the All Star Moves, it doesnt guarantee first place. So you got to aim your shots right to win in first place.
However, a criticsm I want to make is the way to unlock characters. In the previous installment, you have the ability to earn Sega Miles in which you can buy using in-game currency for the characters so you can essentially save to get that specific character. However, in this game, you are forced to go in the Career mode to get some of the characers unlock. You have to get to that tier while also reaching a certain threshold in the number of stars. meaning you have to play the certain mission in a harder difficulty. P.S. The S Ranks are brutal and can only be unlocked when you again reach a certain tier.
Overall, this game is just fantastic. If you want to play a good and fun Kart racer but you dont have access to Mario Kart, look no further as Sonic All Stars Racing Transformed got you covered.

Initially, I find Strife's ideas and execution to be refreshing.
1> the community is for the most part awesome.
2>  The controls and latency are tight and responsive.. In 20 games now I've had 0 problems with ping or the servers.
3> Every point of spell power also adds to attack power (balancing different types of character and opening up a slew of potentially devastating custom builds)
4> You can prearrange your list of items to buy and skills to purchase, autoleveling or not as you please.
5>  Last hitting shares the gold with every teammate in the lane (at a respectably high percentage ...35g on one minion solo or 15g on the same minion with 5 players nearby)
6> The jungle is there, yet doesn't offer much by the way of outleveling lanes, so choosing the path doesn't give you any major advantages. (This opens the meta to where any combination can do okay, including ones without a jungler.)
... I could keep this list going for a long while.. but I'll stop at saying that the developers of Strife have listened to players and watched the evolution of MOBAs very carefully, and this game feels like their scientific child of love.
Try it out! (unless you're a horrible person, in which case I suggest you go back to DOTA2)

Oxenfree provides a casual setting which turns into an not-so-casual adventure.
Let it be said that the game is not a hard one to play but a difficult one. What I mean by that is that it is not challenging your skills in any particular field. The difficulty stems from the limited time you have to reply and perform tasks - which for this type of narrative-driven game is the way it should be!
Every dialogue seems to matter and even minor trivia facts that you find along the way might be important later on in the story.
It is a satisfying uncertanty throughout various stages of the story to be left asking yourself : "What if..." ... "What if I replied differently?" ... "What if decided to go to the other place first?" ... etc.
Critique:
The writing - while surprisingly funny, sarcastic and down-to-earth - seems to lack a sense of drama. Without spoilering anything...No relatable person would react as calm and collected as the characters in this game if confronted with a similar situation. The voice actors do a great job but some dialogues seem inadequately unrealistic for certain situations.
Furthermore walking around the island is not as enjoyable as it could be. The visuals are kept in a unique style which adds to the flaire of the island and the music is also fantastic! However the non-challenging walking/climbing gets a bit dull since there is no option for example to start random dialogues with the other characters.
Verdict:
I found my time in the game to be enjoyable and I will play it again just to see what other choices can be made by playing differently.
If you enjoy games with a compelling story and you are okay with walking around a bit then this might very well be a good choice for you.

There’s an old school vibe to this game as well. You will use an analog radio to hone in on the supernatural and other anomalies. VHS type effects also occur when you are in a parallel world situation. It’s done very well.
I’ll admit I was a bit confused on the story when I first started. I had to start over several times to get myself hooked on what it is we were doing. Not a negative, but it was odd so I wanted to note it.
The characters are fleshed out nicely and can easily be remembered. They are relatable and you’ll more than likely find yourself favoring a character or two.
There’s a small amount of collectibles you can go for. Letters and anomalies. With a little patience walking around the different areas, you’ll easily be able to collect everything. The letters do explain more about the story, so it was neat to read those.
The graphics and art style are also well done. Very crisp at 1440p. The art style fit the whole vibe of the game perfectly.
Voice acting is a very strong point. I found each character delivering their lines genuinely and like a normal conversation.
Make your first playthrough your own. Don’t read any guides or try to focus on achievements.
One great addition is New Game +, or continuing the timeline. You play the same story over again, but still retain knowledge of your first playthrough. Dialog, dialog choices and some situations are different. It does give the game a fresh feel and is a really cool thing for the devs to add. I actually ended up playing the game 3 times. First was my own playthrough. Second was having Alex be a jerk to everyone. Third was simply not talking at all. This last playthrough was surprisingly fun in seeing how the characters interacted with each other without any input from me.
+60fps
+Great story
+Fantastic voice acting
+NG+ for replayability
+Art style
+Creepy/eerie vibe
+More specific counter or tracking for collectibles
+Characters can be long winded at times
+Traveling across the map seemed a little slow

It's a competitive, multiplayer, class-based first person shooter.  Each of the four classes has four or more heroes with their own abilities.  The balance is such that there are no real hard-counters (a game mechanic I absolutely despise in shooters, looking at you Overwatch) and skill matters more than class in combat engangements.
You select 3 heroes before the match starts, and equip a loadout per selected hero.  Once the match starts, you can only switch between the three heroes you picked.
Loadouts consist of a different mix of primary weapon, secondary weapon, melee weapon and 0-3 bonuses.  These bonuses that allow reloading while sprinting, faster cool-downs for support skills, etc.  Default loadouts have no bonuses.  You always have access to the default loadouts.  Loadouts that have bonuses come in three rarities, with the first tier having only 1 bonus, the second having 2 bonuses, and the rest of the tiers having 3 bonuses.  The difference between tier 3 and up is simply cosmetic.  This means gameplay-wise you only ever need tier 3 loadouts (copper rarity loadout cards).
The free-to-play aspect comes from obtaining heroes and loadouts.
A few heroes are free at any given moment with a weekly rotation of 3 heroes, but permanent access to a hero requires that you buy them through in-game currency or with real money.  With hero prices going up to 30,000 and even 50,000 in-game currency and 10 hours of constant gaming getting you around 10,000 in-game currency, it will take a fairly long time to buy heroes using in-game currency alone.
Do you need access to all the heroes to have fun?  No.  If you want to unlock 3 heroes ( as mentioned before, you can only bring a maximum of 3 heroes into a match) which fit your playstyle you can do so in the first 20-30 hours of play, and be happy.  I bought 2 heroes with in-game currency (and stayed with 1 of the default heroes), and was happy for my first 80 hours of play.  The default heroes are very good (even better than some of the non-default IMHO) but the heroes are fairly well balanced as of now.  Every newly introduced hero is usually very strong and sees some kind of small nerf though.
Loadouts are obtained by purchasing them directly for around 18,000 in-game currency, or for around $0.80 USD.  This lets you choose the exact loadout you want, and these are usually tier 3 (copper).  Alternatively, you can get them through crates that have a random drop chance of loadouts for any hero, at any rarity (including heroes you don't have, though you can use those when that hero is in free rotation).  Crates are dropped when you level up your account, and for daily login bonuses.  Loadouts you don't want can be deconstructed for parts which can then be used to craft loadouts for specific heroes.  Overall, it doesn't take much time or effort (maybe 5-10 hours, depending on if you want to buy direcly or to take a chance on crates) to get a tier 3 loadout for the hero you want.
Loadouts also affect cosmetics.  Overall, the skins aren't really all that different from each other regardless of rarity so any tier higher than tier 3 doesn't really matter.  This could change in the future though.
If you are dedicated and REALLY don't want to spend any cash, you can do that and have quite a lot of fun. I did that for the first 60 hours I played.  The different heroes are pretty well balanced and though the loadout bonuses can be very impactful to gameplay, tier 3 loadouts for your hero of choice can be obtained fairly quickly.
However, as a gamer who doesn't really like F2P systems, I prefer to spend around 15-60 USD and never really spend any more.  That is, I like treating F2P games that I find fun as $15, $30 or $60 games. Dirty Bomb lets you do that as the game isn't completely reliant on constantly having to purchase more and more stuff with real money.  If you want to do what I did, my suggestion is to purchase one of the hero bundles offered and to not sweat the loadouts as tier 3 loadouts are all you need for max bonuses and they're fairly easy to come by.
The gameplay consists of objective-based rounds with usually 3 different defence/attack objectives per round.  The round ends when the time runs out or all 3 objectives are completed by the attackers.  Some modes have only 1 round, other have more.  The maps are fairly well-designed and have opportunities for different classes to shine by interacting with different objectives and side-objectives to open up or close parts of the map, or by keeping the team in the fight, or even by simply killing the opposition.  The game is worth a try and I say it's worth buying the different hero bundles offered, but it isn't needed.

This is one of those games that my mind drifts back to repeatedly.  At its core it's "just" a puzzle game.  But something about the worlds they're set in gives the game a weighty and sardonic sense of place.  It's solitary, lonely, forgotton, and yet majestic in its decay.
Back to the game play, like most good puzzle games, there's a basic vocabulary of pieces that you employ to solve your predicaments.  You start off simple, and more pieces and complexity are added as you go along.  A couple puzzles are nigh impossible unless you happen to "get it", and there are a LOT of hidden easter eggs.  But the pysicality of the puzzles make it really interesting, and the backstory helps weave it all together.  Also, visually it's beautiful.
(Thematically, It's also a great companion piece to SOMA)

Disclaimer: I DO recommend the use of this app (for fan control only!), just NOT ON STEAM. Get it from EVGA's website.
PROS:
- Gives you full control over your GPU.
CONS:
- Gives you full control over your GPU.
- Sets your status to "In-app: EVGA Precision X" forever while you have it in the background even when play a game. Can mess with game invites and matchmaking through Steam.
SHORT SUMMARY:
using the app to control your automatic fan curve to keep your GPU cool. (If your GPU is anything like mine, it waits until the nuclear holocaust to turn on the fan at all.) My "recommendation" is set to NO in this review because there is no point to using this app *on Steam*. Just download the app from EVGA's website. The Steam version overrides your "In-Game:" status by maintaining "In-App: Evga Precision X" while it's in the background, which messes with Steam matchmaking.
OTHER COMMENTS:
I would recommend avoiding overclocking (DON'T PLAY WITH THE SHINY BUTTONS) since overclocking often damages your hardware (SETS YOUR COMPUTER ON FIRE) in exchange for a *chance* at a small performance gain (60FPS -> 61FPS). You'll spend more money buying replacement card(s) for the one(s) you break overclocking than you would spend just buying a card with higher performance in the first place.
If you download this, I hope you know what you're doing, or you'll end up like the schmucks in most of the other reviews. Also: achievements? Why EVGA?

I could easily write a lengthy essay about this game, but I will try to be concise.
The visual environment is vibrant and immersive in a way that one does not expect in this genre. Visit locations themed after great historical epochs like ancient Greece, Egypt, and medieval Europe, and take in beautiful natural, heavenly places. A perfect way to take a break from solving the challenging puzzles.
The plot of the game has more to it than what appears on the surface- the puzzles are unusual and challenging, but beyond the puzzles themselves lies a greater mystery.
The juxtaposition of logical problem solving and abstract thought that the game calls for is quite unique and very stimulating- mature players with an IQ north of 110 will find it exceptionally satisfying.
I believe that Talos Principle is worthy to be called an achievement in gaming history, and there are few games like it. If you are bored of predictable and cliched gaming experiences, and have a little bit of patience, this will be a great addition to your library.

I've had this game installed for over a year now, and I have only about five puzzle worlds to complete, and I've been putting it off. Not because I don't like it - but because I cried like a wimp after every playsession.
Yeah, there's things about this game that could be improved. Sometimes the puzzles felt kind of counterintuitive; I had to look solutions up a lot from about midway through the game, and I never had any trouble with Portal games or other puzzle adventures. It gave me mad motion sickness. But the emotional payoff outweighs that by far.
The game is very bittersweet and wistful, and slowly unraveling the story - without much fanfare or any dramatic reveal moments - tugged at my heartstrings. It really has a great atmosphere, and it doesn't rush you - it encourages you to roam, to think. And part of why I'm putting the endgame off is that I still don't know what my choice is going to be; am I ready? Can I make this big a choice for myself and for everyone else that follows? Not to mention that a single terminal entry mentioning someone's last act of kindness had me actually crying. Triple-A sci-fi games honestly can only wish about this sort of emotional investment from me.
The Talos Principle is a lovely gem of a game, and I recommend it to anyone who'd like to try playing something slow-paced and introspective.

They have done it again. Some of the minds behind Super Meat Boy have created yet another amazing platformer. Super Meat Boy was, and still is, one of my favorite games of all time, and already I can say that The End is Nigh is rising up to that point. It has smooth, tight controls and all sorts of new challenges. One of my favorite things about Super Meat Boy was the insane challenge that some levels presented, but then also the incredible feeling of beating those levels. The End is Nigh delivers on this as well, as the controls and gameplay are so well formed, yet simple, that you really feel accomplished when you beat a level. It's that classic "hard, but fair" type of game where the levels may be crazy, but the tight controls can't be to blame for the difficulty. I highly recommend this game for anyone who loved Meat Boy and anyone who loves platformers and incredible challenge.

Jogo bem legal, gostei bastante. Apesar de parecer um jogo de plataforma comum, ele oferece mais coisas do que aparenta. Os combates são um pouco chatos pra pegar a manha mas depois que vc aprende, o jogo fica bem divertido. Vc deve aprender os padrões de golpe do inimigo pra então planejar o seu ataque e acredito que esse seja o principal motivo de tanta gente não ter curtido muito o jogo. Não adianta vc ficar apertando freneticamente o botão do controle esperando atingir o inimigo o máximo de vezes possível. Se vc jogar assim, não vai conseguir chegar muito longe e vai acabar se frustrando.
O combate é o que na minha opinião tornou esse jogo bem divertido. Não chega a ser aquela coisa apelona do dark souls hehe, mas bem de leve lembra um pouco, pelo fato de vc ter que calcular os movimentos dos inimigos e quando vc deve o atacar.
As fases são geradas aleatoriamente, por isso cada vez que vc morre, volta ao começo. O objetivo do jogo é passar pelas diversas cavernas até chegar no chefão final. Quando o personagem morre, vc mantém o progresso dele e também o dinheiro coletado. Nessa estrutura das cavernas, existem 3 níveis, fácil, médio e difícil. O padrão de dificuldade também é aleatório, vc pode tanto ir por uma trilha só com cavernas de dificuldade fácil ou logo de cara ter que passar por uma com a dificuldade difícil.
No começo é meio difícil pq como as fases e dificuldades são geradas aleatoriamente, vc já de cara pode ter que enfrentar 2 fases da maior dificuldade, e nisso vc vai penar pra passar por que seu personagem está ainda fraco. Mas ao longo do jogo e à medida que o personagem subir de nível e ganha novas habilidades, juntamente com o fato de que vc provavelmente irá controlar melhor o personagem por ir pegando a manha dos combates, o jogo fica bem mais tranquilo. Quando eu cheguei mais ou menos no nível 10, já consegui chegar na penúltima caverna antes do chefão final sem morrer nenhuma vez.
A trilha sonora do jogo é bem legal, casou bem com a atmosfera das fases. Os gráficos são ok, nada muito extraordinário mas também longe de serem ruins. O ponto forte é pra paisagem das fases, que são bem desenhadas e o design dos inimigos, que é bem psicodélico. Eles até me lembraram os inimigos do jogo Zeno Clash, que foi feito por essa mesma produtora.
O único ponto fraco do jogo é o controle, que poderia ser mais preciso. As vezes os comandos não saem e isso frustra um pouco, mas nada que chegue a tirar a diversão do jogo. No mais, eu recomendaria esse jogo pra quem gosta desse estilo em plataforma e também goste de jogos mais difíceis e desafiadores. Se vc procura um jogo desse estilo porém que seja mais casual e mais simples, eu recomendaria procurar outras opções. Acho que esse jogo é meio 8 ou 80, ou vc vai gostar muito ou de cara já vai odiar e deixar ele de lado.
