*blink blink* ......wait, that's it? It’s over? Finished? Completed? Ended?
OKAY THEN. Onto the review!
This is a game where you get to name the main character, so naturally, I named him Billy Bob (because Billy Bob Joe Blink wouldn't fit). And made him a wizard. Because why not.
The first word that comes to mind with this game is “huh?” promptly followed by a shrugging “meh”. It has several good characteristics and several bad ones too. What are they?
Let me get the positive aspects out of the way. The battle system and animations were nice, the map layouts were quite good, and the sprite work itself seemed quite decent. Plus, I suspect there’s a bit of replayability, based on how the ending played out for me, but this game didn’t engage me enough to make me get another ending. Also, the choices you got to make in regards to your Party Members were a nice touch. And let us not forgot the original sound track, because even I think it's quite good. I'm pretty sure there are other positive aspects I could mention, but my mind is drawing a blank right now. But just because it is, doesn't mean there aren't more positives.
Anyway, now that that’s over with, lets begin with the negatives…
The plot itself wasn’t actually too bad, when you get down to it. I won’t say what it is, but it definitely has potential by itself. If put into more competent hands, I think we’d have a really great RPG Maker Game on our hands. However, what fails is the delivery; more specifically the dialogue.
Not to mention that the writers try to make the main character cool, but instead makes him come across as a jerk. The “Jerk with a Heart of Gold” Trope is a very fine line to walk. The first scene of the game, he forces his love interest to help him fight in the first battle of the game. This would be cute and all if it was established that she was a fighter babe and have them bond as a couple during this. But she's kidnapped promptly after (because of course she is), and she's wearing A FREAKING ROCOCO DRESS! This is the kind of gal the hero would look good defending, not one you drag into the battlefield! Even ignoring that, he seemingly complains about everything. True, it could be because of some of the things I made him do, but proclaiming “I hate monasteries” upon entering one does not make him look good. I almost want him to die…
.
Okay, saying this guy’s a complete jerk is not fair. This guy is 50% jerk and 50% idiot. He asks squirrels why they look sad and even said an open fire was delicious. Billy Joe can read the facial expressions of squirrels? And can taste fire without touching it or getting burned? Most of the dialogue does not sound natural in the slightest, even from the side characters and NPCs. This is an actual exchange I had with my friend when I quoted one of the lines from the game:
"I have the blood of innocent people on my hands! Why!?!?!"
Me: I dunno! You tell me.
Friend: durrrr
Which I thought was an excellent summation of this game's dialogue.
Also, this game is confusing at times. Like, the first enemy of the game is a slime, and I think it swung a sword at me...without hands. And I think there was an archer I fought who shot an arrow out of a bow while holding it backwards. I don’t fault this with the game, though, since these things are a pain to fix, especially someone who is terrible at programming like I am. However, it just looks...odd sometimes.
What about the characters, you may hypothetically ask? They’re all one dimensional, and some don’t even make sense. There was this freaking angel chick that appeared out of nowhere halfway through, and I STILL don’t know what’s up with her. Long story short, this is not a game you play for the characters. Moving on.
I felt like I wasn’t allowed to explore the world as much as I would have liked to. The two boats in the game only gave you the option of going straight to one destination, negating any potential exploring. Why? Why not make little optional areas for the player to explore? This would make them feel like they've discovered a secret area or something. Granted, a lot of RPGs are quite linear, but this one felt even more so.
Lastly, there was what I think was supposed to be religious commentary that left me rather confused. The main character says he won’t read a Bible he comes across because he “doesn’t believe in the big man”, but just goes along with this random demon dude
? Wouldn’t that be evidence enough to repent and join any religion in hopes to avoid meeting such a fate when
?
And even if Billy Bob is a stubborn old magical geezer who ain’t easily swayed by such life changing events…the rest of religious stuff just puzzles me… There’s an underworld, demons, and monster roaming around, clearly indicating that this is a different world than our own, yet they have the Bible? That’s kind of Earth-specific, especially the Old Testament, which is the Hebrew accountings of what many believe to be the World’s History. What the heck is it doing in an RPG Maker World?
Also, there was a bookshelf in the monastery that was apparently on “all kind(sic) of religions”, which doesn’t make sense, considering that monasteries were dedicated to only ONE religion. But this makes a lot more sense than the monks having a secret mine where they forced slaves to work… Do the writers even know what the definition of a monastery is? Or what people actually did there? I just... What?
Another curious thing about this is that this is clearly a different world than our own, but they have the Christian Religion? Like, I get that those sprites come with the RPG Maker default set, but other games have avoided this issue by saying that the religious imagery is for a completely different religion. Which works to an extent where the audience can let it slide. However, here, it’s specifically Christianity, since the main symbol is the cross (an execution method during much of time of the Roman Empire), and very few other religions worship a single deity, let alone call them “the Big Man”. In that case, wouldn’t that mean this game is saying that Christianity is the TRUE religion, since it spans over multiple worlds? But, if that’s the case, then why Christianity portrayed with such hostility throughout the game?
Look, I realize I’m overthinking this, and that’s because I’m a religious person, myself. I am not ashamed of that fact, but I’m also not afraid of hearing and understanding opposing opinions. With that said, if you’re going to criticize my religion, can you at least do it in a way that makes sense?
Overall, I guess I’m mostly neutral about this game, though I have more negative things to say than positive. While the religious commentary didn’t make any sense, it wasn’t offensive either, so you can argue this game is mostly harmless. If you want an RPG that’s kinda mindless, but still fun to play, I guess this one isn’t too bad. But if you’re like me and can’t help but pick apart bad dialogue, point out plot holes, and look for deeper meaning in stories, then there are better games to spend your money on.

Squad is a team-tactical FPS. No fancy HUD, no high-tech weapons, no scorestreaks. Everything is based on real-world weapons, abilities, and tech. Much of the tech in the game is dated(old) i.e. the scopes and vehicles.
At the time of this review there were two objective modes. One is "domination" i.e. holding an area with your squad with superior numbers. The other is more of a "Search and Destroy" mode. You aren't prevented from spawning but you do have to find the enemy weapons cache and destroy it.
3 voice channels allow you to communicate locally, with your squad, or your squad leader can communicate with your entire faction's squad leaders on a command channel.
No perks, meaning everyone has the same advantages and disadvantages, with only one exception. You choose your role in the squad, which determines the type of weapon and loadout you carry. The heavier the weapon, the faster your stamina runs out, the slower you move. You trade high-powered weapons for speed.
Stealth and tactics are key... but there are no silent kills in this game, at least not yet. Headshots kill. Body shots require 2 or more hits if the target is at full health. If you get shot once, you will bleed out if you don't bandage yourself. You require a medic to restore you to full health.
Snipers are deadly, but the maps are huge. Lay down a fob, build up sandbags, razor wire, place .50 cal turrets, and hold your areas.
This is an Alpha review, not a review of the final game at completion.
Pros:
☼ Multiple voice channels
☼ Realism maximized
☼ No gamertag giveaways. (You can't be spotted by gamertag, situational awareness prevents TKs)
☼ Lightweight game = great performance and still has decent graphics.
☼ Encourages teamwork and a deeper level of gameplay than you experience from most MMOFPS games.
Cons:
☼ No Favorites option in Server browsing.
☼ No simple method for creating a private server.
☼ No simple method of banning users from squads.
☼ Vehicles are often fought over between squads at round starts. Assigning vehicles to squads and giving the option to abandon would be a better approach to ensure everyone has a fair chance.
☼ CROW system (speaking from experience here) has the ability to lock on to moving vehicles for precision fire. Would like to see this added for realism's sake.
☼ The game lacks instructions for most of the advanced features i.e. zooming in a turret system. (Press Q)
As an Alpha I give the game an 8/10. A few things need to be fixed and added and this game is a solid 10/10 for me.
Like I said, it's an Alpha review so if you think the rating is too high or low, wait until the game is completed and the review will be updated.
Update 1: While I still believe this game is an excellent combat sim, there are a startling number of Admins on various servers who come away from each game with 30+ kills per game. I want to believe that they are just "really good" and "I'm just bad" but more often than not I have encountered an admin who had a near-psychic ability to know exactly where people are and snap-aim and one-shot kill myself and my team mates. I've watched a single admin wipe 2 squads with little or no resistence. I've even watched one take multiple grenades while standing up and not take damage. I have seen the command list for Admins and do not believe that there is a "god mode".
If these Admins are indeed highly skilled, they tend to run in the same squad, and thus unbalance teams. You will VERY seldomly win a game against a squad of admins. The rest of the team becomes irrelevant.
Until some form of anti-cheat is in full effect and reports of people being VAC banned start circulating, I'm uninstalling the game. I don't want to become so frustrated with the game that I become toxic, so instead I'm going to take a break and come back. I hope things improve. I hope team balancing includes some skill-based factor, limits of a specific number of admins-per-squad, better hitboxes (sandbags vehicles and ridges) less floating object, and vehicle flipping glitches.
I still recommend this game. There are many benefits to the game that you will gain hours of enjoyment from. You will eventually encounter what I'm talking about, though.

It's a competitive, multiplayer, class-based first person shooter.  Each of the four classes has four or more heroes with their own abilities.  The balance is such that there are no real hard-counters (a game mechanic I absolutely despise in shooters, looking at you Overwatch) and skill matters more than class in combat engangements.
You select 3 heroes before the match starts, and equip a loadout per selected hero.  Once the match starts, you can only switch between the three heroes you picked.
Loadouts consist of a different mix of primary weapon, secondary weapon, melee weapon and 0-3 bonuses.  These bonuses that allow reloading while sprinting, faster cool-downs for support skills, etc.  Default loadouts have no bonuses.  You always have access to the default loadouts.  Loadouts that have bonuses come in three rarities, with the first tier having only 1 bonus, the second having 2 bonuses, and the rest of the tiers having 3 bonuses.  The difference between tier 3 and up is simply cosmetic.  This means gameplay-wise you only ever need tier 3 loadouts (copper rarity loadout cards).
The free-to-play aspect comes from obtaining heroes and loadouts.
A few heroes are free at any given moment with a weekly rotation of 3 heroes, but permanent access to a hero requires that you buy them through in-game currency or with real money.  With hero prices going up to 30,000 and even 50,000 in-game currency and 10 hours of constant gaming getting you around 10,000 in-game currency, it will take a fairly long time to buy heroes using in-game currency alone.
Do you need access to all the heroes to have fun?  No.  If you want to unlock 3 heroes ( as mentioned before, you can only bring a maximum of 3 heroes into a match) which fit your playstyle you can do so in the first 20-30 hours of play, and be happy.  I bought 2 heroes with in-game currency (and stayed with 1 of the default heroes), and was happy for my first 80 hours of play.  The default heroes are very good (even better than some of the non-default IMHO) but the heroes are fairly well balanced as of now.  Every newly introduced hero is usually very strong and sees some kind of small nerf though.
Loadouts are obtained by purchasing them directly for around 18,000 in-game currency, or for around $0.80 USD.  This lets you choose the exact loadout you want, and these are usually tier 3 (copper).  Alternatively, you can get them through crates that have a random drop chance of loadouts for any hero, at any rarity (including heroes you don't have, though you can use those when that hero is in free rotation).  Crates are dropped when you level up your account, and for daily login bonuses.  Loadouts you don't want can be deconstructed for parts which can then be used to craft loadouts for specific heroes.  Overall, it doesn't take much time or effort (maybe 5-10 hours, depending on if you want to buy direcly or to take a chance on crates) to get a tier 3 loadout for the hero you want.
Loadouts also affect cosmetics.  Overall, the skins aren't really all that different from each other regardless of rarity so any tier higher than tier 3 doesn't really matter.  This could change in the future though.
If you are dedicated and REALLY don't want to spend any cash, you can do that and have quite a lot of fun. I did that for the first 60 hours I played.  The different heroes are pretty well balanced and though the loadout bonuses can be very impactful to gameplay, tier 3 loadouts for your hero of choice can be obtained fairly quickly.
However, as a gamer who doesn't really like F2P systems, I prefer to spend around 15-60 USD and never really spend any more.  That is, I like treating F2P games that I find fun as $15, $30 or $60 games. Dirty Bomb lets you do that as the game isn't completely reliant on constantly having to purchase more and more stuff with real money.  If you want to do what I did, my suggestion is to purchase one of the hero bundles offered and to not sweat the loadouts as tier 3 loadouts are all you need for max bonuses and they're fairly easy to come by.
The gameplay consists of objective-based rounds with usually 3 different defence/attack objectives per round.  The round ends when the time runs out or all 3 objectives are completed by the attackers.  Some modes have only 1 round, other have more.  The maps are fairly well-designed and have opportunities for different classes to shine by interacting with different objectives and side-objectives to open up or close parts of the map, or by keeping the team in the fight, or even by simply killing the opposition.  The game is worth a try and I say it's worth buying the different hero bundles offered, but it isn't needed.

This is a puzzle game with a lot of philosophy.
The gameplay: The puzzles are a brain tease and gives you a good intelligence workout. They are however a bit too easy if you ask me. The problem is that for every new item they give you to solve more complicated puzzles, they give you easy puzzles so you can get used to them. This results in the problem of only a handful of puzzles actually makes you feel smart for solving. I still think it was good and the ending puzzle in the tower is really cool!
The Philosophy/story: I’m not sure what to say about this. I’m speaking out of a very subjective viewpoint here. For me, who is atheist, Swed, had philosophy in high school and am, at the time of this writing, 28 years old. For me, it felt like it would be interesting at age 14-16. I have already talked and studied these things at a young age. It didn’t give me anything here. The conversations you had with the computer was fun but limited. For example. When I said I want to do whats best for me the computer asks: So you would use people and steal from them? I could only answer: “No, I have morals” (which is something religious people have) or “Yes! (which wouldn’t help you at all since humans are so much better together socializing).
Anyway: In short I would recommend this to people who really like puzzle games, those who felt they missed out on philosophy in high school, religious people and anyone of age 14-16.
PS: It works on Linux!

I don't quite know what it is about this game that keeps me coming back to it. (At least twice after my initial playthrough.) I know nothing about the Might & Magic world or the other games set in it. I'm sure there's more story the characters and events in this game. I hope so since the story felt a bit disjointed and incomplete. I was put in middle of events I have no idea why they happened. The characters were never properly introduced either. Or built upon.
But the gameplay. There is that little something in the gameplay. I can't quite put my finger on it but best I could describe it is solid. This feels and plays like a very solid game. What that means I'm not too sure. I have no problems with any of the gameplay mechanics. I just love how the gameplay feels.
The graphics, despite being an old game, still hold up just fine. It has that old time 3D feel but that's just fine. I think it adds to the game. It is also worth noting that this is a very linear game. There is very little exploration to do. And I dislike most linear games.
I really like this game. Every time I think about it I get the urge to try it out once more. The story isn't all that interesting to me and graphics just do their job. It's the combat and overall gameplay that keeps me coming back. But I just don't know why.
If this ever goes on sale again I definitely suggest picking it up, just don't expect a great story. Even so this is one of my favorite games among such popular hits as Trine 2, Mirror's Edge, and Psychonauts as you can see from my profile showcase. I feel like this is a very underrated and unknown game.
If you're a game designer or a wanting to be one I suggest you check out this game. Perhaps you could take apart and analyze why this gameplay feels so different from all the other sword and sorcery RPGs. I genuinely  think there is something to be studied here.

As a Super Meat Boy veteran, I find The End is Nigh really, really nice.
The platforming itself is top notch, because of the high quality level design and tight controls. This time around, there's a lot of exploration, and the difficulty has been ramped up considerably.
The visual side is well done too. Each area has its distinctive colour palette and style. You gather game cartridges, which can be played in the player character's home - these are reminiscent of the warp levels in Super Meat Boy. That is to say, they're retro platformers with big pixels, with chiptune accompaniment. Also, they get really challenging. (Especially when you find so-called iron cartridges - but I'll shut up about those.)
I think I'm about halfway done with the game, according to the in-game completion percentage, with 13 hours played at the time of writing. I don't think I'll ever get 100% completion because of the insane difficulty, but even finding most of the stuff and getting a "normal ending" (if there's such a thing), will provide hours and hours of more gameplay.
Highly recommended if you like challenging platforming with short levels and lots of repetition to get it right, with high production values.

Why hello there friend. Say, do you enjoy ATLUS games? Do you enjoy roguelikes? Well how about fighting games, surely you enjoy those. If the answer to any or all of these questions was a resounding yes then I have some great news for you! Abyss Odyssey is a game which manages to combine all of those things into one complete package - and then some!
This game has beautiful visuals, strong atmosphere and easy to get into yet hard to master gameplay. The combat has more in common with a fighting game than a simple side scrolling action RPG, there are several quick button combos and cancels that can be performed across each character giving all of the heroes (of which there are 3) a unique feel. The core game mechanic is that of the roguelike, you will enter into the randomly generated abyss and proceed up ways and down ways and sideways and the like, each section offering new peril and new reward. If you enjoy games that have a dark yet almost serene atmosphere about them I would say this is definitely one to pick up, the game does a great job with its varying environment types within the abyss and the subtle musical accompaniments contribute to that package.
Like most roguelikes you can expect there to be a bit of a difficulty curve, items and levels will always be lost on death but your wealth will remain with you to make your next descent a bit easier. If you are on the fence about this one but you enjoy any of the things I mentioned above I would say go ahead and pick it up, it's worth it!

Genre: Fighting-Rougelike
Overall rating: 86%
Gameplay: 17/20
Sound/Music: 9/10
Graphics: 4/5 - Art design: 5/5
Controls: 3/5
Replay value: 5/5
Gameplay;
It's a fighting/platformer game with rouge-like elements. Combat works just like in a fighting game, every character/enemy has a proper move set, but instead of just a one screen arena, you have to fight through a randomized dungeon with multiple floors and paths.
The game has around 40 characters, three of them are main characters with the ability to capture enemy souls. This is one of the key features of the game, because once you capture a soul you can use that enemy/boss in the game. There are some ballance issues with this though, some are near worthless some are op and this can impact versus mode.
However it's not just a regular figthing game with platforming. The game has co-op and an inventory system, your main charactes can level up and gain skill points to strengthen moves they have found.
Sound/Music;
Music is excellent, sometimes reminds me of Castlevania, it creates a good atmosphere for the levels and characters. But it doesn't have any "God tier" songs that I would put on my mp3 player so it's "just" a 9 out of 10.
Graphics;
Nothing extraordinary here, good dungeon prop variety and nice backgrounds makes the dungeons look good.
But that's it, doesn't look bad or particularly good, it serves it's purpose.
Art desing;
Absolutely fantastic and very creative. The characters are very well designed, they are intersting, beautiful, creepy, terrifying. Things that look like a nightmare or a dream. (the game takes place in a nightmare) Levels are beautiful, and sometimes weird dream like. The menu is super cool.
Controls;
Oh my GOD the controls they seem bad, and they kinda are. But they aren't that bad once you figured out,
You can also walljump which is completely useless and annoying. Blocking and dodging can get awkward too sometimes. Also might need X360ce for your controller to function.
Replay value;
Randomly generated dungeons with loot and secrets, every enemy has like a dozen moves not just 2 or 3 and you can play as enemies and bosses. With random encounters to keep things interesting. (some of them are pretty creative) It also has versus mode and co-op.

The problem is the execution in the online-play. There are latency BUGS, oh sweet pete, the bugs. There's the 'stuck-in-falling-animation'glitch (which comes with a free 'mid-air-platforms-are-now-invisible' bug), the 'not-pulling-myself-up-onto-that-ledge-when-I'm-right-there' bug, and on rare occasion, the 'keep-spawning-1-or-2-platforms-ABOVE-where-you-just-dropped' thing.

Abyss Odyssey exists at this weird crossroads between art nouveau stylings, Smash Bros mechanics, and roguelike design. If that just made your brain ache I implore you to stay with me, because it's not the mess it might seem. No, it's a potent mix that you never fully get used to, one of those rare indie games that feels incredibly indie no matter how long you play it. Perhaps even more remarkable is the way these elements harmonize to form something not just unique, but entertaining as well.
It's the close of the 19th century and something nasty is happening under the streets of Santiago, Chile. You get dumped into the world as the absolutely drop-dead gorgeous Katrien, a hardy swordswoman who is refreshingly up-front about her mysterious origins. There's a warlock slumbering deep beneath the surface, and his nightmares are becoming reality. To put a stop to it, you descend through a randomly-generated network of caves, collect gold, weapons, and items, and defeat a bizarre host of monsters on your way to end the warlock once and for all.
The way this plays out is in a long series of short levels that are light on platforming and heavy on beat-em-upping. Comparisons to Smash Bros are not lazy, because this game uses the same facing systems, same jump mechanics, and it even has a sort of Smash button for special moves. If you ever played the story mode in SSB Brawl, in fact, this will feel very familiar. Monsters range from jaunty skeletons to deer people to flying regalia, and the bosses that you sometimes run across are some of the most unique I've ever seen. There's also a really cool capture system where you can claim an enemy's soul to use as a second character, making the wide variety of creative foes even more appealing.
My only real knock against this game is the uneven difficulty curve... or maybe it's actually the learning curve. The first few times I played, I couldn't make it more than a few floors. Then one night I had some kind of breakthrough, and I haven't died since. One irritation is what happens when you die, because you get replaced with a weak, clunky soldier and you can't get Katrien back unless you find a special shrine that only appears once every few floors. Floors can be rated easy, medium, or hard, which has a dramatic effect on how aggressive enemies will be. However, the AI can get confused pretty easily, slipping between countering every move and standing there to get wailed on. You'll need to stick with it awhile to really get into the flow, but there's a surprising amount of secrets and special floors to discover along the way.
I don't need to tell you how good this game looks, because just look at it. The art style sets the whole thing off, working perfectly with the late 19th century setting and the dreamworld motifs. There are two additional characters to unlock, additional special moves to upgrade, and a colorful cast of mysterious figures to learn about. It's going to take some getting used to, no doubt, but the eclectic style and unabashed uniqueness make it worth the effort. Once you learn the rhythm of the game and learn where to spend your gold, you'll have plenty of fun venturing into the abyss again and again.

Squad is a PVP, semi mil-sim game; that stands somewhere between Battlefield and Arma 3.
My experiences and opinion are about alpha 8.8 (and around that release), and you have to take into consideration that my primary role is medic. Also, I was a squad leader level backer, so I sunk some more hours into the non-steam versions. I'm going to update my review in the future if things change significantly.
Things I like
- More realistic than Battlefield.
- Faster than Arma 3.
- Teamwork and communication are encouraged by the community.
- Runs quite well. (note, I'm playing on 1080 with tons of ram)
- Looks nice (especially after patch 8).
- It's a blast to play with a good squad leader.
- Base building is fun.
Things I dislike
- Complete lack of player customization, you are locked to one weapon and loadout based on your role in the squad. It would be significantly better to have fewer roles, but being able to customize each loadout a bit. Few weapons to choose from, optics, grenades, etc. Just like in real-life, wherein some armies, soldiers are allowed to customize their gun.
- Can't pick up weapons or drive captured enemy vehicles.
- Can't drag drowned people out of harm's way.
- No helicopters.
- Vehicle physics are oversimplified.
- Sometimes it's hard to find a good squad leader.
- Lots of people become squad leaders, who are clearly not meant for the job.
- Some squad leaders tend to push their bad decisions on their squad mates, even if it's clearly their fault.
- No destruction.
- No doors.
- Around certain hours, there is only one Australian server, and it's either full or empty, so I have to jump on US servers.
- Night maps are awful without the equipment to improve visibility. Like night visions or flares.
- Base building is finicky and finding the right spot for digging can be annoying.
- Bandaging doesn't work sometimes, and people transport randomly around after reviving.
- There isn't an ammo bearer role.
- It's hard to play together with friends; no lobby system whatsoever.
- No silencers.
- Stances are limited, and it is inconvenient to shoot over cover. Either you are exposing too much by not standing up, or you end up hitting the edge while crouching. Arma 3 is far superior in this aspect.
- No zeroing.
Note, I totally understand that some of the things I dislike are there because of balance decisions, but I keep my right to disagree with those.
So, as you would expect, I won't recommend the game in its current state for 40 USD. If you can pick it up for 10-15 bucks, then go for it, give it a go. Otherwise, wait for the full release.
Alternatively, you can also go for Arma 3, which is a way more fleshed out game, and a more serious mil-sim, even with all of its problems (performance, and awful movement system).
----
There is something else I want to mention. As a (semi) mil-sim, Squad tends to give their players a sense of superiority over other games, which clearly shows in the reviews. My favorite phrase is, "if you don't want to play in a team, go for CS:GO or Battlefield." I always have a good laugh at these people. :)

Where SMB was a platformer that shot-for-the-middle, had tight controls and interesting levels, making just an all-round good platformer, The End is Nigh never really shows anything too mechanically innovative (other than the appliances of the ledge-jump), which makes it very much the same as SMB. However, as a fan of Edmund's previous work, I still throughly enjoyed a taste of something new, giving me another game to challenge myself with. It doesn't feature any aspect that is glaringly bad, and for those looking for this type of game (like myself), The End is Nigh is likely to satisfy.

Opposing Force is for people who enjoyed the gameplay of HL1 and are looking for seconds, preferably with wackier weapons and a grappling hook.
I played original Half-Life back in the day, but not the expansions.  So when I picked up the original in a nostalgia rush, I decided to fill in that particular omission.  So I came to this with nostalgia for the original game and all its flaws, but not this iteration.  And I enjoyed it; I think it's inferior to the original, but as an expansion that's expected.
The gameplay is the main strength here.  The new weapons show variety and creativity.  The two melee weapons are arguably better than Gordon's iconic crowbar; at the least, they give more depth to close combat.  The alien weapons are where things get really creative, and also creepily cute.  The Shock Roach is more satisfying than the Hive Hand ever was; you lose the ability to shoot round corners, but the damage feels better and you gain the ability to accidentally suicide in water.  The Spore Launcher offers interesting reloading strategies and bouncing projectiles that reward skill, plus amusing idle animations.  The Displacer Cannon rewards experimentation. Lastly, the Barnacle "grappling hook" enhances the overall experience by adding a third dimension of mobility.
The new enemies are nice to see, though I don't think they add anything tactically.  To me, they fill roles similar to the Xen aliens in HL1.  There are some good set-pieces, such as the conflict in the sewers.  The presence of squad mates is fun, though it is limited by the dated AI.
The story is a bit of a trickier proposition.  While the creators clearly put a lot of effort into the plot and how it is told, it doesn't feel quite as polished as the original.  A bigger problem, perhaps, is that nothing here is directly mentioned in later games.  Skipping this doesn't affect your enjoyment of the larger Half-Life narrative, hence my recommendation above.

When you hear people on Steam lament about "another RPG Maker game," it's because of stuff like this.
The writing isn't bad, no. It isn't even worth referring to as "writing." This may have been made by some youngsters or something because this reminds me of the kind of thing I wrote with my buddies back in middle school because of the absurd lack of depth to anything and childish dialogue. EX: Main character walks into a monastery and comments, "This monastery is s**t!" or some such. He just uses profanity and yells at things I ASSUME so that he sounds like some kind of cool dude with a 'tude or something? That's half the time. The other half he's just blandly helpful. He loves his girlfriend (or I guess you could choose to not tell your girlfriend you love her?). He's mostly helpful, but he complains a lot. Which is probably supposed to be some kind of parody of RPG tropes and their bland fetch quests and such. Maybe he's supposed to be bipolar? Regardless, there are a ton of easily avoided spelling and grammar mistakes (EX: use of the word "abandonned").
I'm not just ragging on these guys for choice of words and typo's, though. Oh, no. The story itself reads like a kid wrote it. Seriously, it's like Axe Cop only not hilarious or creative. For example, at some point you enter a village and are asked to go to a cave to stop... bandits or something (?) from attacking said village. A mercenary guy joins your party to help you as he is emotionally invested in helping this village, I think. In the cave you fight some kind of ghostly knights and an ogre. Then you stumble upon a time travel amulet for no reason. The main character goes "Sweet!" and finds out how to go back in time. The whole reason you came to that cave (remember the village being attacked?) was completely forgotten the moment you stepped into that cave and the warrior who joined you silently sticks with you for the rest of the adventure, given no characterization or lines of dialogue again (save for maybe pointing out the amulet is a time travel amulet). Later on, after you're done using the time travel amulet, a pop-up tells you the amulet is now broken. I can only assume this was some kind of afterthought when someone asked, "Why don't they just travel back in time again?" Maybe it only held enough magic for one use, but where does this place you in time? And why was the demon you were chasing exist in the same time line? It seems like when it broke you went back to the future and yet he's there with you. What kind of sloppy nonsense is this!
The whole game is like this. The first town has you start in a prison that you break out of. But then it's said the prison guards somehow hold the town hostage. So, doesn't that make them warlords or something? Not just "prison guards?" Why do they bother running a prison? Did they turn the castle into a prison? And they all live there? What?
How about the combat? Well, it's overly basic. I guess some people think this is par for the course for RPG Maker games or JRPG's, but I think it's plain lazy. Sometimes you have to heal or manage your mana, so I guess that's something. But there's so little strategy and so much overlap between the classes.
If there's one consolation it's the music. Sweet Christmas, this person poured his/her heart into it. I mean, it's not that it's outstanding. You know? Like I'm not rushing to get the MP3's onto my iPod or anything. But there's actual composition, effort, know-how, and emotion in it. There's even a live (I think) guitar in there! I'm a sucker for metal, true, but those boss fights were intense ONLY because of this chugging distortion and orchestral synth-work. Composer, please, whoever you are, ditch these guys. You actually have some amount of talent and skill! These guys can't even piece together any kind of semblance of a game.

Pretty basic fighting game with various problems.
But first the positive:
-Nice game concept
-Interesting background story
-Fun for the first few hours
-Potentially amazing genre-mixup
Now for the negative:
-For one, there's only very limited characters to be played.
-The character's power level varies widely (some are totally useless, others really op)
-A lot of said characters (including the op ones) feel really clunky
-The PvE feels dull and (especially the "nightmare mode") often pretty unfair (enemies keep you stunned until you are dead etc.)
-The "skill system" seems like a nice touch at first but does not add any depth to the game because adding skillpoints to ceratin moves only increases either armor during the move, the mana gained or flat damage output
-The "special skill" is, again, a nice idea but poorly implemented. Every character has the same and it takes forever to gather the mana needed in order to cast one
-During PvE you level up your hero. The problem here is that a levelup only gives very minor improvements to stats and a (pretty useless) skillpoint every now and then
-Waiting times to find a PvP match are off limits. Seriously. I just kinda gave up after a while
-The inventory system is really bad. You can only store 6 items, can't change their order, delete them or even use them under certain circumstances.
As a conclusion I would only recommend this game to the most hardcore Fighting/Platformer fans and/or people with a pretty high frustration tolerance. Everybody else should probably just play Street Fighter or some good old platformer

Oxenfree is a fully voice acted horror-adventure game with a great setting and an effective radio mechanic. It’s also a visual treat with an attractive art style and dreary colors. However, the game does have some uncomfortably annoying parts to it that take away from the 4-hour experience. I strongly recommend having a natural playthrough without looking up anything and using a controller since the mouse cursor is just the Windows default which looks tacky.
You play as Alex, a seventeen-year-old teenage girl, who’s on her way to meet up with the rest of her friends on a beach located on Edwards Island. Everything’s fine and dandy when you first arrive, but from that point onward, the situation slowly takes a turn for the worse and the horror elements start creeping in.
You’ll find no jump scares in Oxenfree. Instead, its focus on setting and atmosphere dictates the mood of the game with great care. As you explore the island, you can tune into the Guided Tour Station with your radio and learn more about the different parts of the island and the historical significance. There are also letters to find and read that add even more backstory. I found the world to be genuinely interesting and wanted to know more. The whole game felt as if I were some detective attempting to solve a grand mystery or an adventurer exploring some ruins and I really loved that aspect of it.
Anyway, the game handles dialogue similar to the Telltale games. You have three choices that you can select before they fade out or you can choose to stay quiet. What you say affects how the other characters perceive you, how they respond, and the ending you achieve. You’ll need to be prepared to hear “like” frequently since you’ll be listening to a bunch of teenagers talk for a good chunk of the game.
There’s no challenge to this game. The puzzles mostly involve just finding the right frequency with the radio. There are other things in there too that I won’t spoil, but they’re not going to give your brain much exercise. The game leans very hard on its story and presentation to compensate for the weak gameplay. I especially liked how the radio’s role in upping the creep factor when checking out the other stations.
Where the game does it best to annoy me is with how dialogue timing is handled. The time pressure is fine, but what bothered me was the number of interruptions that result from providing a response. Sometimes, when selecting a choice, the other character(s) will finish what they’re saying and then Alex starts talking. All the other times, she’s interjecting and cutting off people left and right. As someone who wanted to hear what everyone had to say, I felt a little irked. There was no way to tell if Alex would wait or ejaculate her responses into the conversation with the finesse of a rampaging elephant which made it extra frustrating.
Another grievance I have with the game is the sound quality of the voice acting. Everyone speaks and the dialogue is the primary method of storytelling for the game, so to have some tinny voices that happen more often than I would like distracted me. One character in particular kept dropping in quality, which is a shame since the voice acting overall seemed fairly good and natural with some stiffness.
The travel speed in this game felt too slow and prevented me from having any desire to backtrack to look for collectibles. If you’re going along the critical path, you’ll run into situations that require your attention and keep you engaged. It’s only when wandering around did I become bored with the pace. I decided against dedicating any time to exploration despite wanting to due to the time it would take. If you have more patience than me, the letters would be worth finding since the content enriches the setting, among other things.
The story was a nice little spooky campfire tale until the final moments which gave it that “open to interpretation” type of deal. I usually don’t like games that do that and Oxenfree is no different. I did spend time reading different theories since the game had some things going for it and the ending variations were interesting to read about. None of the endings offer any real resolution when taking what happened into consideration which is what hurts it. I suppose with how the game uses certain themes, it’s not possible to have a neat conclusion or it’s just weak writing. I just have to live with the disappointment of not having a real answer.
Oxenfree was a fun experience with an ending that could have used more work. It should be a fun ride for most people since I’m assuming that I’m being harder on the game than others. I truly was on the fence and kept changing my mind about whether to recommend this game or not while writing this review, but in the end, I believe it’s a good game being held back by the aforementioned issues.

TL;DR don't play this. Play LoL or Dota 2.
EDIT: The game has had issues with matchmaking for over a year (from what I can see on reddit) and it still seems that noobs get matched with top 100 players regularly, which can be a BIG turnoff for new MOBA players or even lower skilled players. Until they fix this issue (not saying they ever will) I will NOT be recommending this game unless you know your way around another MOBA. If you're looking to get into the genre, don't start with Strife, go with Dota 2 or League of Legends instead.
Strife® is an excellent addition to the current MOBA generation (along with LoL, Dota2, Smite, HotS, etc.) as it renews old concepts in new ways: The pet system to mix up the summoner spells from LoL with the pet system from Dota2, the item upgrades to replace the rune system from LoL, the boots to emulate the summoner spells from LoL once again, items that have unique abilities like in Dota2 (and LoL to a certain extent) etc.
If i had to make a comparision and say which other MOBA is similar to this one, i'd have to say League of Legends, with a hint of HoN (Heroes of Newerth, S2's previous MOBA). The abilities strongly remind me of League and i'd say 80% of abilities from Strife® have an equivalent in LoL (Maybe with other MOBAs too, but I feel like the similarities with League of Legends are a bit more obvious).
I will now list all the pros/cons that Strife® has at the moment, in my opinion of course.
____________________________________________
*Pros*
-Very instructive tutorial for new players
-A sweet story mode (I had never seen this in a MOBA)
-Easy to pick up for any MOBA player (im talking about bird's view MOBA's here not the FPS ones)
-Leveling up is fast
-You have the entire hero pool unlocked from the start
-Short queue times
-They try really hard to discourage toxic behaviour
-Leaving is HEAVILY penalized (you have to wait like 30 mins if you leave one game, and it gets worse with every game you leave)
-You can easily play with top players/achieve a high rank because of how low the playerbase is
-The hero designs are VERY weird
*Cons*
-Very low playerbase at the moment.
-Small variety of heroes (not the number of heroes, but the variety between those heroes)
-Matchmaking is broken (You will get matched with people who are alot more experienced with the game sometimes, even as a noob.)
-Balance isn't optimal right now (Heroes like Blazer, Lady Tinder, Malady, Nikolai, Trixie, and others seem to be picked almost every game because of how easy it is to win with them)
These are my views on the new Steam arrival *Strife®* and in my opinnion it's worth giving a try. Of course, the artstyle isn't as cool as LoL and the graphics are not on the level of Dota2 but nevertheless, it's fun.

This game is absolutely stunning looking. But that is really the only thing it has going for it to be quiet honest.
The fighting is complete garbage. There's no real combos because your moves hit them away from you. To actually get combos you have to juggle the poor enemy against a wall or use your super. All the reviews that are comparing it to smash bros are somewhat correct but mostly assanine and not really helpful. Lke in smash bros, if you hold up and press attack, you will do an attack that is known as an up tilt, and this applies to all the directions, like in smash bros. The same rule follows aerials but they don't really lead to combos that often either. That is literally the only thing this game has in common with smash bros. So do not think you will be getting a cool game where you can combo people. There's a super move you get to use when your mana becomes completely full that can get you a pretty decent combo relative to the rest of the game though. By that I mean around 6 hits, which doesn't even kill an enemy. Useful.
Edit: There's fast falling like in smash bros as well. There's also grabbing and rolling out of shielding, but that's kind of standard for these types of games.
You get three specials as well, and they are pretty easy to spam and honestly make quick work of the enemies usually. There's no real reason to use the regular attacks after you get them unlocked. Hell the first girl gets a fireball which is mediocre but then she gets a counter, which you can just stand still and spam then you get a pokey attack that seems to put the enemy in enough hitstun to follow up with another pokey attack.
There's random items throughout the map, which is randomly generated every time you die and go down there. There's weapons which can range from being incompatable with your character to being able to catch them on fire or freeze them. There's other passive armor type things and potions, antidotes and mana things you can pick up. Not much to say about that. Then there's these other items that you can activate that will let you completely transform into one of the enemy units. I have no clue if these are helpful in any parts but so far I find my character to be more comfortable to use.
Now, you're probably wondering why I bothered typing out most of that? It's because the tutorial does absolutely nothing to help you other than your movements and give you your first special ability. That's it.
I wouldn't recommend this game at $15. I wouldn't at $10. I might say it's acceptable at $5, which is what I think I picked it up for during the Autumn sale. If there's anything I was vague about that would help your decision on bothering with this game, ask me. Or honestly, just pass.

Tough, fast, and nail-biting. That's how I'd sum up Dirty Bomb. Tough, because you will run into someone who has the aim of a god, fast, becuase the gamespeed rolls through combat and engagements at great speed, nail-biting, for when the C4 has just enough time left for you to try and use your pliers to defuse it.
Dirty bomb is probably viewed as a class-based team shooter, with a huge focus on objecitves that the team must work together to fulfill, and they're right in a sense, but the only classes there really are, are the three primary roles you can use when selecting your mercs (which are what the characters you can play as are called). Medic's: Healers, and the only ones with access to defibrillator type abilities, allowing you to pick up downed-but-not-out teammates, and deploy various medkits and healing actions. Specialists: Sometimes better suite dto defense, mostly because of the nature of their abilities, but just as good attacking. Can complete, arm, defuse, and repair the primary objectives way faster than the rest of the mercs. Then we have the last one, split between two snaller subclasses Recon, and Fire Support: Fire supports are one of the two kinds, either a straight up fragger, with lots of good offensive options and weapons, or they trade some of the offensive prowess for the ability to resupply teammates with ammo, which they will need. Recon are entirely either snipers or sharpshooters, capable of suppressing a lane of access, or covering teammates with deadly fire.
Main gameplay is obj based maps, which run through the map as you complete obj's as the attacker, or the defending team prevents that by keeping the attacking team from completing them. Around three or four obj's to use in various maps, such as planting C4 and getting it to blow, repairing generators and escort vehicles, and delivering containers. A much more noticable part of the game is the  fast shooting, players juking and weaving in and out of cover as they blast at each other with various types of guns. This is necessary, but remember that you win not by just killing the enemy team, but either by defending or completing objectives. You also do not spawn ten seconds after death, but must wait for a timer to run out where then all dead players, enemy and friendly, will respawn.
You have only three mercs you can equip in your squad loadout, So rather than pick from all the characters you have unlocked, once you go into a match, only the three mercs you put in your squad will be the ones you can play in that match. (Pro-tip: Bring at least a fire support, a medic, and a specialist. If your team doesn't want to play medics, fire support, or specialists, maybe you can be the tipping point in the match,)
I reccomend this game, but several warnings before you jump in. There is a microtransaction system, for cases that contain Loadout Cards. Cards change what weapons the merc in question is armed with, and certain tiers of cards (Bronze and up,) confer three small stat based changes to the merc, like damage explosion radius, how fast they reload, extending jump range or removing fall damage. These aren't really game changing in my opinion, becuase mostly the cards are for weapons or for a shiny skin the card can give. However, the card, while the bronze level can be purchased for in-game currency, the Cases that hold these cards give you a random card of varying rarity. And since the game is free, the way the developer makes money is selling you these cases, as well as special bundles and mercs. You can craft cards of higher rarity, but it'll take time. So if you don't like rng based buying systems, this might not be your kind of game.
Although, all technical detail aside, this is still a very skill based game. Sure, the mercs all have various powerful abilities, but the impact is lessened by the fact defibs exist. No matter how powerful the ability, there is a chance that you can just get right back up after getting fragged. The wave based respawn system is also more suited to an objective focused game, making full team wipes very important. Keep your aim true, your positioning smart, and awareness at heightened levels, and you will be feeling at home inthe game in no time.
Time for an inflammatory comment, one that I stand by.
Dirty Bomb is a better Team-based Objective Shooter than Overwatch. The Objectives are smarter to play and defend, the maps are more open and less designed to arficially create easy choke points, the characters are better by virtue of you master the weapon before you master the abilities, and many cases, it is smarter and more efficient to actually handle guns that don't have weird design choices to account for various strengths and weaknesses the character has. Just design a character that has an actual firearm instead of some cartoony, wacky, definitely not nerf-toy-juryrigged-into-lethality-by-a-giant-monkey. Feel free to dismiss this opinion as salt if you disagree.

I have only recently joined Squad when it was on sale, already owning Arma3 i didn't see buying this game full price worth it since Arma is a bigger game. However this game has grown on me. First of all the team work aspect of Squad which is what it is built around is good, and yes that still depends on the competency of who is the Squad leader and how well everyone communicates on the mic and works together varies. But most of the time it works as intended.
Squad has locked roles, its not like Arma where you can equip a sniper rifle and have an AT launcher on your back. Each role is important for the success of the team if those roles are played as they should be and its up to the Squad Leader to make use of them effiectively.
Also Squad has some gameplay elements such as being able to deploy a Rallypoint by the Squad Leader which the squad can respawn at although limited to 9 spawns, but also can place a FOB which has no spawn limit but can be overrun or destroyed by the enemy, along with being able to place defences such as sandbag walls and static machine guns. A logistics truck can resupply the fob. So where you place these on the map and how much defenses are put down is part of the strategies. It is what makes Squad more than just a shooter.
I used to play alot of Battlefield 4, which rarely your squad worked together at all. Sure the having destructable environment is a draw card in the Battlefield series but it is too far arcadey. By far Squad is more fun than Battlefield and more realistic too (no bullet sponge combat here). Another game i have played that is similar is 'Insurgency' and that game is fun too, but the maps are too small and respawn times too long for my liking, and is mostly a CQB. Squad has much larger maps, some areas open and other areas dense city areas with many dwellings you can go into and plenty of places to find cover, so there is variety. I would ever dare to say some of the maps in Squad are more interesting than maps in Arma (although Arma takes the cake for map size) but Squad could at a later date expand their map size when aircraft are introduced. When I saw interesting I mean there are decent size villages on some of them, and I would love to see large towns in the future.
Wrapping this up. Squad not only creates a teamwork feeling in your squad but sometimes you have a Squad Leader who knows what they are doing and it can be satisfying holding your ground or taking capture points. The winners will be the Squads that work well together and also Squad Leaders that communicate and work with other Squad leaders. Sometimes you can be on the receiving end of that, where no matter where you go your team gets put down fast.
There is more content to come which will expand the game and this will only make Squad better with more strategies and tactics to enrich the teamwork experience of Squad.  If you are into more casual games like COD, Battlefield and the idea of patiently holding an area for twenty minutes or more seems really boring then this game is not for you. If you hate the idea of being given orders and you follow them without arguing then you will not like this. Nor would lone-wolves survive long.

In the first and second games the mechanism was a standard search-and-find, where you look for the named object and that's that. A lot of people were displeased that it changes to a game where you have to search for objects that shift in shape instead of objects on a list. I suppose some don't like change, but this did not bother me. I will admit it does get slightly easier than it was before, but they do attempt to raise the difficulty by replacing still, picture environments to search in, with moving backgrounds. Twitching leaves, running water; things that catch your eye more than the shifting objects. If you're really bothered about that I would stay away from the game, because the search and finds are less prominent in this game. As before mentioned, it made no difference to me, because in the Ravenhearst story, it's not really the gameplay, but the storyline, that's the main feature of the game.
If you've ever played the original MCF: Ravenhearst, you will know this to be true. The entire point of the first game is finding out the story behind Charles and Emma's relationship, and their affiliation with Rose and her two daughters. The second game is mostly the story of Charles' crimes; the story of how you find the mansion, find out what Charles has really been doing with the place, and attempt to stop him and save what's left of the poor Rose and her daughters.
This game is Charles' story. As with any criminal, the backstory has a lot to do with their actions, and this game gives you a nice walk through Charles' memory lane (against your own wishes). I won't lie. It's messed up. But if you know what his crimes are, you'll probably expect that. If you don't know, then good luck. The game lives up to its name by the fact that you have to escape from Charles' meticulous trap and save Emma, Rose, and her two daughters. Again.
The art is fantastic, and I must give credit to Charles' actor. He really catches the sadistic and tormented side of Charles, and seeing as he appears to torment you quite often, you always have that cruel voice waiting for you wherever you go. I can't even fault any of the other actors, though Victor's dancing is the best comedy aspect of the game. That is just... wonderful. The story is a good level of creepy and shocking, and amongst all the puzzles and problems to solve, you get to do fun things like blow up Charles' mom with a pie.
All in all I don't think this game deserves the hate it's got, but maybe I'm biased because I'm not too bothered by the search mechanism. Sure it's a short game, but most search-and-find's are. The art is great, the actors are good, the storyline is really interesting, and the puzzles are challenging in a good way.

I do not recommend this game for a simple reason: it doesn't support anti-aliasing in AMD graphics card. This reason will not keep me away from this game, I'll surely play a lot more of it and I definitely recommend it if you have a Nvidia card or don't care about horrible aliasing, but I've seen lots of people upset about this and hence, cannot recommend it to everyone. And remember the game uses OpenGL, so, there's no way to use a AA injector (you can still use downsampling though).
Graphics: 4/10 - The lack of AA doesn't allow me to see the game's full potential here.
Sound: 7.9/10  - Although they are not outstanding quality-wise, the dialogue lines are extremely funny as so are the sound effects. The music is a little annoying, but it's a matter of taste.
Gameplay: 10/10 - You can blow worms, make them drown, punch them in the face, burn them, etc, all with flawless gameplay, big weapon variety, destructible environment and guaranteed laughs.
Environment: 9/10 - The environment is completely destructible, there's a nice map selection available and a map editor. The water available is also very useful and well made. The background animations also make the soldiers really look like worms, in previous worms games I always felt like they were giant mutant worms.
Final result: 7.7/10 - As I stated before I cannot recommend this game to everyone due to the lack of AA in AMD cards. There are lots of people who are really engaged into the "graphics war" and if one of these people buy this game and have an AMD graphics card they'll be nothing short of frustrated. If you have a Nvidia card or just don't care for heavy aliasing this is an awesome title to get.

I bought this game since I am a huge fan of McMillen's previous games. I spent a lot of time playing and completing everything in Super Meat Boy, so when I heard about a new platformer I got really excited, and I think a lot of people will be in the same situation.
It's important to understand that while they both are hardcore platformers, they are quite different. The End is Nigh is set in a semi-open world and each "level" is connected with another, compared to the "world-by-world" setup of Super Meat Boy. Sometimes you'll have to go back to another level to access a secret or another path, which make it really interesting.
Also interesting that there isn't any bosses, which to me was both a pro and con. Meat Boy had some great bosses ideas, but most of them could be rendered trivial due to the limited options related to being a two-button platformer, so not having those kind of fights between worlds felt like a good idea to keep the rythme of the game.
The level-design is rich, and you never really get to grow tired of a specific mechanic as new ones are introduced regularly. Since you don't get any "upgrade", the level-design will dictate your possibilities, and I feel like you get a linear progression that is extremely rewarding.
Lots of different worlds will help with the basic story-telling of the game, but don't expect too much bare a couple cinematics and some hidden text. It's a gameplay-first kind of game.
Talking about that, it's pleasing graphically and the animations are really fluid, which should be no surprise to those who played Super Meat Boy. They know how to make a platformer feel great.
I personally finished the main-levels but still have a lot to discover, which again is kind of the trademark of McMillen's games.
All in all, get this game if you want a challenging but rewarding experience that feels good to play, and have the patience to accept thousands of deaths. It's a steal for this price and one of the best platformer I ever played.

This expansion to the original Half Life puts you in the shoes of shepard, a Marine sent to Black Mesa to detain Gordon Freeman. But as anyone who has played the original knows, anything that can go wrong will go wrong, and things go to hell pretty quickly. The main draw of this is a new capaign, new areas, new weapons, and some new mechanics like a grappling hook and squad commands. The game succeeds in new areas and new weapons, with a much needed sniper rifle and hevay machine gun, as well as a few alien weapons rounding out Shepard's arsenal. I'm not sure how successful it is with the new mechanics though. The grappling hook, made from a detached Barnacle, works very well, but rope climbing and swinging feels wonky at best. Squad AI is extremely basic and they frequently get in the way more than they help, but they're useful if for no other reason than drawing enemy fire while you blast away at the myriad creatures you'll be facing, including some now aliens and Black Ops soldiers who have been sent in to clean this messy situation up. Not perfect, but pretty solid, even if the ending boss fight feels basic and the ending itself underwhelming.
Even in alpha this game has captivated me for longer than my time says. I look forward to future updates and seeing where this game goes

If you're looking for a roguelike type game, you could do a lot worse.
This one isn't great, but I have to give em points for a fairly neat concept - a 2.5D game that feels a bit like Diablo, but every time you die, the dungeon resets (and no, I'm not referring to Diablo III, get that out of your head, I refer to the first game here). It's got the same idea as the Cathedral.
The controls are... um... awful. I hate to say it, but they just straight up are. I wouldn't really want to play this with a keyboard. I've played games of a 'certain type' which have better controls than this. The only way I can describe the combat, is like if you took Super Smash, and then made it really really really goddamn slow, took out sprinting, and then made it awful to boot. Now, to be as specific as possible when explaining the controls, it feels unresponsive because of all the animations, and the way that animations differ in speed wildly all on the same character is utterly bizarre.
Let me explain. So the first character you have, she has a sword. She has a few abilities, one of which is an uppercut, which is executed extremely quick. Her basic attacks are slow as hell. Her fireball is molasses by comparison, and same with her spin attack. She plays like Link from Smash, basically, but somehow worse.
The combat is just tolerable. It's not fun. That's what drags this game down. It's just, mash your attack button, or spam your specials, and hope the enemy dies. You can't really play this on a fightstick, it's not that kind of game. It's like a... brawler. So I need to use my DS3 or whatever. And that sucks, because even then the control scheme is awful. So many wasted buttons.
I have seen enough games done right to sort of judge the storyline and atmosphere as average at best. Pretty stock standard stuff, "I'm gonna save the world" and all that. Not in so few words, but that's what it boils down to. The graphics are pretty awful for the Unreal Engine in 2014 - I've definitely seen better.
The soundtrack is... not that great. People like it, eh, it's alright. It's about as passable as everything else in this game.
All in all though, I still can recommend this game. It's not a bad game, by any stretch of the imagination, it's just... okay.
If you can pick it up on the cheap, maybe give it a go if you're really a die-hard roguelike fan.

Squad is a PVP, semi mil-sim game; that stands somewhere between Battlefield and Arma 3.
My experiences and opinion are about alpha 8.8 (and around that release), and you have to take into consideration that my primary role is medic. Also, I was a squad leader level backer, so I sunk some more hours into the non-steam versions. I'm going to update my review in the future if things change significantly.
Things I like
- More realistic than Battlefield.
- Faster than Arma 3.
- Teamwork and communication are encouraged by the community.
- Runs quite well. (note, I'm playing on 1080 with tons of ram)
- Looks nice (especially after patch 8).
- It's a blast to play with a good squad leader.
- Base building is fun.
Things I dislike
- Complete lack of player customization, you are locked to one weapon and loadout based on your role in the squad. It would be significantly better to have fewer roles, but being able to customize each loadout a bit. Few weapons to choose from, optics, grenades, etc. Just like in real-life, wherein some armies, soldiers are allowed to customize their gun.
- Can't pick up weapons or drive captured enemy vehicles.
- Can't drag drowned people out of harm's way.
- No helicopters.
- Vehicle physics are oversimplified.
- Sometimes it's hard to find a good squad leader.
- Lots of people become squad leaders, who are clearly not meant for the job.
- Some squad leaders tend to push their bad decisions on their squad mates, even if it's clearly their fault.
- No destruction.
- No doors.
- Around certain hours, there is only one Australian server, and it's either full or empty, so I have to jump on US servers.
- Night maps are awful without the equipment to improve visibility. Like night visions or flares.
- Base building is finicky and finding the right spot for digging can be annoying.
- Bandaging doesn't work sometimes, and people transport randomly around after reviving.
- There isn't an ammo bearer role.
- It's hard to play together with friends; no lobby system whatsoever.
- No silencers.
- Stances are limited, and it is inconvenient to shoot over cover. Either you are exposing too much by not standing up, or you end up hitting the edge while crouching. Arma 3 is far superior in this aspect.
- No zeroing.
Note, I totally understand that some of the things I dislike are there because of balance decisions, but I keep my right to disagree with those.
So, as you would expect, I won't recommend the game in its current state for 40 USD. If you can pick it up for 10-15 bucks, then go for it, give it a go. Otherwise, wait for the full release.
Alternatively, you can also go for Arma 3, which is a way more fleshed out game, and a more serious mil-sim, even with all of its problems (performance, and awful movement system).
----
There is something else I want to mention. As a (semi) mil-sim, Squad tends to give their players a sense of superiority over other games, which clearly shows in the reviews. My favorite phrase is, "if you don't want to play in a team, go for CS:GO or Battlefield." I always have a good laugh at these people. :)

Did you notice the 'Rogue-like' tag on the store page? i did not. So i thought this was a story driven beat em up game  just like earlier ACE team made Zeno clash games (awesome games btw) but now as a platformer. Well it really is a Rogue-like game and a very unique one.
Is it any good? Depends. It is very hard. frustrating in fact. rage quits are never far away. But at the same time it got a very unique recipe for making you come back and have some more punishment.
Unique. That's the word i will use to describe this game.  Everything about it is unique. I dont think i have ever played a rogue-like game that takes it's combat system from a real beat em up game and mixes it with flowing game play such as Dust:Elysian Tail. But unlike Dust in this game it is not possible to just mash the buttons and get a good combo. Getting 'in to the flow' in fights and timing are essential. Also getting the proper moves and really getting into things like 'juggling' or 'teching' or 'normal attack cancel into a special move' -stuff.
Sound too much like a beat em up? Well no it's not that but you will need to learn these things. vice versa just being good at Rogue games will not cut it. But if you like Rogue games then this game will provide you with a nice challenge with it's learning curve so fans of both genres should at least check this game out.
Be patient. Thats the one advice i give on this game. Be patient and learn. read guides if you must and train with the training doll.

TLDR:
Very short game (4hrs or less) with great astetics and premise but an end result that is not worth the price. Consider only  if it is on sale by 75% or more, you like linear dungeon crawlers and
if you own a controller. Otherwise stay clear.
Full review:
First of all, no, this is not a non recommendation due to the controls as it seems to be the case for a lot of other Steam reviews for this game. I actually found the controls to be pretty good and easy to learn ON A CONTROLLER (do NOT play this game otherwise, it IS a nightmare to play using the keyboard).
Gameplay is pretty interesting, mainly thanks to the movement and attack controls which make even the very first enemies you encounter a decent challenge. However it can also get a bit too repetitive when most of the enemies follow a very similar pattern and you can even do the same tactics to defeat them, even to the point where you can stun-lock them on endless grab-throw moves ("final boss" included).
I really love the asthetics and theme of this game, the artwork and spine-chill lovely music really gave me the good old Castlevania vibes. Even the voice acting feels like top quality with its few dialogues (that guitar playing skelleton chilling = GG).
The big negative point why I cant really recommend this game, is the fact it is very, VERY short. Barely 4 hours in, as a below average skill player and I already cleared the 3 entrances to the Abyss, unlocked the 3 playable characters and gathered pretty much all of the "journal pages". There is nothing left to do other than probably try get a couple achievements if I was ever interested on those.
Another letdown is that while the game presents you with what could be a very complex and interesting developing story about the origin of the abyss and of the characters you play as, it ends up being mostly told on the previously mentioned journal texts you can find after killing enemies and from what little dialogue there is each time you reach the Warlock. You kill the final boss and what do you get?
Nothing more, regardless of how many times you do it.
If you see this game super cheap (75% discount or so), you feel like playing a very linear dungeon crawler and you own a controller, I'd say go for it and give it a try not expecting much, I had fun playing it but its flaws really outweight the good stuff unfortunately and at this price, there are a lot of far better games out there.

So lets start with the good why don't we.
This game looks beautiful, it absolutely does. It's colorful, pleasant to look at and the animations are nothing short of great. You won't get tired of listening to the music either. Although the design of the enemies is not the best.
The story is really interesting, it seems like it is a twist on a story from the 1890's but I wouldn't know. For me it was really unique and the presentation of it all was one of the things that kept me interested although it had a rather abrupt ending that leaves little to no closure but aside from that the game being roguelike, the respawns, the monsters and pretty much everything is explained by the nature of the story. They all mix together nicely. There's some decent voice acting as well. .
The combat... Here is what a lot of people have a problem with. I think it's because they go into the game expecting something else. The game includes 3 characters, 2 of which are unlockable. One fast character, one slow heavy hitter and one with a crazy reach.
You can have up to 3 specials with each character and there are 5 in total for each one.  You can bind each special to whichever direction you want, front, up or down
The combat system is based around cancels. Canceling your current move / animation to do a fast combo, canceling from normal to special to dodge etc. You can have up to 3 cancel points which act like stamina. There's also a block and grab button, the grab ignores the enemy block. You can upgrade specials with up to 3 different traits. One for defence, extra damage and mana regeneration. When the mana bar is full you can do a seal attack and the enemies you hit will be marked. If you defeat them in time and if you are on the same level as them you can capture them and turn into them. Here is where the game shines the most for me. Each and every enemy you encounter, bosses included, is playable each with their own skillset. It's amazing and there's a decent enemy variety.
I personally love all of it. The mechanics are robust and the controls are responsive.
The AI. So when you first play this game you will get your butt kicked in and you will be so frustrated you will want to punch a hole through your monitor. Fear not, it does get better, although you will have to read a couple of guides. This should never be the case but the tutorial and in-game guide are not good at all. There IS a trainning mode where you can experiment at your own pace though.
It will seem like they are reacting based on what button you just pressed but it really is just AI done right. With time you will get better and you will feel good about overpowering it. Some people though give up from the first hour and write a negative review on steam :lol:
The platforming. There's a certain degree of challenge to be found in the platforming elements as well. Lots of traps which you can use in your advantage in fights as well. The procedural generation is done really well. With most dead ends leading to trasure / check points and sometimes secret "doors".
So the actual bad of the game
The multiplayer. Now there are 2 modes. The coop and the fighting mode which acts as a regural fighting game with each person having 2 characters. That mode works as intended for the most part but the coop is buggy as hell. If you actually manage to get through the connection lost errors you will encounter the following:
Your character level resetting to lvl 1. Don't worry it's only for the game session (not working as intended)
Knocked down and not being able to get up.
A looooot of lag.
SHARED CAMERA. IT'S GREAT WHEN YOU FALL IN A PIT AND YOU CAN'T SEE WHERE YOU ARE (working as intended)
At least there's local coop as well... Plug in a second controller and play with a friend of yours.
Also the game comes with it's fair share of crashes. Mainly when you alt tab and tab back in but it's not a big deal.

A philosophical exploration of the freewill/obedience paradox of the judeo-christian herritage. Oh, and it's robots and lasers too.
This is a puzzle game dealing with gates, switches, blocks and lots of the usual mechanics -- nothing too inventive here, but not bad either. Most were pretty simple, although a few at the end took some time. Finding all the hidden stars was a little tricky, although just being unsure where to look was frustrating at times. I got a list of which maps they were in, so I wasn't combing 8 puzzles looking for a single star, and I felt it was better that way.
The game also has a strong metaphysical/ethical element. Most of that's pretty good, but a little pointed if you're from a religious background. It's certainly not a game I could've played in my parent's living room back when I was growing up. There are some moments when you're in dialogs with an AI, and you have to have philosophical discussions by picking from a list of preset dialog options. Those will probably look familiar to those with formal philosophy training, and feel restrictive to those who's philosophical beliefs can't be neatly divided into one of six options.
Overall though, I enjoyed the game. I realize the religious themes will make it inaccessable to some, but I'd still recommend it to those who don't feel threatened by alternate viewpoints. And you have to be cool with avoiding killbot turrets.
