A monumental success such as Half Life is bound to spawn sequels. And rest assured, in 1999 "Opposing Force" saw the light of day.
  This praised expansion pack features the same timeline as the original, and once again obliges you roam the halls of Black Mesa. This time from a different perspective, and a different set of eyes. Adrian Shephard, a U.S. Marine, is deployed on a confidential mission. Ignorance is bliss, perhaps, as he is de facto part of an operation whose main objective is to silence any civilian survivors in an desperate attempt to ameliorate the damage of the Resonance Cascade. For good or bad, the plan doesn't go accordingly. Shephard's transport aircraft gets promptly shot down in the vicinity of the research facility, putting an abrupt end to his escapades. Or rather; that would be the case, hadn't a certain quick-witted scientist assisted you with first aid. The mute protagonist seemingly dismisses the scientist's courageous act, hastily setting out to locate the crash site. At the wreckage, an advantageously placed radio informs the Corporal that the military forces are abandoning the area. And thus begins; not a heroic quest to save the day; but rather, a struggle for survival.
  And what a struggle. A new alien species: "Race X" – in addition to Xen – apparently took advantage of the dimensional tears and invaded Black Mesa simultaneously. This highly intelligent breed has mastered the technology of teleportation; and is masterminded by the Gene Worm. Luckily, once again our combatant is armed to the teeth, featuring an impressive array of firearms. And, once again, he is not afraid to use them...
is similar to the original Half-Life in terms of gameplay and setting, but personally, I found the levels to be more atmospheric and better in layout. Most of the elements that was cherished from the forerunner made a comeback, even expanding on concepts, making them better. The AI deserves an honorable mention here. Even though clunky at times, surrounding soldiers and personnel have a bigger impact then ever. The Medics, indicated by their white bandeau, have expertise in first aid, consequently allowing them to heal wounded soldiers. One might argue the Engineers are even more fundamental, as they grant you a pass through locked doors. These computer-controlled units were certainly ahead of their time and brings a new dimension to the gameplay. Yet, it is still impossible to derive from the fact that this extension is rather brief. Clocking in at about five hours, this add-on could be fully experienced in an afternoon. Though it's worth noting that the levels were remarkedly more demanding - playing a higher difficulty will permit you a few more hours of entertainment. Although, what it may lack in depth or sheer length, it makes up for in almost every other aspect. Opposing Force set a new benchmark for what to expect from expansion packs and add-ons.

Right off the bat, Dark Messiah makes me question the simplistic nature of all combat in the Elder's Scrolls games. One thing is clear, though. Dark Messiah is a PC game, meant for gamers rather than mainstream turkies (gobble gobble!).
Comparisons aside, this game has its moments but the AI is rather simplistic. Combine this with highly linear mapping and progression, and you have something very close to a late 90's-early 2000's, relic. Still, the distinction between the "classes" is well done. Magic, however, is feeble through most of the game without certain gameplay "tweaks". Typical really, as most devs have little vision for such things. Once you get a certain upgrade, however, you become untouchable. That's abstinent, rudimentry balancing if I ever saw it. The main problem lies with the adrenaline system and why magic had to be tied to it.
Like most medieval-based games of this nature, Dark Messiah is catered primarily towards fans of swords, shields, and gimmicky action. I will say they did a good job of it, though. Progression and mapping may be simple, but the environment itself can be a lethal weapon. Magic may be feeble, but it's done just well enough to be enjoyable.

Nice blend of roguelike, platformer and beatemup genres. You are able to capture defeated enemies' souls and play as those creatures yourself switching between them and your main char on the go giving you immense tactical possibilities.  Yes, ALL of the enemies in the game have a full arsenal of standard, forward, high, low, jump etc attacks in both fast+weak and slow+strong variations. Dashes, grabs, rolls, blinks, magic projectiles, spinning AOE and vomiting poison make combat both varied and challenging.
Unfortunately, all this gorgeousness comes at a price: instead of Metroidvania-styled gameplay Abyss Odyssey is way too much linear and kinda lacks other content. The whole game is just a succession of randomly-generated beutiful 'biome' arenas that consist of a single vertically-oriented long corridor with a few dead end branches that have loot in them. More often than not when you reach a predetermined point in the arena enemies just spawn offscreen and you are locked in a small 1-2 screen sized battleground until you defeat them or die trying sorta JRPG-style. Apart from that and a handful of NPCs that train you or sell you stuff there is nothing to interact with. Don't get me wrong, Streets of Rage+Megaman roguelike is a welcome thing, but i'd prefer a +5-10$ in a price tag and a bit more content to deepen gameplay a bit (DLC maybe?).
As for drawbacks, kb+mouse controls were a bit clunky, but now devs seem to have fixed everything and I was able to beat the game fwo times out of three tries while I haven't been able to beat it even once before due to unresponsive controls so I got rekt in harder levels because of slow character response. Also devs got a tiny bit lazy and out of a few dozens of enemy types (ALL PLAYABLE!) a couple are just a reskinned or posessed versions of your own characters, doubling as minibosses every now and then, but there is a good variation of unique bosses too though so it's not that bad.
All in all a nice game i'd recommend.

Yeah, this hit all the right buttons for me.
Abyss Odyssey is a beat 'em up game with fighting game mechanics and loot grabbing - it has platform levels that change every playthrough, loaded with traps and secret rooms.
Bad- controls are wonky. it's set up to attack left and you have to face right again and then press right to go in that direction. Some of the characters are limited because they are too big for an area or, in the case of the first soldier, cannot climb walls at certain heights. It's pretty flawed in these specific control problems. Most people cannot overlook this (thus the mixed Steam reviews) and I don't blame them.
Good - but what shines in this game is the art, animation and design. The whole drips with polish and satisfying visuals in the art style of Art Nouveau masters like Mucha. The characters are strange and interesting with amazing movesets and fantastic animations - some of the pick-up enemies are more fun to play than the three main characters! The story is facinating Chilean myth with a bizarre twist that makes the mood eerie and one of a kind.
Basically, if the controls were patched, this would be one of my favorite games, no doubt about it.

This is the most incredible 2d platformer I've ever played.
Too many people getting upset and leaving negative reviews because they lack the patience and skill it takes to conquer a challenging platformer just tells me you're not good enough.
This is not Super Meat Boy, so don't bother calling it "Super Meat Boy 2". This game's leaps and bounds ahead of SMB, and I loved Meat Boy.
The fact that you run at a consistent speed is a positive and the fact that you cannot wall jump lets the levels be as creative with ledges and mechanics as possible.
This game is much more technical, mechanical, and pure as a platformer than Super Meat Boy which is simply a bad game compared to The End Is Nigh.
Pros
- Simple yet complex, this game has fall control, ledge manipulation, multiple jump heights and 2+ ways to jump off ledges.
- Certain levels like 'SS Exodus' feature objects with physics that are super fun to play around.
- Secrets and collectibles that are way more satisfying and challenging than collecting stale bandages.
- Non-linear open-world platforming which is far less boring than the stage-by-stage snoozefest that was Meat Boy.
- Challenging learning curve and challenging "retro" levels that require practicing and learning to gain mastery of the level.
- NPC's scattered around levels with interesting dialogue, behind a challenging way to reach some of them, of course.
- Some of the most clever and challenging level design in a 2d game.
- Many different enemy types to challenge you with their own strengths and weaknesses to learn and conquer.
- Tyler Glaiel is the best programmer yet. Day one, this man was fixing bugs and patching the game, there's been almost 10 updates and this game has been out only for 4 days.
- Edmund McMillen games are always extremely creative and interesting, lore-wise.
- Best music in any Edmund McMillen game.
Cons
- None I can think of at the moment...yeah, none.
Get The End Is Nigh. It's worth it.

My first review dedicated to my favorite game of all time. Yes, you most likely know where this is going already. Let me tell you exactly why this game deserves your attention.
The most common thing i hear about this game is "It reminds me of Portal" While it certainly does share the same genre, this game is doing its own thing. Its unique. Not only does it deliver brain teasing puzzles, but it also makes you think about your own morals, belief and even life, whenever you put the game back down. If you ever wanted to go down the philosopher's path, then this game is for you.
Pros:
- The game makes you think out of the box (litterally)
- Great narration from start to finish.
- Exploring is rewarded with collectibles that requires you to solve extra puzzles.
- The soundtrack is beyond amazing and really fits into the world. (may i suggest you buy that as well)
- The puzzles are fairly easy at the start so give it a chance, but an hour or two into the game you find yourself with very challenging puzzles thats really going to test your skills.
- The game will make you question your own morals and beliefs.
- The DLC is 100% recommended. Its still the same concept as the main game, but with more story packed into more than 6 hours of extra gameplay.
- A sequel is announced, and i will sell my soul if i have to, so i can get to play it.
- Its on sale often, which kind of annoys me because this game is worth every penny at the original amount.
Cons:
- I think they need to smooth out the difficulty a little bit during the start. It feels way to easy and it might turn players off who are looking for a challenge.
- Had some minor frame rate issues here and there, but nothing that didn't go away after a couple of seconds and it was only in the "hub" area.
- The collectibles are a little too hard to find sometimes, i doubt anyone managed to do it without cheating (i know i didnt) and that kind of ruins the experience.
- More variety in the worlds. The concept of the game gives the developers complete freedom in terms of world design, but they kept it very "standard". The "wow factor" happened, but not enough. I hope this will change in the next game.
All in all, a beautiful game with an amazing soundtrack and narration that really draws you into the world. It deserves all the praise its getting. If you were ever looking for something to spend some money on, you have come to the right place. You wont regret buying this game, neither at the original amount or on sale. Personally i felt bad buying it on sale after i played it, but thats just me.

There is an unusually large discrepancy for this game in regards to the critic versus consumer level reviews. It's a fantastic game where, when faced with several appointments at once, the primary factor in your survival is how foolhardy you are. Do you have audacity? Often it's your only chance, but it'll be your downfall too. To me, that's how being surrounded by a group of armed men should feel. Systematically killing them doesn't make sense - either you manage to immediately try to shift  the odds more in your favor somehow or you're dead. Throwing pots, ropes, kicking, pushing, trying  oh so desperately not to get flanked, other? I've only played two other games that are satisfying in this regard (on Hard at least). Dishonored (made by the developers of Dark Messiah) and Chivalry: Medieval Warfare. Winning when you're attacked by other players 3v1 in Chivalry feels absolutely fantastic. But anyways, as far as PvE combat goes, Dark Messiah is great. The story line isn't fantastic, it's not a free roaming RPG, and you might like to make more RPG choices. But the game has excellent combat, a comfortably earthy fantasy tone, and the level design is good (with the exception of too many spikes wall things - too many damn spikes).

When it comes to survival/base-building games this has got to be one of the best. I've been playing for a number of betas at this point and RimWorld just keeps surpassing expectations and hope with every patch. The game can be brutal. Your survivors can die on a whim but it'll always be enjoyable. The Storyteller AI is always there to keep you interested. It'll deliver blow after blow only to offer a sweet balm before it swoops in for the kill. Clever play and a little luck and you'll be able to build a bustling encampment only to watch it all come down in flames and tears. And let's not even get started on the massive modding scene this game has. You will almost literally never run out of stuff to do.
Play this game. You won't regret it.

This game is great in so many ways.
I originally held of playing this for... whatever reason, and I regret not getting into it faster because this game blew away my low expectations 10 minutes into the game.
When it comes to games like this, I.E a lot of time spent walking... and talking, voice acting is almost at the top of the pillar of importance for me.
This game absolutely nailed the voice acting. It is superb. All of the characters have very unique and specific personalities and all the voice actors perfectly expressed it, it all felt genuine, I felt real emotion. 10/10 voice acting.
The soundtrack isn't something I absolutely loved but it was far from bad, some songs where great and the rest was just OK. It is a VHS Synth-Pop style soundtrack.
The art-style of this game is very different to most, if not all games. The art mixed with the 2.5D game is a great combo.
Great art direction.
Graphics are great, ran smoothly throughout my entire gameplay.
Controls are also smooth, and simplistic.

I sorta wish they had gone with one of those, preferably mouse-only.

Oxenfree is a true 'choices matter' game. Choices you make has impact on the game later, whether that be small flavour stuff,  dialogues with characters or relationship changes. For better or worse?
That's your choice.
All characters, as previously mentioned when I talked about voice acting, have their own unique personalities.
Not going to spoil as to which character has what personality, I think you should discover that for yourself while playing the game. But who ever worked on the character writing did a very good job.
The story is indeed a big mystery and gets weirder and weirder the more and more you play.
Has a ton of weird turns and the ending was fantastic(keep in mind there are multiple endings; I.E Choices Matter).
The game, at least with me, draws you in emotionally, whether that is negative emotions you have towards a character or positive feelings towards another.
The game draws you in emotionally in many different ways at the same time.
The music may perfectly fit the scenery and a major event may just have happened in the story etc...
The gameplay is not complicated but keeps you invested.
This game has replay-ability the same way
has replay-ability.
You can replay the game to take a different path of choices, to discover more or complete more achievements.
This game is tagged as a horror game.
It is not. It is also tagged as psychological horror, which it is.
It is an ominous, Lovecraftian mystery thriller with psychological horror.
It is not horror in the sense of jump scares, being chased by a boogeyman etc...

The Wolfenstein saga was my first true FPS, my department head at the college I was attending in 1993 passed the shareware version to me and I was hooked. This chapter of the game is the most heart rending story of the FPS world to date. The look at the realities of war and how people are ground up by the ambitions of those who are "protected" from the violence and make the rules is very true to life in my humble opinion. The action is intense and the choices made during the game play effect the outcome and is in effect 2 different games depending on the choice made in a pivotal point of the game.
In spite of the serious natter of the story line, I really had fun with it. The inclusion of the mini games of the original Wolfenstein 3D were a really fun, and brought back great memories of playing it when it was new. It really shows just how far the game world has progressed since the first 3D shooters began.
The game is not for the squeamish or faint of heart and definitely not for young children. Some of the cut scenes are adult in nature and quite well done.
If you are a fan of FPS this is a must have to add to your collection.

The Talos Principle is a truly excellent first person puzzler that deserves to be in the same tier as the portal games when it comes to this genre.
The Talos Principle is set in a world comprising of regions from antiquity (Ancient Egypt, Ancient Greece and what appears to be Medieval Western Europe) and follows the narrative that you are a servant doing the bidding of God, who goes by the name of Elohim. The backdrop to the game world is one of existentialism and philosophy. The game is full of thought provoking dialogue, discussing the nature of self, intelligence and life. Despite being made by completely different companies and teams, I find this game to be a spiritual companion to SOMA, particularly in terms of the subject matter discussed. The journey of following this philosophical narrative drives the storyline of the game (of this I shall refrain from saying more due to spoilers) and really immerses oneself in the absolutely beautifully designed game world. There were many times where I would just stop and admire the scenery.
As I just touched upon, graphically this game is gorgeous (and naturally a little demanding on the system) and the art direction is one of 'ultra realistic'. The audio design accompanying this is also beautiful, with a fully realised aural ambience accompanying you throughout the game, from Elohim's booming voice to the sound of insects hiding in the foliage. Game controls were perfectly smooth and intuitive. Basic FPS controls, nothing to complain about here.
Overall, I found the end product to be overwhelmingly engaging, intelligent and just flat out well put together. A lot of attention to detail, from even the gameplay settings menu (they have motion sickness options!) to the textures employed in creating the world. The story narrative is one of the best I have come across, and many of the puzzles that help to drive this are very challenging. By the time I had completed The Talos Principle, I felt like I had been on a journey. And perhaps I was a tiny bit wiser for it.

Ok so it feels like a pretty sweet side-scrolling RPG. You jump around, you stab things, and it feels like it should except for the fact the levels all look the same when you're in the same theme.

I assume this becomes less of an issue as you level up but it's incredibly annoying to find a couple of good items and a new weapon and POOF. You lose. That's the first.
The second and worst part of this game is the multiplayer option. The game feels ok when you're alone but woe to those who have a friend or anyone else join in. Even worse in the multiplayer is TEAM HITTING! You're using swords in a small area fighting swathes of enemies. Great concept, but too many things holding it back.
Abyss Odyssey has many things going for it: interesting story, nice graphics, an encapsulating theme. Unfortunately, it just doesn't feel right when you play it.
Tutorial: the tutorial is very sparse. Sure it shows you what it wants you to do, but doesn't tell you the right inputs to do them, or the intricacies, like the difference between double jumping when facing a wall vs not facing the wall, or even wall slides. They don't teach you what number button quaffs what potion.
Controls: The default controls are garbage, and should be reconfigured. Further, the tutorial doesn't really help you choose what suitable inputs should be. Ultimately, this leads to a lot of frustration for a player who want to just pick up and play.
Combat: Combat feels a little clunky. It's slowed down in the interest of making combos, but it feels unresponsive at times. The AI doesn't have large enough tells. You would expect that weak enemies would have obvious precursors to their attacks, as would strong enemies' strong attacks, but many of the attack animations appear quickly and often seem uninterruptable.
Lack of instruction is a problem here a well: There isn't any instruction as to how to combo. New players are left frustrated as the AI pile on multi hit attacks, while they are stuck with a basic 2 hit combo. Nothing tells players that the timing of the block matters in terms of breaking combos and counter-attacking.
I disliked being constrained into artificial combat areas to fight particular non-boss enemies. It seemed unnecessary, particularly when they were already using a key system as a gateway.
Also, being limited to fighting 1-3 enemies at a time was disappointing. I never felt overwhelmed by enemies, though at the beginning I did feel overpowered by them. Also, the enemies would often just stand still, waiting for your attacks! I felt as if I went to the bathroom and came back, the enemies would still be there waiting for me to make a move.
Death Mechanic: Personally I liked the death mechanic of having a second chance, with a weaker character until you could find a revive spot.
Environments: The levels are procedurally generated. Overall they felt luxurious, but sparse to me. I feel like there was a lot of wasted real estate, which could have been filled with smaller enemies. Unfortunately, the game seemed to want to focus on fighting one or two enemies at a time.
The relatively linear exploration was somewhat disappointing to me as well.
Inventory: You are allowed 1 weapon, 1 of each type of accessory, 1 soul transformation. If you want something else in a slot, you have to throw your current item away, and can't even sell it to a merchant. Very arcade video gamey, but not something I desire for a regular game. Would much rather have had a configurable inventory so I could switch swords.
Plot: The fight seemed inconsequential after your first death. You die, you get reincarnated. Simple. What were the soldiers fighting for? Why didn't they just stay home and avoid the abyss, only guarding the exits? Were the monster's stealing children,♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥women, setting fires? Nah, the soldiers just wanted to commit suicide by jumping into an abyss to fight said monsters. A lot of wasted potential here.
Overall, this is a game with a lot of potential if you can get into it. However, it's lack of instruction, odd difficulty curve, slower combat system, and lack of drive will make it meh to most players.

Want to love this game, I really do. The combat feels great, shooting is solid. The movement is tight and mastering parkour is very rewarding. So why is no one playing it, why are queues so long?
The main issue with this game for me is the randomness of loadouts. There is too much RNG in what items you end up equipped with. You win a loot-card that has a main-hand, sidearm, and melee weapon. Each of those items can be completely different. Then you have up to 3 traits on each card as well. On top of that you have different tiers of cards, this recipe ends up leaving you with a lottery based reward system that I would consider a disaster.
The abysmally low currency gain you get from actually playing the game compounds the issue. No doubt it was an economic decision from someone over on the Production/Development team to leave players in a constant grind or starved for currency. The whole point of the game is to push you towards micro-transactions. Micro-transactions fuel your crafting and crafting lets you take a stab at the lottery system to end up with that 1/10000 perfect loadout.
You are forever chasing that dragon, it may as well be some kind of drug. Leaves me really disappointed, I think the characters have a lot of heart and the maps are fun, but these people have killed their own game with the money making model. Also, it takes way too long to actually get into a game. Work on the down-time.

Squad is an excellent shooter for anyone who is interested in more intense and challenging combat gameplay.
Obviously the comparasion to Project Reality BF:2 is apt, being a spiritual successor to it. If you liked the gameplay and experience of PR then I think you will find comfort in the familiarity of Squad. As of now it doesn't have the extent of vehicles and equipment that PR has, but all of that is coming along down the road. If you really only care about a true combined arms experience such as PR offers, I would reccomend you sit on this one until those features are rolled out completely.
I have found the gameplay of Squad to be some of the best I have seen in terms of more realistic shooters. The gunplay and movment is still somewhat unpolished, but doesn't feel super janky and robotic. The maps are well detailed and the game looks visually impressive. So far the mechanics of the game have done a great job at aiding and encouraging teamplay over lone wolfing.
The relative lack of forced structure allows for it to stay new and fresh every time I play. Despite being on the same maps every engagment is different. There is never a point where it feels like everytime I'm just fighting in the same spot doing the same thing over and over.
If you love team oriented shooters and want some realism and itensity I cannot reccomend this game enough. The developers have also been really great at communicating and regularly releasing fixes and new content updates.

This is the definitive next generation MOBA. The gameplay mechanics are so on par and not only make the game more fun, but also keeps the game way less toxic compared to other MOBAs I've played in the past, such as DOTA and League.
The heroes don't feel like cookie cutter generic "insert name and price tag here" characters. Each one looks different, sounds different, and plays different. With the huge variety in the game from all the heroes (with more to come), every match is filled with intense action, as I always have to figure out a new strategy so that my main MLG 360 Crow Scoper (a.k.a Rook) can wreck.
CSing is shared between players, so people actually work together in order for both of them to boost their CS, which is great. Kills and Assists are generally weighed the same, so supports get all the love too now. Unlike League where you've got to wait all day for your Sona to get your Ardent Censer up and running, you'll be able to get all the items you need for your support character just as you would with any other character.
Overall, the community (although somewhat small) isn't toxic at all. I've yet to come across a single toxic player throughout my matches, and I know that it says I've only played about an hour at the time of writing this, but I've invested at least 50 hours into this game before it released on Steam.
The game also rewards you for playing with 1 Gem per match, so over time you can buy a free skin or an account boost, which is a great thing that the devs did.

Borderlands is a game that plays very similarly to Call of Duty in the controls department, however, nothing like it at all in the actual gameplay. Unless you're gonna be nitpicky and say "hurr it's a shooter." Borderlands features unique classes with their own personalities, a VERY large array of guns and weaponry to use, from a basic pistol to an SMG that shoots 4 bullets per round fired that light people on fire. The possibilities are endless. Oh, and you loot stuff too. See an enemy? Blast his face off and steal his gun. You can then use it, or sell it to a vending machine (Yeah, i don't understand either). Absolutely Recomended. The Talos Principle is probably my favourite puzzle game since the first Portal. That said, don't expect this game to be all too similar. There are some superficial similarities, such as an omnipotent robot voice in the sky, and discrete puzzle 'rooms', but the tone and style of puzzle are very different.
Unlike Portal, the puzzles in this game don't place much value on execution. If you can conceptualise the solution, you have it in the bag, regardless of your reflexes or skill at first person games. If you're ever stuck on a frustrating jump, you probably haven't considered some other piece of the puzzle.
The story part of the game is found through audio and text logs, as well as the robo-skygod talking to your character. No spoilers, but I found it well written, and absolutely worth hunting around for the odd hidden terminal.
Presentation is also top notch, with some great visuals and a great soundtrack. The game runs great on both my desktop and on my rickety old laptop with a 650m.
This game is a great sequel to Portal! Packed with hours of intense action and brain teasing puzzles it sure to make everyone think as hard as possible. Would recommend.

Kicking Orcs Off Ledges Simulator 2006 still stands up today as the ultimate kicking things off ledges experience.
There is more to it than just kicking, however. It plays sort of like Deus Ex in a fantasy world where a fragile coexistance between magic and the protagonist's omnipotent legs is begining to fray because of, like, some Necromancers or something. I forget. It doesn't really matter, does it? You don't buy simulators for rich storytelling, after all.
Anyway, the game gives you free reign to explore levels full of creatures to kick and things to kick them off of or into. Along the way you'll get some skill points to distribute. So, you'll get the opportunity to learn different types of magical spells, become an expert archer, or simply finish a BA in Orc Studies from the University of Ledges. You can shrink goblins and step on them, freeze surfaces and watch orcs slide off ledges without dirtying your boots,  or immerse yourself in the best first person swordplay out there.
However, this stuff is all secondary to the amazing power of the protagonist's legs. You could kick down the fourth wall and become demon emperor of the universe with those bad boys.

Read carefully.
Don't try overclocking unless you know what your hardware's limits are. Look up on Google what your Graphics Cards' Reference Clock is and check what reviewers have managed to clock it. If you try to clock it too high without knowing, you probably will fry your Tech.
These days our GPUs are built to downclock or crash if it reaches temps it's not built to withstand. But sometimes Volts arent counted into that failsafe, so you can/could kill your GPU that way.
Again, please. Make sure you know what the limit is before testing your new clocks. You don't know it, but you just might be overreaching and killing your cards...
But to those that DO know how to reach the limits with Software Overclocking: This is right up our alley.

Squad is an excellent shooter for anyone who is interested in more intense and challenging combat gameplay.
Obviously the comparasion to Project Reality BF:2 is apt, being a spiritual successor to it. If you liked the gameplay and experience of PR then I think you will find comfort in the familiarity of Squad. The game is good fun, but if you are looking for something that is hardcore and going to replace LoL/Dota 2 in the competitive scene, then this game is likely not for you.
To address the concerns that this game is pay to win: Simply put it isn't. As one of the negative reviewers state there is a a crafting system that allows you to get in-game advantages. Although this is true, the advantages are pretty slight and they are available to everyone at the cost of elixirs. You can create permanent crafting recipes with ELIXIRS alone. To whomever said Gems (the in game currency equivalent to Riot Points from LoL) were needed is incorrect. The only use for Gems are for cosmetic upgrades or unlocking pets early (which can be unlocked with the other currency for free eventually).
I feel as though many negative reviewers were either A) Looking for a replacement game for LoL/Dota 2, or B) are not interested in the MOBA scene at all. Although games can tend to drag early on in your Strife playing career, you will find games run shorter once you play with more experienced people as objective control allows for harder pushing and thus earlier game endings.
The biggest issue right now, in my opinion, is that lack of a champion pool. There are only about 30 champions and it isn't hard to go through them all quickly. If you do like to change up the champions you play each game, you will find you run out quickly. But if you (like me) prefer to stick to one role and choose from a small group of champions that fulfill that role, you will not be disappointed.
Another issue iI have is that the in game shop is cluttered and sometimes difficult to understand for new players. Although it is Early Access, I can only hope they fix this soon.
I welcome everyone interested in the MOBA genre to try the game before being completely deterred by the rage. If you are a MOBA fan you will find this game might be enough to keep you entertained when losing interest in other MOBAs.

A clunky fighter rogue-lite hybrid that, while decently fun despite he game handling like all your controller inputs were first translated by a monkey and then handed off the game developers who then decide whether or not your button press occurred or not, pretends to have much more depth on offer than it actually possesses. Collecting enemy souls isn't really that big of an appeal, they handle differently but each enemy type has one or two combos or moves that are just much better than the others and I find it difficult to want to invest time into learning how to handle this game knowing that my reward for high skill play is more monsters to learn.
Since the only thing you keep are levels and levels don't offer a significant enough increase from level to level the game feels the same the first time you beat and every time after that. You'll be strategically choosing monster souls based on what is and isn't good or what you do and don't know how to play which doesn't really encourage learning new ones even if the game throws a bonus stage with a random monster at you after every boss (actually this can be more annoying than exciting, having to learn a whole new moveset to fight a mob or two is actually pretty frustrating even if there isn't an actual penalty for losing.)
I want to like this game but the RPG and rogue-lite elements are limited, monster collecting doesn't appeal to me as it only serves to add a flimsy excuse to learn more about a game whose versus lobbies are deader than the extinct species list, and the storyline is only a bit interesting (less so when you realize you don't have any actual influence on it and reading about it doesn't actually give you any real benefit beyond a decently arranged story.) It's a decent game but it can only ever be decent when it is so riddled with flaws and the fact that the main menu contains an advertisement is just icing on the cake.
I can't recommend this purchase, I like it but it isn't where it would have to be for me to say you should pick this one up. If you really want to learn a clunky fighting game system so you can fight the same 12-15 enemies over and over then go right ahead but I'm not going to be the guy encouraging you to do it.

The End is Nigh a very great spiritual successor to Edmund McMillen and Team Meat's addicting Super Meat Boy.
Edmund McMillen and Tyler Glaiel's new beast of a game is one of my new favorites.
The objective of the game is to make a friend, and you do that by going through levels to find pieces of this friend. The story behind it, is gloriously macabre because the character you play as has nothing better to do since the apocalypse. You'll get a kick out of the cutscenes that play when you progress through the game because Ash is voiced by Rich Evans from Red Letter Media. The music is stellar thanks to Ridiculon, so no point in the game ever feels dull. The music matches the graphics, a grim world with our character going through a wide variety of settings and themes. All of the aesthetics of the game gets packed into this charming 2D HELL of a precision platformer.
The layout of the game is a open-world 2D platformer. The worlds interconnect, so there are many routes to take, nearly a hundred secrets and there's multiple endings. The game just won't stop coming at you just when you think you are done!
The worlds will challenge you, and you will die. The secrets in the worlds will challenge you further, and you will die more. The cartridges that can be found as secret collectibles you can play at home will definitely challenge you to your limit, you will never not die. 100%ing the entire game and getting all achievements is nearly impossible, but aiming to 100% a save file is doable. There's something that will get to you. One cartridge kept me from 100% for 6 hours. Doing that deathless is about double that practice.
The controls are smooth and tight at the same time. The mechanics can be quickly understood, but the true meat of the game lies with how advanced the movement can get. The option for speeding through the game dying as little as possible is on the table.
I can't get enough of this game, if 2D platformers appeal to you at all, this is a must. You might have a great time looking for tumors, or have a mind-boggling time seeing how deep this game goes.

TLDR; I absolutely love this gosh dang game
This game is just super amazing. Every single piece of it is polished to a tee.
The controls are tight and responsive. You are always in complete control and any mistake is your own. The jumps are smooth and the game quickly helps you understand how every jump feels. Even more responsive than Meat Boy, imo.
The visuals are fantastic. The platforms stand out well from the background, always making it clear where you have to go. The lines are smooth and the background design is lovely
THE MUSIC. I found Ridiculon's stuff in Isaac to be great, but nothing you would listen to out of the game. These tracks are straight up slamming and are definetely going onto my playlists.
The tumours and cartridges around the levels are a heap of fun to collect. They may takes hundreds of deaths sometimes. But that's OK, because the resets are quick and fluid, making sure you are right back into the action.
Unlike Edmund's previous platformer, this game has a more fluid level progress, allowing you to just breeze through all the gameplay, with no menuing to break up the action. The map design of this game also allows for little secret areas, which allow you to get more cartridges and tumours
If I had to have a gripe with this game, it would have to be how much info it gives on the controls. There are things that I had to discover myself that would have helped a lot more if I had found them 10 minutes earlier into the current screen.
Edmund has really outdone himself, making a Super Meat Boy for the (even more) modern gaming age. 10/10

I don't usually write reviews, but seeing that at the time I'm writing this the game's reviews on Steam are "Mixed" I feel the obligation to give you guys my opnion:
Man, do I love ACE Team games? And this one is no exception.  It's an action platformer that supports online co-op. The art style, the music, the setting, it's all gorgeous, even if the story might feel too simple. I noticed some people complaining the controls were clunky, I think that doesn't do this game justice at all. The controls do feel heavy, but it sounds to me clear as day that it was a design decision. They didn't want to make another generic action game, they want you to think before attacking. Also, there are some really neat mechanics that help the game to stand out even more among other similar titles. My favorite one being releasing a charged attack that lets you "capture" an enemy and use him as a playable character in the current run. You're probably gonna chance characters a lot when running out of life in the lower levels (forgot to mention this game is all about venturing deep inside a dungeon to reach and kill an old man). This game is its own thing, just like all other ACE Team games. I highly recommend giving it a chance.

Despite of following its ancestors, Wolfenstein: The New Order is not all about shooting Nazis.
It's year 1946. Despite of Allies having advantage over Nazi-Germany, Nazis have turned the tables, thanks to mad scientist called Wilhelm "Deathshead" Strasse, and the war machines he invented.
Allies have decided to make the final attack against Strasse, and are going to invade his castle.
You, B.J. Blazkowicz, as one of the members of Allies, are going to help at the war front.
The characters are each one of their own kind, you can feel the ways they react, and how they interact with each other.
I absolutely love the fact how characters and story completely took me with them. The more i played, the more i grew respect to the characters, and their backstories, how they lived before war and what made them the people who they are today.
I love how i felt different feelings against different characters, hate, love, pity, sadness. I might have cried tiny manly tears at some point.
Nazis are corrupting the world and the people who live there, one of the best moments without doubt is to revenge with large variety of guns and weapon modifications, for example, automatic shotgun, and assault rifle.
The gameplay part is mostly about shooting, but all the stages contain lots of puzzles, but only few of them are needed to make progress in the game.
Wolfenstein: The New Order has lots of similarities with so-called "old-school games", and with this i mean that you have to collect your own Ammo, Health and Armor throughout the game.
You can stay stealthy in shadows and take out guards without getting detected, or just take over the guns and destroy every living thing on your way. Game does not choose for you, You choose for yourself. I like that.
As you process further, game makes itself harder by adding more enemies. Enemies in the end of the game have lots of armor, do significant amounts of damage, and patrol more actively. Some might say they grow brains.
Need to point out though, how i managed to kill a guard in front of another guard with throwing knife without the other one noticing.
About the replay value; there are lots of in-game collectibles like concept art, gold statues, character bios, upgrades, letters and Enigma codes, which unlock modes to game. For example, Permanent death mode (1 death is game over without continues).
I played through story in about 10 hours with 2nd difficulty. There are 4 difficulties to choose from.
About the bugs and/or glitches, there are some, but on my sessions none of them caused game crashes.
It's a good game and you can get it for fairly cheap for 19,99€ on Steam Store.
About the system requirements though, this might not play on a bit older computers.
I recommend for players who are excited of war-themed games with great story and variety of characters.
And of course, whacking Nazis.
Thanks for reading, hopefully this helped.
Constructive critissism would be appreciated!

Abyss Odyssey is amazing. It's a rogue lite action game that sort of resembles Super Smash Brosh in its control scheme. Simple but elegant. The game has some bugs though, the end boss is rather lame and the controls aren't sublime either, but despite this it's one of the best games I've played in a while. The reason is Abyss Odyssey is one of those games that prove that games can be art too, and that art doesn't have to be all that pretentious and self-important. Abyss Odyssey is a piece of art that's fun.
The game has plenty of weird and interesting characters, like the duck man, the bull that shoots laser and samba Zorro. On top of that you can use all of them yourself. So although there are only three main characters, there's plenty of others you can use. The atmosphere is odd and mysterious. Its set in the Chilean civil war, there's the devil playing the fiddle, you can steal the shopkeeper's soul. You never know what you're gonna see next. The voice acting isn't that great though, but there's not much of it anyways.
The extra life system is quite ingenious as well. When your main character dies, a Chilean soldier appears, and you can control him. If you find a shrine, you can revive the character. It feels weird at first, but it's more interesting than the traditional "lose one life"-thing. There's also two player co-op that's fun and chaotic.
Like I said earlier, Abyss Odyssey has some bugs, so it's not perfect, but despite playing it just left me happy, because I felt like I experienced something new and exciting. I've played hundreds of different games in my life, and games nowadays rarely make me feel like I did when I was 10; this one managed it. Abyss Odyssey is some group's incomprehensible Dantean vision which I was happy to share.

Oxenfree is one of those games that you know you're never going to forget, even before you finish it.

Personally, I love the choice based nature of the game, and the way your dialogue choices affect every aspect of how other people relate to you. The way the conversation flows is brilliant, and the characters are all well fleshed out and very emotive (although I would love to see more of Nona as a character).
The controls flow smoothly using a controller or keyboard, and the small puzzles in the game work well with the atmosphere, but I think my favorite thing about the whole experiance is definetly the soundtrack. The music fits the mood and shapes the atmosphere of the game in the best way possible, and even contains hidden clues for anyone willing to pay a lot of attention.
All in all, this is a brilliant game that I highly reccomend anyone buying, especially people who enjoyed games like Life is Strange, Undertale or Until Dawn.

Half-Life: Opposing Force is my third experience with the Half-Life franchise, and like the other original classics, it is phenomenal. New weapons: Pipe Wrench, Combat Knife, Barnacle Grapple, Desert Eagle, M249 machine gun, Displacer Cannon, Sniper Rifle, Spore Launcher and Shock Roach (weapon). New type of aliens not related to Xen called Race X: Pit Drones, Shock Troopers, Shock Roachs (enemy), Black Ops (male), Black Ops AH-64 (helicopter) and Voltigores as well as two bosses the Pit Worm and Gene Worm. New mechanics like climbing ropes, and a new perspective of the original Half-Life as a U.S. Marine apart of the HECU called Adrian Shepard. All this content added, which was absent in Blue Shift, has made this one of the best DLC out there for the price of $4.99 USD, the amount of new content, the playtime of 6–7 hours and the fantastic story that goes with it. Overall Half-Life: Opposing Force is a very underrated and sometimes unknown Half-Life game that even triumphs over the original, 10/10.

Castle Crashers is a beat-em-up with a heavy multiplayer focus. While the game works and doesn’t become overwhelming in singleplayer, this game got its reputation for its multiplayer. The more the merrier, but even playing with just one friend can be a hoot. And with its constant sales, it isn’t too hard to pick up, either.
But what of the game itself? Castle Crashers is a rather short game to beat if you aren’t going for Hard Mode. However, its short length may be a blessing, as the entirety of it is a good time that’s just fun to play. There are plenty of unique enemies per area that don’t get stale and the game’s aesthetics and art direction make each screen nice to look at. Plus, the game has so much charm put into it. You can actually get a good amount of mileage out of the game by replaying it, either to show it to a new friend or even just to pick up one day after being like, “I kinda wanna play Castle Crashers.” The only problem you might run into here is you may need to completely refresh all of the progress on a character you got a high level if you want to play them from the start.
That isn’t too much of a problem, though. Castle Crashers has an absolute myriad of characters to unlock and choose from. And this unlocking feature also adds on to the game’s “postgame” beyond Hard Mode, as hunting down each condition to unlock a character or each animal buddy is rather fun even after beating the game. And all of these characters and animal buddies all have different attributes (the most noticeable being all of the different magic), so playing as a new character might give off a slightly different experience just by being a different character. That doesn’t even mention the level up points system, where you can level up things like health, attack, speed, or magic every time you level up for different character builds.
Castle Crashers may be relatively short, but it makes up for that with its variety and its multiplayer-driven gameplay, You can even play with strangers online if you want; I used to LOVE playing through Hard Mode and helping strangers through it over and over. So give this game a try; it’s a classic for a reason!

You might dismiss Sonic and the Car Stars in: Transformation Trouble because of the similar ability in Mariokart 7 to travel by air and water, but the transformation mecahnic is wildly different - the different modes have different handling and speed and in fact you have to remember to employ a completely different set of skills. Pulling stunts off static jumps for boosts when driving is simple compared to doing the same off sudden waves in the water, and entirely different to barrel-roll dodging obstacles for "risk-boosts" in the air. Super Sonicokart Bros. Transposed is built more around such racing skills than lucky pickups, in every sudden drop and every shortcut and every level 3 drift opportunity.
My complaints with Sonic & Friends Magical Racetime Adventure 2 are mostly aesthetic. The character's victory animations and voice clips are boring and irrelevant. There is dialog that has been recycled out of context from existing games, and anything new is poorly voiced and sounds to be written as if after a cursory glance at the respective Wikipedia article. This is all in stark contrast with the lovingly crafted vehicle and especially course designs - with their ambient action and easter eggs - as well as the clever selection of amazing reimagined music. It also bugs me that the pickups aren't themed around Sega games, in what is otherwise a consistently nostalgasmic package.
A more substantial complaint is that the control configuration is seperate from the proper game, and you might even think the defaults are confusing.
Sonic & Pals Friendly Fun Time Xtreem Death Race 3000 deserves much more recognition. The spectacular set pieces, scripted terrain transformations, and hidden surprises in every course (capably delivered by the amazing graphic detail) make each race feel like a trip to Disneyland, and the gameplay is equally exciting and beautiful for all the same reasons. I hear the PC version isn't a sloppy port, but the best version of the game, running at 60fps to the consoles' 30. Play this game right now or live forever in shame and sorrow, laying awake each night wondering "what could have been...?".

Squad is the spiritual successor to the Battlefield 2 mod Project Reality. This game is ostensibly a balance between Arma III and Battlefield 4. Teamwork and communication are required. The controls could use some work and there is still a lack of content, but that is explained by the game's early access status. The developers release large, satisfying updates on a regular basis. There is a clear emphasis on mod-ability; Squad has it's own developer kit, akin to Bethesda's Creation Kit, built in the Unreal Engine. The community itself is normally good-natured; a good majority of community members have an interest in doing well in the game and are likely to treat newcomers with respect.
If you are into casual gaming, Squad may not be the game for you. Unlike Battlefield or Call of Duty, you can't just hop into a match and lone-wolf it. Teams are divided into squads. A squad consists of eight players and a Squad Leader who can place down build-ables such as mounted machine guns, ammo crates, and sandbags. The Squad Leader can also place down a rally point that allows their squad nine respawns. There are multiple roles that the members of a squad can take: medic (arguably the most important), rifleman, automatic rifleman, grendier, light anti-tank, marksman, and scout. The success of the squad ultimately depends on which roles are assumed by the squad members and how they are used in combat. If these things are ignored, it is very likely that you will have a bad experience in Squad as a more organized enemy will easily keep you from completing your objective.
This is not to say that you need to join a military similation clan in order to play Squad. As long as you spend some time in the firing range to familiarize youself with the controls, communicate with your squad, and follow the Squad Leader's command, you are likely to have a good time.
Pros
- Active development team
- Emphasis on modability
- Solid early access build
- Recent optomization updates increase framerate considerably
- Good animations and physics system
Cons
- Lackluster controls
- Moderate learning curve
- Unintuitive menu system
- Lack of content (no helicopters, limited weapons and vehicles)
This game is early access done right.

I've been playing Planetside 2 on and off since the tech test and from time to time I decide to reinstall the game, this time via Steam because I had issues with the downloader. The reason why is mainly because modern shooters keep being such anti-consumer dissapointments, however I quickly end up uninstalling it again as the game has retained one aspect throughout the years... Its ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t. Aggravating ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t.
What do I mean by that? Well the game itself is a passable shooter, with some half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥attempts at going beyond that e.g. the construction system, but the game suffers from the fact that, at least on the european side, it lumps people with widely different regional backgrounds together into one laggy crockpot. You then couple this with the game designers' consistent insistence on low time to kill style of gameplay, which enevitably leads to frustration. Unless of course you're from a region where you can abuse the latency difference to your own benefit.
That could perhaps be forgiven had the game had shown any real signs of improvement over the years, yet with Planetside 2 things are never quite that simple. No matter which company you're referring to, be it SOE or Daybreak, one thing has been a constant: One step forward and two steps back. With the recent'ish revamp of the vehicle gameplay, which ended up making quite a few vehicle players quit the game, there isn't much left for those whom at this point haven't become addicted to the game over these many years, which I tend to liken to being in an abusive relationship.
This leads to next issue, which is an extention of my first complaint. What happens to most new players whom run afoul of veterans, especially the laggy ones? They get killed over and over and over again. There are so many ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t ways to be murdered in this game, most of which you will have little to no defense against, that it's no wonder that this game and its community has driven away most of those whom dare to venture into the pit of forgotten promise.
This game will never live up to the legacy of its predecessor, as the only plans that the developers seem to have are those relating to making more money from their F2P model. But, at least it's not anti-consumer like modern shooters are, so there is that. If you want to play an average, but free, shooter that doesn't try to rip you off then look no further. Just be aware that you will most likely not enjoy your time playing the game, as the vast majority of remaining players are veterans whom know exactly how to ruin your day.

I used to play DotA All Stars, and i love DotA 2, so i installed Strife and bought the collectors edition to check game capabilities. Of course the game is in beta and there is a lot of things to do, but i don't think i will recommend it to veteran players. This is a game for newbies in MOBA's.
Plus:
1. The game is pretty casual and after DotA it's some kind of rest. Just running with teammates and kicking people. And in this case it's a plus, no stealing, last-hitting is easy, money-spreading, no denies is a bonus for this game. If you want hardcore — go play Invoker you know where.
2. Pets and crafting system. Interesting thing to create your own builds for heroes, totally love it.
3. Raid bosses. They are great. Teamfights near them during their respawn and good bonuses to push after win.
Minus:
1. As I see some people say it's hard to play without paying money for crafting system. If it is so — that's not really good, good monetization way is a bonus of getting all this gems faster (I have 50% boost with collectors edition), but selling this stuff directly for money only harms the game. Yes. A bonus to start with that boosters at the beginning is good. Selling after — bad. And skins of course. The best way to monetize today is skins, but I perfectly understand that you are not Valve, but you need money too.
2. Heroes. There are plenty of them, but they feel to be the same during the teamfight. In DotA i perfectly see who is fighting, and in Strife it's kinda mess of coloured models everywhere.
3. Towers. They are too strong. If you dive - get ready to have really great troubles. I like playing Caprice and she can actually do it with a jump-anchor-hit-jump back, but the tower is a 90% chance so save yourself. Too good gank-protection.
4. Leavers. Today 90% of wins or looses are because of leavers. You can start a game with 3 teammates. Once i played against a team of 1 hero, because 4 left before the start of the game. There must be harmfull punishments. I know one — give a -50% boost for items for a couple of days for leaving the battle. And the game start must be a 5x5. Dota's way to start is much better.
As you see i told nothing about ballance. I would play this game more to complete this review about that, but i totally made Caprice (with crafting specific items, making my own build and taking a good pet) a good initiator with pretty good escaping and disabling abilities. Also can live longer now, cause Caprice can easily be killed without a good build. Also I can tell nothing about commuity now, it is not toxic today but I already played with some weird guys that we usually wish to die in pain in DotA.
And the verdict is that you can get this game and test, but there are a lot of minuses to be fixed to make it good. The donation system have to be reconstructed in some ways. Good donate is a thing we want to buy, but not a thing that will help us to dominate other players. I would still play it sometimes and I hope it will be a good MOBA one day, but not today. But yes. I changed my review to "Recommended" now. If you are newbie in MOBA — install this game, play this game. If you would think this is an easy one — install Dota 2/LOL and play some hardcore with us.

I was thinking on waiting till this game came under sale before buying it, as the screenshots surely interested me, though I decided to buy it anyways for $28 Canadian (included with the OST), and boy was I ever glad I did. From the first five minuted till the very end, I had chills vibrating down my arms, spine, and legs. The puzzles, mystery, and supernatural effects had me chilling and on the edge of my chair the entire playthrough. If you're a fan of games with multiple endings, all of which are effected drastically by the choices of mere dialogue you make, then I highly recommend this game. The characters all have different personalities, you can choose to side with a select few, all of them, or have all of them hate you. The artwork is absolutely stunning, the plot is original and non-generic, and if it left me of all people chilled and shocked, as is -very- rare for I, then it will surely knock you off your seat. I've heard complaints that the game is "too slow", but really thats one of the best parts. It allows you to take in the moment of every scene, every loop, supernatural aspect, or merely respect the characters reactions to what you choose to say. Unfortunately the -only- downside I thought of this game, is how short it is. If you sit through a single playthrough, without deciding to enveil the rumoured big island mystery, and just play the story start to finish, its about six hours give or take, at least thats what it took for me. I honestly find so much trouble putting this games ♥♥♥♥ing gorgeousness and originality into words, so I just push you to buy it and enjoy it as I did, as i'm already starting my second playthrough, to once again feel those chills down my arms which left me frozen for seconds as the game progressed. The story just reels you in closer and closer as your delve deeper into its beastliness. If you're the boring type to only enjoy mindless violence and shooting, and never find yourself into story, nor have the patience to listen, then unfortunately this game is not for you, though you should buy it anyways because I give a probable chance it will change that. I surely hope the creators of this game make a sequel, or at least another game of its origin, because I cannot get enough now, and if im being completely honest, I will never enjoy any of my others games as much as I used to after playing this. I have finally found a game I have bought without even the singlest, slightest regret. 10 out of ♥♥♥♥ing 10.

Imagine Super Meat Boy.  Now remove the wall jumps.  Now remove the world map and make it so that moving off the screen edge put you into the next room.  Oh, and add a bandage to every room.  Same excellent precision platforming, same tight controls, same instant-respawning-after-death pace, same exponential difficulty curve.
The soundtrack is a terrific arrangement of well-known classical music that complements the thick, bleak atmosphere.
The level design is the biggest departure from Super Meat Boy, and it works quite well, with lots of secrets to discover and many clever ways it interacts with how you move about the map.
Oh, and Rich Evans from Red Letter Media voices the player character in the opening, so I imagined the whole time I was playing as him and it added a lot of enjoyment to my experience.

Despite of following its ancestors, Wolfenstein: The New Order is not all about shooting Nazis.
It's year 1946. Despite of Allies having advantage over Nazi-Germany, Nazis have turned the tables, thanks to mad scientist called Wilhelm "Deathshead" Strasse, and the war machines he invented.
Allies have decided to make the final attack against Strasse, and are going to invade his castle.
You, B.J. Blazkowicz, as one of the members of Allies, are going to help at the war front.
The characters are each one of their own kind, you can feel the ways they react, and how they interact with each other.
I absolutely love the fact how characters and story completely took me with them. The more i played, the more i grew respect to the characters, and their backstories, how they lived before war and what made them the people who they are today.
I love how i felt different feelings against different characters, hate, love, pity, sadness. I might have cried tiny manly tears at some point.
Nazis are corrupting the world and the people who live there, one of the best moments without doubt is to revenge with large variety of guns and weapon modifications, for example, automatic shotgun, and assault rifle.
The gameplay part is mostly about shooting, but all the stages contain lots of puzzles, but only few of them are needed to make progress in the game.
Wolfenstein: The New Order has lots of similarities with so-called "old-school games", and with this i mean that you have to collect your own Ammo, Health and Armor throughout the game.
You can stay stealthy in shadows and take out guards without getting detected, or just take over the guns and destroy every living thing on your way. Game does not choose for you, You choose for yourself. I like that.
As you process further, game makes itself harder by adding more enemies. Enemies in the end of the game have lots of armor, do significant amounts of damage, and patrol more actively. Some might say they grow brains.
Need to point out though, how i managed to kill a guard in front of another guard with throwing knife without the other one noticing.
About the replay value; there are lots of in-game collectibles like concept art, gold statues, character bios, upgrades, letters and Enigma codes, which unlock modes to game. For example, Permanent death mode (1 death is game over without continues).
I played through story in about 10 hours with 2nd difficulty. There are 4 difficulties to choose from.
About the bugs and/or glitches, there are some, but on my sessions none of them caused game crashes.
It's a good game and you can get it for fairly cheap for 19,99€ on Steam Store.
About the system requirements though, this might not play on a bit older computers.
I recommend for players who are excited of war-themed games with great story and variety of characters.
And of course, whacking Nazis.
Thanks for reading, hopefully this helped.
Constructive critissism would be appreciated!
-Nate

That's already enough to NOT recommend it, because combat was clearly the main focus of this game, and they failed to deliver, but there are some more things that keep me from recommending it:

So I am writing my first review for this game. Why you ask? Because its one of those "games" that a simple thumps up or down doesn't do justice.
So here is why as a game Oxenfree is bad. The game mechanics are nearly non existent and basically all you do is walk from A to B to B and back again. In between you choose the dialouges which then determine the relationship you have with the other characters. So that's it, you don't do much more expect switching the frequency on your radio which ends up pushing the direction mindlessly until you feel vibration in your controller. So much for the bad, but everything else is fantastic.
The story is great and refreshing, the characters loveable and actually reasonable in how they react and what they do. Everything about this game from the artwork over the soundtrack to the story is amazingly done and has an incredible feeling. So that's a 9/10, maybe even more. However the game mechanincs in itself, since nearly non existing are just terrible 1/10.
So if you are looking for an intriguing story with loveable characters and choices that kinda do matter then this game is for you. But if you play games, because you like to play and don't care much for story this game will just bore you to death.
I had a great time though, an awesome game, but that's because I favour story above great gameplay. However it did leave me a bit unfulfilled at the end I feel like I missed out on some stuff, but is it enough for me to come back someday? Maybe, to change some choices and explore the story a bit more. Sadly when I think about it, I already dread the mindless "press stick into the direction you wanna go" gamemechaning, because there just not much else there.
Anway, If I could I would give this both; a big thumps up for everything exept gameplay and a thumps down for exactly that. In the end this game was so refreshing I still have to give it a recommend even though there could be a lot more game in this title. I grabbed it for 5€ at the steamsale, I think I would mind having payed the full price though

Well, what can i say?  This game has some excellent qualities, and holds on to you for a bit.  One of the greatest side-scrolling hack and slash games' I've found for those thirsty for some hack and slash, without the over-the-top gore and special effects, not to say it doesnt have it's own special effects.  Probably one of the most beautiful side scrollers I've played in a loooong time, the environments are either lush, or barren, dependening how deep into the abyss you get?  There is a Beautiful Soundtrack that enhances the mood tenfold, alot of thought was put into it, with beautifully instense piano clips, and music fitting the mood, perfect for the environments you find yourself in.  The Environments follow the old platforming standart of Earth,Wind,Water, and Fire, which are gorgeously Illustrated, with deep levels of parrallax scrolling.  You can sit and pick out details in the background that look like you could just reach out and grab them, not quite on the level of Trine or Trine 2, but beautiful, and effective nonetheless.
Now here is the news on combat, you can either play this game just mashing the buttons and not get as far, but more than likely, you are going to have to develop some sort of strategy, at some point,  The game basically ramps up the difficulty to make it more of a challenge when you rank up, and it does subtle changes to the AI when the game realises you are dying waay too much.  The combat system is pretty nice it uses the Xbox 360 controller very well, all of the buttons are taken into account from the beginning.  I'll let you discover the combos on your own, it'd be a spoiler to take away the fun of discovering how deep the control scheme actually is.  I actually found it good enough to go into the "Practice" gamemode, This game wants you to beat it, but not too quickly.  Therein lies the good and the bad, the story is paper thin, which allows you to basically hack and slash your way through it without thinking too deeply, and adds a little emptiness and sorrow to the game, without detracting from it's character.   It sometimes gets real hard to navigate through the abyss you hit a "hard" room and it can be all over in one encounter (I.E. the Life that you enter the Abyss with Is all you get), which isn't bad, but you don't want to give up even if you only have 400+ health out of 2200, and you can still pick up characters that you defeat. and add them to your inventory to use in a pinch.  It's all really fun, and frustrating, which I believe it strikes a perfect balance.
In Closing, i highly recommend this game to any hack and slash platform lovers, it will not dissappoint.

This game has the best combat system I've ever seen. You can use the enviroment to help you in combat. Dirty bomb is a very good shooter that is fast-paced and complex. There are about 30 characters (called 'mercs') to play as; there is a slight p2w feel as you only get 2 at the beginning and the rest you have to buy with a. real money or b. a ridicoulous amount of ingame money. You basically have to play 3 months every day and get the money through daily bonuses. However, you are given enough currency at the beginning to buy 1 merc; and every week there are 3 on rotation that you can play as.
As oppose to most shooters, where you buy/unlock guns for each character and kit them out, dirty bomb works through 'loadout cards'. Each character has a default one, then there are 6 tiers: lead, iron, bronze, silver, gold, cobalt. Lead gives you 1 extra passive, iron 2 and bronze-cobalt 3. Silver-cobalt are no stronger than bronze but are essentually the equivilant of getting rare gun/character skins. Each card comes with a primary, secondary and meele weapon (although from what i've played the meele is cosmetic as they all act in the same way).
The gameplay is fun and fast paced. It's easy to get into. Even the snipers have to keep moving to avoid getting shot. The tutorial even discourages scoping/ironsighting unless absoultly necessary. The fast moving objectives and quick descision making makes this game fast and fun.
There are a few problems with the matchmaking system though and don't come in expecting instant matching; the ui sometimes breaks and the game causes other problems. That being said, it's much less broken then most other beta shooters I've played, so don't worry about it causing you computer to brick.
If you're willing to commit the grinding time, and you like fast-paced shooters, this game is a must.
